geometry_source: B3LYP/6-31G* and CASSCF/6-31G* optimizations/frequency characterizations of ground-state reactant/products, triplet and singlet biradicals, conformers, and transition states; B3LYP IRC for one transition state
method: CASSCF(4,4), CASSCF(6,6), and CASSCF(8,8) mechanistic calculations compared with unrestricted/restricted B3LYP
active_space_orbital_description: For triplet t3 conformers, CAS(4,4) contains pi/pi-star of the newly formed C1-C2 pi bond and sigma/sigma-star of C2-C3; CAS(6,6) adds sigma/sigma-star of C1-O; CAS(8,8) further adds the C3- and N-centered nonbonding orbitals carrying the odd electrons. For [2+2] t2 formation, CAS(6,6) contains sigma/sigma-star of the forming C3-C4 bond, the C2/C5 odd-electron orbitals, and pi/pi-star of C2-C3. For [3+2] path a it instead includes forming N6-C4 sigma/sigma-star, C2/C5 radical orbitals, and C2-C3 pi/pi-star; path b uses forming C3-C4 sigma/sigma-star, C5/N6 radical orbitals, and the same C2-C3 pi pair.
active_space_protocol: The four t3 conformers were explicitly checked with nested CAS(4,4), (6,6), and (8,8) spaces; relative ordering is stable except that the largest space increases the penalty for d-t3. Production reaction-path stationary points and singlet-triplet gaps use CAS(6,6). The source describes optimized state-specific stationary points and does not report state averaging or multiple roots in one optimization.
nroots_per_mult: one targeted singlet or triplet root for each reactant, biradical, conformer, or transition structure
electronic_structure_description: CASSCF(6,6) places the hydrogen-shifted triplet t3 6.81 kcal/mol below t1 and gives adiabatic 1-to-t1 and 1-to-t3 excitation energies of 59.37 and 52.56 kcal/mol. Across CAS(4,4)/(6,6)/(8,8), doubly hydrogen-bonded a-t3 remains the lowest of four t3 conformers; b-, c-, and d-t3 lie 3.16, 26.60, and 16.77 kcal/mol above it at CAS(8,8). For ethylene addition, CASSCF(6,6) transition barriers are 13.2-13.9 kcal/mol on the t1 [2+2] channel; on the t3 [3+2] channel, N attack (16.0-16.3) is lower than C3 attack (18.4-18.8). Optimized singlet biradicals lie much higher (18.3-21.1 relative to the corresponding triplet reactant-plus-ethylene references), leading the authors to favor triplet cyclization.
Other: The photoexcited quinone, t1-to-t3 hydrogen shift, four t3 conformers, six ethylene-attack conformers per channel, all transition structures, singlet/triplet biradicals, fragmentation alternatives, and three final cycloadduct connectivities are consolidated as one overall fixed-reactant reaction system. Important caveats: the paper calls unrestricted-B3LYP singlet biradicals with <S^2> near 1.0 'pure singlets,' although a spin-pure singlet has <S^2>=0; those broken-symmetry DFT states are substantially spin contaminated. No spin-orbit coupling, minimum-energy crossing seam, or ISC rate is computed, so the claim that intersystem crossing is impossible follows only from energy differences. The conclusion that gauche-out is always most stable is also not supported uniformly by the CASSCF tables: for t2 and path-a t4, the CASSCF intermediate energies are lowest for anti, while only the t2 formation barrier slightly favors gauche-out. Ground-state product stabilization energies (-20.7, -2.6, +1.7 kcal/mol) are B3LYP-only and not separate entries.

CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations are single points on DFT geometries.
method: M06-2X, BP86, and B97D geometry/frequency calculations followed by CASSCF and CASPT2 spin-state energetics and vertical spectra; Cholesky-decomposed two-electron integrals
software: Gaussian 09 for DFT; MOLCAS 7 for CASSCF/CASPT2
basis_set: DFT: TZVP on Ni and SVP on other atoms, with all-atom-TZVP checks. Multireference: ANO-RCC-TZVP on Ni and N, ANO-RCC-DZ on peripheral C/F/H, and ANO-RCC-TZVP on PAPy carbon atoms
active_space_orbital_description: Primary spin-state space: eight Ni(II) 3d electrons plus two electrons in an equatorial porphyrin-N sigma-donor combination, distributed over five predominantly Ni 3d orbitals, their five diffuse 4d-like double-shell partners, and the porphyrin-N sigma orbital. The ESI plots every orbital. A CAS(12,12) test adds both equatorial and axial sigma-donor orbitals to the double d shell in five-coordinate species. The optical CAS(10,8) instead contains four porphyrin/PAPy bonding pi or N-lone-pair orbitals and four antibonding orbitals, omitting metal-centered excitations.
active_space_protocol: CAS(10,11)/CASPT2 single points compare singlet and triplet roots of trans-sqp, trans-spy, and cis-spy on M06-2X geometries. CAS(12,12) checks the singlet-triplet splittings of the two five-coordinate conformers without unbalancing the four-coordinate complex. A separate state-averaged CAS(10,8)/CASPT2 treatment gives the spin-allowed vertical spectrum of trans-sqp; four reported excited singlet states describe the Q/near-UV region. All conformers, coordination numbers, spin roots, dissociation-scan geometries, active-space tests, and DFT variants are consolidated into this one chemical row.
nroots_per_mult: One low-spin singlet and one high-spin triplet per coordination conformer for spin energetics; at least four singlet vertical excited roots in the CAS(10,8) spectrum
electronic_structure_description: Four-coordinate square-planar Ni(II) has paired d8 electrons and a singlet ground state, whereas axial pyridyl coordination narrows the 3dz2/3dx2-y2 gap and stabilizes a triplet square-pyramidal state. Dispersion-driven porphyrin-PAPy stacking mixes the accepting porphyrin pi-star and azo pi-star character. The calculated Q-band promotion therefore weakens N=N and can trigger trans-to-cis isomerization, after which pyridyl-N coordination locks the high-spin form. Intersystem crossing is part of the proposed mechanism, but no explicit spin-orbit matrix elements are computed.
Other: M06-2X places cis-spy triplet at 0.00 eV, trans-spy at 0.28, trans-sqp at 0.42, trans-sqp-open at 0.72, cis-sqp at 0.91, and cis-sqp-open at 1.32. CAS(10,11)/CASPT2 energies relative to cis-spy triplet are: trans-sqp singlet/triplet 0.26/0.39 eV, cis-spy singlet/triplet 1.07/0.00, and trans-spy singlet/triplet 1.32/0.29; CAS(12,12) preserves the five-coordinate ordering. Trans-spy pyridine dissociation is nearly barrierless, while cis-spy rises by 0.84 eV at Ni-N=3.3 A, excluding a stable all-trans switching mechanism. The two lowest CAS(10,8)/CASPT2 Q-band excitations are 2.59 and 2.65 eV with oscillator strengths 0.0370 and 0.0560 and populate mixed porphyrin/azo antibonding orbitals. A direct azo pi-to-pi-star root is near 7.25 eV at SA-CASSCF and suffers severe CASPT2 intruder states, so it cannot explain 500-nm switching.

For 2A2 the out-of-plane pi space is strongly delocalized, but adding in-plane degrees of freedom can reintroduce lower Cs solutions, so the true symmetry remains uncertain.

geometry_source: Ground-state neutral and cation equilibrium structures and cation normal modes were optimized by B3LYP/aug-cc-pVTZ (H,C,Br)/aug-cc-pVTZ-PP (I). Appendix 2 gives neutral/cation r(C-I)=2.156/2.154 A, r(C-Br)=1.944/1.938, r(C-H)=1.080/1.082, angle I-C-Br=114.87/95.48 degrees and H-C-H=112.39/116.27. method: single-state CASSCF for neutral and five-state-averaged CASSCF for cation potential/dipole/SOC curves; one-dimensional time-dependent wavepacket propagation with explicit SOC and strong-field coupling; B3LYP/TDDFT comparison model
software: MOLCAS 7.2 for SA-CASSCF/SOC; Gaussian 03 for B3LYP geometries and normal modes; Fourier-grid/Split-Operator quantum dynamics implementation
basis_set: CASSCF: ANO-RCC contracted to TZP, H 3s2p1d, C 4s3p2d1f, Br 6s5p3d2f1g, I 6s5p3d2f1g; DFT geometry/model: aug-cc-pVTZ for H,C,Br and aug-cc-pVTZ-PP for I

The five cation diabats are dominated by one hole/singly occupied orbital in 4a-prime, 2a-double-prime, 3a-prime, 1a-double-prime and 2a-prime, respectively; the 5a-prime and 6a-prime sigma-star orbitals are empty while remaining active orbitals are doubly occupied.
active_space_protocol: The neutral ground curve is single-state CAS(12,8); the five lowest doublet cation curves use equal five-state averaging in CAS(11,8). Diabatic CASSCF potentials, coordinate-dependent transition dipoles and AMFI SOC elements are transformed to adiabatic curves and propagated as one singlet-neutral plus five doublets for each ms=+/-1/2 (eleven electronic components total). All charge stages, states, scan points, field strengths and photodissociation products are consolidated as one reaction/dynamics system rather than split into intermediate-state rows.
nroots_per_mult: one neutral singlet root; five state-averaged cation doublet roots, doubled into ten ms/SOC components
electronic_structure_description: The SOC-free cation states along the bend are a 2A-prime, a 2A-double-prime, b 2A-prime, b 2A-double-prime and c 2A-prime. SOC strongly mixes/distorts especially the lowest two and makes the ground adiabatic surface anharmonic; b 2A-prime/b 2A-double-prime mixing opens two comparable one-photon channels. A pump-created ground-cation bending wavepacket crosses the probe resonances with opposite momenta, and strong-field dressed surfaces produce markedly different dissociation probabilities for left- versus right-moving packets.
Other: The multistate CAS model confirms the simpler fitted TDDFT mechanism but resolves essential state mixing. Its neutral-to-cation vertical IP is 0.4 eV below the DFT value/experiment, plausibly because the neutral is state-specific while the cation is five-state averaged; resonance tuning compensates this in dynamics. Both models give a roughly 350 fs/95 cm^-1 wavepacket period and FC distribution centered near vibrational quantum 7 with about five-quanta FWHM. Explicit SOC splits the nominal b-state resonance into locations u=0.21 and 0.45 a.u.; strong probe fields create dressed-state reflection/barrierless transfer, Stark population of state 2, and near-three-photon access to state 5. More than two cation states are required for detailed dynamics even though the two-surface DFT model captures the main modulation.

electronic_structure_description: Compact CASSCF-a is unbalanced: four active orbitals are doubly occupied, one singly occupied, and only one antibonding orbital is empty, yielding neutral Re=1.789 angstrom and omega=603 cm^-1. Adding five Br 4d correlators gives CASSCF-b Re=1.740 and 709 cm^-1, close to experiment, because 4d occupations reach about 0.016 and recover d-p/pi-p backbonding. CASMP2/ECT+(2df) gives neutral 1.726 angstrom/720 cm^-1 and BrO- 1.828/598; CASPT2 with Br 3d correlation gives 1.722/715. method: state-specific CASSCF geometry optimization for S0, S1, and T1; CIS transition electronic dipole moments; crossed-molecular-beam photofragment translational spectroscopy with forward convolution
software: Gaussian 98 revision A.9 for CASSCF and CIS; CMLAB2/KELVIN for beam-spectrum analysis

active_space_protocol: The identical state-specific CAS(8,7) is used to optimize S0, the first singlet excited state S1, and T1 for each meta/ortho/para isomer without symmetry restrictions. The paper reports no state averaging, root weights, or post-CASSCF dynamic-correlation correction. CIS/6-311G* is a separate single-reference calculation for transition-dipole direction, not the source of the recorded CAS.

electronic_structure_description: For all isomers, S0-to-S1 shortens C-Cl and C-CH3 while lengthening the aromatic C-C framework; orbital analysis assigns the transition predominantly as pi-to-pi*. Meta and ortho T1 retain bound C-Cl bonds (figure values: meta 1.779 angstrom versus S0 1.750; ortho 1.754 versus S0 1.782). Para T1 is qualitatively dissociative: C1-Cl=3.925 angstrom, an alternative C2-Cl contact=3.636 angstrom, and the C1-Cl direction leaves the ring plane by 54.4 degrees, suggesting coupled Cl migration/bond cleavage.
Other: CIS S0-to-S1 transition-dipole/C-Cl angles evaluated at S0/S1/T1 geometries are meta 23.0/22.8/17.8 degrees, ortho 6.1/26.6/25.7, and para 54.3/54.2/63.0, matching positive experimental anisotropy for meta/ortho and negative para anisotropy. At 266 nm, meta has beta=+0.5+/-0.2 and mean translation 3.15 kcal mol^-1 (28% of available energy); para beta=-0.6+/-0.2 and 3.28 (29%). Ortho requires two channels: about 60% slow o-tolyl+Cl with beta=+0.7+/-0.2, 2.06 kcal mol^-1 (18%), and 40% fast proposed benzyl+Cl with beta=+0.1+/-0.1, 5.09 (46%). The source proposes meta predissociation through T1 or internal conversion, direct dissociation on repulsive para T1, and for the ortho fast channel pre-dissociation H transfer to 1-methylene-2-chloro-3,5-cyclohexadiene (MCC) followed by Cl loss. Ortho S0 has a reported intramolecular Cl...H contact of 2.651 angstrom, suggested to facilitate transfer.

electronic_structure_description: The full-pi CASSCF wavefunctions describe alternating positive and negative carbon 2p_pi spin polarization localized most strongly near the radical center, together with increasing C-C bond-length alternation toward the chain ends. Relative CASSCF spin populations (largest positive site normalized to 1) are C3: terminal 1.000, central -0.343; C5: C1 0.75, C2 -0.31, C3 1.00; C7: C1 0.64, C2 -0.30, C3 1.00, C4 -0.42; C9: C1 0.47, C2 -0.24, C3 0.81, C4 -0.39, C5 1.00. The CASSCF distributions are qualitatively close to RCCSD(T) benchmarks, while both DFT functionals delocalize spin too evenly and UHF is severely spin contaminated.

For allyl, CASSCF also gives central C-H 1.078 angstrom, averaged terminal C-H 1.074 angstrom, and the tabulated C-C-C angle 124.7 degrees. The authors use experimental EPR hyperfine ratios through the McConnell relationship to benchmark carbon spin-density ratios: full-pi CASSCF is good qualitatively, RCCSD(T)/UCCSD(T) are closest for C3-C7, and absolute ab initio proton hyperfine constants can still be poor. CASSCF C11 and C13 results provide the largest feasible multireference benchmarks; the paper's C41H43 neutral-soliton calculations use only ROHF/UHF/BLYP/B3LYP and are therefore context, not a CAS entry. Those large-chain DFT calculations overestimate the experimental 18-carbon soliton half-width, whereas ROHF makes it too short. No spin-orbit Hamiltonian or spin-spin term is included.

active_space_protocol: Geometry tests used CASSCF(7,7), CASSCF(13,13), CASSCF(15,13), and CASSCF(19,15). The limited (7,7) space incorrectly gives a nonplanar short-bond structure; enlarging the space restores planarity but leaves a strong active-space dependence in the central O-O distance. MRCI geometry optimization used CASSCF(13,13) orbitals, while the reported CASPT2 geometry used CAS(13,11). CASPT2 and MRCI+Q stability calculations used a CASSCF(19,15) orbital set and included all valence electrons in the correlated multireference treatment.

electronic_structure_description: Planar trans-HO3 has an X 2A-double-prime ground state with the stated configuration 10a-prime^2 2a-double-prime^2 3a-double-prime^1. The singly occupied 3a-double-prime natural orbital has occupation 1.02. The long central O-O linkage forms through sigma interaction of one O2 unpaired electron with the HO unpaired electron and also gains weak pi character from O2-pi/lone-pair interaction, enforcing planarity.
Other: Central O2-O3 distances are 1.459 angstrom at CASSCF(7,7), 1.742 at CASSCF(13,13), 1.660 at CASSCF(15,13), 1.758 at CASSCF(19,15), 1.739 at CASPT2(13,11), and 1.647 at MRCI, versus 1.688 experimentally. The preferred CASPT2 thermochemistry gives Delta E=-6.03, Delta(E+ZPE)=-2.06, and Delta H(298 K)=-3.21 kcal/mol relative to HO+O2 and an estimated formation enthalpy of 6.12 kcal/mol. CCSD(T) stability results are rejected by the authors because T1 diagnostics reach 0.052. At the long-bond AIM critical point, QCISD/MRCI values are rho=0.23851/0.16356, Laplacian=+0.16977/+0.31533, ellipticity=0.12061/0.12671, and energy density=-0.1471/-0.0700 au: not a conventional covalent topology but stabilizing and partly pi-like.

electronic_structure_description: Cis-HO4 has X 2A configuration ...16a^2 17a^1, with singly occupied natural orbital 17a at occupation 1.02. It is an O2+HO2 radical adduct: sigma/antibonding orbitals 16a/18a arise from pairing one unpaired electron on each fragment, while interfragment lone-pair/pi and in-plane pi-pi overlaps add weak pi bonding. The cis conformer also has a stabilizing O1...O4 closed-shell contact and ring critical point, explaining its advantage over trans-HO4.
Other: For cis-HO4, CASSCF(11,10)/B2 gives central O2-O3=1.459 angstrom, whereas MRCI/B1 and QCISD/B2 give 1.805 and 1.691; trans-HO4 QCISD/B2 gives 1.583. Trans is 6.01 kcal/mol above cis at 0 K and the cis-trans ZPE-corrected barrier is 7.65. The reliable dissociation barrier is 4.31 kcal/mol at CASPT2 and 4.99 at MRCI+Q; the lower CCSD(T) TS2 barrier is rejected because T1=0.053-0.054. QCISD frequencies diagnose weak interfragment bonding: central stretch 438.3 cm-1 cis and 376.1 trans. AIM central-bond rho/Laplacian/H values are 0.15543/+0.31696/-0.0621 au (QCISD), while the cis O1...O4 contact has rho=0.02618 and H=-0.0045 au.

active_space_orbital_description: The valence reference is CAS(4,4): four pi electrons distributed over bonding 2b1 and 1a2 and antibonding 3b1 and 2a2 orbitals. Symmetry-specific excited-state spaces add the relevant diffuse orbitals: one a2 3d orbital for A1 states; four a1 orbitals (3s, 3p, two 3d) for A2; two b2 orbitals (3p,3d) for B1; and two b1 orbitals (3p,3d) for B2. active_space_protocol: A separate state-averaged CASSCF calculation was performed in each C2v symmetry. MRMP treated each electronic state individually. MCQD treated same-symmetry Rydberg states simultaneously, while valence states were computed separately, avoiding inappropriate valence/Rydberg mixing in the effective Hamiltonian. The article does not report state-average weights or a uniform root count.
nroots_per_mult: Multiple singlet A1, A2, B1, and B2 roots spanning valence and 3s/3p/3d Rydberg excitations; exact SA-CASSCF root counts and weights are not stated. Table II reports 13 singlet excited-state entries.
electronic_structure_description: The lowest valence 1B2+ state is predominantly the ionic HOMO-to-LUMO 1a2-to-3b1 pi-pi* configuration (CASSCF coefficient 0.967). The weak 2nd 1A1- valence state is covalent and strongly multiconfigurational, mixing the conjugate 1a2-to-2a2 and 2b1-to-3b1 single excitations, HOMO-squared-to-LUMO-squared double excitation, and some Rydberg character. The higher 4th 1A1+ state is ionic/multireference and is the strongest transition.
Other: MRMP/MCQD vertical energies are 5.19/5.27 eV for the lowest 1B2+ valence state (MRMP f=0.146), 6.42/6.47 eV for the hidden covalent 2nd 1A1- state (f=0.00391), and 8.11/8.16 eV for the bright ionic 4th 1A1+ state (f=0.502). The first 1a2-to-3s Rydberg state lies at 5.62/5.66 eV; three 3p origins cluster at 6.24-6.32 eV, five 3d states span about 6.81-6.97 eV, and the second-HOMO-to-3s state occurs at 7.80/7.81 eV. Dynamic correlation lowers the ionic lowest 1B2+ state from the CASSCF value of 7.74 eV by roughly 2.5 eV.

method: B3LYP and ROHF geometry/frequency calculations; CIS screening/assignment of visible doublet excited states; state-specific CASSCF excited-state gradients projected onto ROHF ground-state normal modes to calculate Franck-Condon resonance-Raman intensities; isotope-resolved time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy
software: Gaussian 98 for B3LYP, ROHF, CIS, and CASSCF calculations; REDONG for conversion of Cartesian force constants to local symmetry-coordinate force constants and potential-energy distributions
basis_set: 6-31G* with polarization functions on every C and N atom for all reported electronic-structure calculations
active_space_orbital_description: For the lower visible transition, CAS(3,4) contains 15b3, 15b2, 16b3, and 16b2 orbitals in D2, or 4b1u, 4b2g, 5b1u, and 5b2g in D2h. For the higher transition, CAS(1,3) contains 15b2, 16b3, and 16b2 in D2, or 4b2g, 5b1u, and 5b2g in D2h. These are the smallest converged spaces after progressive expansion through all orbitals of the transition symmetry; the numeric fields record the larger CAS(3,4).
active_space_protocol: CIS first requested four doublet excited states in each D2 model to identify the two lowest transitions with appreciable oscillator strength and their dominant orbitals. Separate state-specific CASSCF gradient calculations were then performed for experimental transition 1 and transition 2 at both D2 and D2h radical-cation equilibrium geometries. Active spaces were progressively enlarged until predicted Raman spectra were stable; the reported CAS(3,4) and CAS(1,3) are the smallest stable choices. The selected configurations have weights close to one.
nroots_per_mult: CIS requested four doublet excited states for convergence; two bright doublet B3 (D2) or B1u (D2h) states were selected and treated in separate state-specific CASSCF calculations.
electronic_structure_description: The open-shell radical cation has 12 pi and two n orbitals, with the two highest-energy orbitals of n type. Both strong visible states are nearly pure one-electron pi-pi* doublet transitions. In D2h, state 1 is chiefly 4b1u(beta)-to-4b2g(beta) and state 2 chiefly 4b2g(alpha)-to-5b1u(alpha); their CIS coefficients are 0.933 and 0.844. For model 2, 6-s-cis PSB has lambda_max 385 nm at SA-CASSCF, 392 nm at MRCI and 393 nm after Davidson correction; 6-s-cis-11-cis gives 387, 394 and 395 nm. The corresponding RPA values are 405 and 406 nm. Longer model 4 gives MRCI values of 493 and 497 nm for the same two isomers, demonstrating the large red shift with conjugation length.

RPA and MRCI differ by at most about 3% in the reported benchmarks, motivating RPA for the much larger real chromophores. The benchmark also shows why truncated models are hazardous: adding conjugated double bonds lengthens nominal single bonds, shortens double bonds through delocalization and shifts absorption strongly. The full retinal/SB/PSB structures, vibrational frequencies, isomer stabilities, torsional frontier-orbital curves, solvent microclusters and full-system absorption maxima are B3LYP, MP2, CIS or RPA results—not CASSCF/MRCI—and are not represented as separate multireference rows. electronic_structure_description: Furan is closed-shell 1A1. Direct C-O opening gives triplet 3A'' L-furan (structure 4) 322 kJ mol^-1 above furan at CASPT2/0 K and singlet biradical structures near 370-371 kJ mol^-1; the lowest singlet is sigma1pi1 rather than the higher closed-shell carbene-like sigma2 state. The viable minor channel proceeds through 1,2-H-transfer TS20 (280), cyclic singlet carbene 21 (264), ring-opened singlet biradical 23 (309), and C-C fission TS24 (352) to ketene+acetylene (225 kJ mol^-1). The dominant channel proceeds through alternative H-transfer TS25 (288), cyclic carbene 26 (279), formyl-allene intermediates 28/30 (130/118), and concerted TS31 (279) to CO+propyne (129). All values are CASPT2/cc-pVTZ plus CASSCF ZPVE relative to furan at 0 K.
Other: The direct singlet/triplet ring-opening routes have only about 0.1/7.6 s^-1 upper-bound rates at 1400 K and are excluded from the kinetic model. The ketene+acetylene cyclic-carbene route is 234 s^-1 and the formyl-allene route 629 s^-1 at 1400 K; their multistep Arrhenius fits are approximately 1.5x10^15 exp(-344 kJ mol^-1/RT) and 5.94x10^13 exp(-294.1 kJ mol^-1/RT) s^-1. Formyl allene decomposes overwhelmingly to CO+propyne rather than HCO+propargyl. A separate formyl-propyne route has TS34 at 356 kJ mol^-1 and only 2.8 s^-1. Methyl abstraction has 73/76 kJ mol^-1 0-K barriers to 2-/3-furyl, a combined 9.7x10^13 exp(-96.9 kJ mol^-1/RT) rate, and explains methane despite 506/514 kJ mol^-1 furan C-H bond enthalpies. The fitted model uses 82 reactions and reproduces shock-tube furan/major-product profiles; it slightly changes the dominant initiation activation energy from 294.1 to 292.9 kJ mol^-1, lowers the minor-channel A factor from 1.5x10^15 to 9.0x10^14 s^-1, and lowers the abstraction activation energy by 9 kJ mol^-1. CASPT2 underbinds triply bonded products, overestimating CO+hydrocarbon and ketene+acetylene reaction enthalpies by about 25-30 kJ mol^-1 versus experiment, so G2(MP2) is better for those closed-shell thermochemical balances. Conversely, CASPT2 is preferred at biradical/bond-fission structures where Q1 is large and single-reference methods collapse or disagree.

active_space_orbital_description: Orbital-count notation (sigma, pi_x, pi_y): (222) = 6 orbitals for an X-state-only test; minimum two-state (322) = three sigma plus two orbitals in each pi component, including sigma and pi correlating orbitals and diffuse 3s-sigma; (422)/(522) add sigma orbitals; (333) adds an oxygen-localized diffuse pi pair; (433) adds another sigma; balanced (344) adds the fourth, nitrogen-centered diffuse pi pair. active_space_protocol: The principal valence calculations used 7 active/correlated electrons. Equal-weight SA-CASSCF over X 2Pi and A 2Sigma+ was compared with separate state optimizations. Tested spaces were 7e-(322), -(422), -(522), -(333), -(433), and -(344), plus an X-only 7e-(222) test. The 11e-(522)-2s variant included 2s correlation. MRCI reference occupations were selected by maximum spin-coupling coefficient thresholds 0.05, 0.025, and 0.01; final reference lists merged those obtained across r = 1.6-2.4 a0. The avoided crossing at larger r was explicitly outside scope.
nroots_per_mult: two target doublet states: X 2Pi and A 2Sigma+
electronic_structure_description: X 2Pi is the ground valence state and A 2Sigma+ is predominantly Rydberg in the studied region. Increasing diffuse character in X 2Pi at short bond length drives the monotonic increase of the A-X transition moment as r decreases.
Other: The transition-moment function is strongly orbital-basis dependent. Enlarging only sigma space from (322) to (422)/(522) changes little; adding an unbalanced oxygen-centered diffuse pi pair in (333) produces a very small Franck-Condon-region moment, whereas balanced (344), with an added nitrogen diffuse pi pair, restores the magnitude and captures the short-r increase. MRCI removes much but not all CASSCF-space dependence because the selected reference lists are nearly identical and orbital bias remains. The authors identify (344) MRCI(7) as best; its spectroscopic constants are re/omega_e = 2.175 a0/1904 cm-1 for X and 2.009 a0/2421 cm-1 with Te = 42257 cm-1 for A. MRCI(11) closely tracks MRCI(7) with (344), showing 2s correlation is small after accurate valence correlation. At 0.01 threshold, (322) MRCI(11) reached 734395 X-state and 1208479 A-state CSFs, yet transition moments were stable across 0.05-0.01. The computed TMF is nearly linear over the strong-band region and gives A-state v'=0-2 lifetimes of 189.3, 186.1, and 183.1 ns; X-state (344) MRCI(7) gives S(1-0) = 123.9 and S(2-0) = 2.14 cm-2 atm-1, both close to experiment.

method: Full-valence CASSCF correlation-energy decomposition compared with a Hartree-Fock-node/fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo (FNDMC) decomposition. RHF/UHF stability energies supply the spin-symmetry-breaking correction Delta; CCSD(T) extrapolated to the CBS limit approximates exact reference energies. Natural-orbital dynamic/non-dynamic correlation indices were evaluated with CASSCF and FCI, and Slater-Jastrow FNDMC used a single RHF determinant node. Published all-electron FCI and CASSCF energies were shifted to the ccECP energy scale for the cross-method comparison.
software: GAMESS for CASSCF/FCI and natural-orbital indices; Gaussian 09 for RHF/UHF and CCSD(T); QMCPACK for FNDMC
basis_set: CASSCF(14,8) and CASSCF(14,16)/cc-pVQZ; CCSD(T)/CBS extrapolation from cc-pVXZ (X = 3,4,5) with ccECPs; FNDMC RHF orbitals in aug-cc-pVTZ with ccECPs and a 0.0025 au time step. Published all-electron CASSCF/FCI values were adjusted by the all-electron-to-ECP RHF energy difference.
relativistic_treatment: Correlation-consistent ccECPs replaced atomic cores in the CCSD(T)/CBS and FNDMC reference calculations; the paper does not present this as a separate relativistic correction.
active_space_orbital_description: CAS(14e,8o) contains the full F2 valence space. CAS(14e,16o) adds one correlating partner orbital for every orbital in the original eight-orbital valence space.
active_space_protocol: Source-explicit full-valence-versus-extended comparison: CAS(14,8) is crowded, with effectively one empty orbital and maximum excitation degree two for 14 electrons, so it under-recovers non-dynamic correlation toward dissociation. CAS(14,16) adds a complete correlating partner shell and recovers more correlation, but that extra recovery is dominated by unwanted dynamic correlation at shorter distances. The authors judge CAS(14,8) the less inaccurate space for correlation-energy decomposition, not a generally converged electronic-structure space.
nroots_per_mult: Ground-state dissociation/stretching curve only; no state averaging or excited roots are reported.
electronic_structure_description: RHF/UHF instability appears above about 1.4 angstrom, and the HF-node non-dynamic fraction rises toward roughly 50% of total correlation at dissociation. CAS(14,8) follows the qualitative growth but lies below the FNDMC non-dynamic reference in the stretched region because its active space is too restrictive. CAS(14,16) lowers the total energy substantially but exceeds the reference non-dynamic component at all sampled distances, producing non-negligible hidden dynamic correlation, especially at short F-F separations.
Other: F2 shows why lower variational energy is not automatically better for a CASSCF-based dynamic/non-dynamic partition: the double-shell CAS(14,16) is more correlated but less clean as a non-dynamic reference, while CAS(14,8) is undercomplete at dissociation yet less contaminated overall. Both active spaces and the full bond scan are consolidated into one physical-system row.

active_space_protocol: three spaces evaluated: CAS(6,5), CAS(6,10) and the large CAS(42,41) from DCSD NOs. Active-space design for transition-metal spin gaps, stated explicitly: small CASSCF-optimized spaces are CAS(6,5) - the five Fe 3d orbitals with six electrons - and CAS(6,10), which adds the five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals to capture 3d double-shell correlation. compound_name: Fe(II)-porphyrin model complex, quintet-triplet spin gap (5A1g vs 3Eg)
ligand_set: porphyrin macrocycle (four pyrrole N donors), four-coordinate ferrous porphyrin model
geometry_source: four-coordinate ferrous porphyrin model system from earlier work
method: FCIQMC-tailored distinguishable cluster (TDCSD) and tailored coupled cluster (TCCSD, TCCSD(T)), with perturbative F12 basis-set corrections, benchmarked against CASPT2, CCSD(T), DLPNO-CCSD(T1), MC-PDFT, diffusion Monte Carlo and DFT-PBE[U]
software: Molpro (tailored DC and TCC methods); NECI for the FCIQMC CI coefficients
relativistic_treatment: semicore Fe (3s3p) correlation included in the coupled-cluster steps
active_space_orbital_description: largest space CAS(32,34): the entire porphyrin pi system plus the orbitals of CAS(14,18); progression of four spaces detailed in active_space_protocol
active_space_protocol: A four-space progression that is itself the key result. CAS(8,11): five Fe 3d orbitals, five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals and one sigma(Fe-N) bond. CAS(12,15): adds the four Gouterman pi frontier orbitals, shown to be crucial for stabilizing the triplet over the quintet. CAS(14,18): NOT an extension of (12,15) - instead it adds four Fe 4s4p orbitals and the remaining three sigma(Fe-N) bonds on top of (8,11), deliberately omitting the Gouterman pi orbitals. CAS(32,34): the largest, containing the entire pi system together with the CAS(14,18) orbitals. CAS(32,34) is too large for conventional CASSCF, so Stochastic-CASSCF optimized its orbitals. Active-space design for transition-metal spin gaps, stated explicitly: small CASSCF-optimized spaces are CAS(6,5) - the five Fe 3d orbitals with six electrons - and CAS(6,10), which adds the five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals to capture 3d double-shell correlation. Large spaces (over 30 electrons in 30+ orbitals) are built from DCSD natural orbitals whose occupations deviate strongly from 0 and 2, with the explicit requirement that both spin states get a similar space - if an orbital type matters for one spin state it is included for both, so the states are balanced. FCIQMC then supplies the CI vectors inside these large spaces to tailor the distinguishable-cluster/coupled-cluster amplitudes.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 3Eg (triplet), stabilized over 5A1g (quintet). Quintet-triplet spin gap dE = E(Q) - E(T), a few kcal/mol with the triplet below the quintet. At CAS(32,34): tailored TDCSD-F12a and TCCSD(T)-F12a both give 5.8 kcal/mol; recent Stochastic-MRCISD on the same CAS(32,34) (correlating 96 electrons in 159 orbitals) gives 6.8 kcal/mol; CCSD(T)-embedded CAS(32,34)+dF12 gives 5.7 and DCSD-embedded 3.6 kcal/mol. Largest doubles amplitude in CAS(32,34): 0.242 (LS/triplet) and 0.221 (HS/quintet) - much more multiconfigurational than the octahedral complexes.
Other: The clearest active-space lesson in the paper: the entire porphyrin pi system must be in the space to stabilize the triplet ground state. Smaller CASs erroneously predict a quintet ground state; only once the full pi system is included (via the Gouterman orbitals and ultimately CAS(32,34)) does the correct triplet-below-quintet ordering emerge, already at the Stochastic-CASSCF level, and tailoring plus F12 enlarges the gap further. Small active spaces demonstrably reduce tailored-method accuracy here - fixed amplitudes in a small space shrink the TCCSD(T) gap far below CCSD(T) - so large active spaces are indispensable when multiconfigurational character is high. All the large-CAS(32,34) tailored methods agree with each other to within a fraction of a kcal/mol.

notes: Fe(II) d6; oxidation state and d count from the ferrous porphyrin assignment. electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitations (calculated, experimental in parentheses): S1(npi*) 3.73 eV / 333 nm (3.76 eV, 335 nm), transition dipole 0.0695 D; S2(pipi*) 5.74 eV / 216 nm (5.54 eV, 224 nm), transition dipole 4.53 D. S1 is almost dark. Along the relaxation path the T2(pipi*) state crosses S1(npi*) with a spin-orbit coupling of 37.96 cm-1, large enough for efficient intersystem crossing; T2 then passes the T1T2 conical intersection diabatically to become T1(pipi*), which is long-lived because its spin-orbit coupling to S0 is only 5.73 cm-1 and the gap is 1.06 eV. In the trajectories no ground-state repopulation through either S1S0 conical intersection was seen: S1 decayed entirely to the triplets with a time constant of about 750 fs (exponential fit 746 fs), consistent with the near-unity triplet quantum yield measured experimentally. Eleven net hops from S1 to T2 and eleven from T2 to T1, all at nearly planar geometries near the S1 minimum, with the wave function changing from 1(npi*) to 3(pipi*); T1 then relaxes to its twisted (pipi*) minimum by torsion about the HC=CH dihedral.

active_space_protocol: XMS-CASPT2(6,5)/cc-pVTZ for the vertical excitations; XMS-CASPT2(8,7)/cc-pVDZ for critical points and dynamics
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitations for conformers 2 / 2' (experimental in parentheses): S1(npi*) 4.87 / 4.87 eV, 255 / 255 nm (4.66 eV, 266 nm), transition dipoles 0.126 / 0.594 D; S2(pipi*) 5.08 / 5.15 eV, 244 / 241 nm (4.96 eV, 250 nm), transition dipoles 4.93 / 5.06 D. The two conformers - BF3 oriented toward or away from the C=C double bond, boron in the plane of the conjugated pi system - have nearly identical energies and spectra. Complexation stabilizes all the frontier pi, n and pi* orbitals relative to the free enone, most strongly the oxygen lone pair that forms the sigma bond to BF3, which is what produces the large red shift and brings S1 and S2 close together so both become optically addressable. The Franck-Condon geometry sits near an S2/S1 conical intersection that acts as a branching point: keeping pipi* character the system reaches a twisted S1S0 conical intersection, keeping npi* character it reaches the S1(npi*) minimum with BF3 rotated out of plane and the O-B bond elongated, from which heterolytic dissociation of the complex is possible in the gas phase and a second, ring-opened S1S0 conical intersection is reached. Unlike the free enone, then, internal conversion competes with intersystem crossing. Spin-orbit coupling between the crossing T2(pipi*) and S1 states is around 25 cm-1. method: N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) on a CASSCF reference, used for full geometry optimization; energies also at CCSD(T)/CBS(T-Q)

electronic_structure_description: Singlet ground state with the triplet 17.9 kcal/mol higher (CCSD(T)/CBS(T-Q)). The Z isomer is preferred over E by 12.6 kcal/mol, and the inversion transition state is essentially isoenergetic with the E carbene, so E would be unobservable in matrix isolation. Z isomer: H-C-N carbene angle 125 deg, C-N 1.23 A (between the C=N double-bond value of 1.27 A and the C-N triple-bond limit of 1.14 A), against 106 deg and 1.31 A in the parent aminomethylene; C-N stretch blue-shifted by more than 300 cm-1. Dipole moments at NEVPT2: 3.36 D (Z) versus 5.29 D (E). The sigma* N-I orbital is the LUMO; NBO gives 372 kcal/mol for donation of the carbene lone pair into sigma*(N-I). CASSCF/def2-TZVPP natural occupation numbers of the sigma and sigma* N-X orbitals are fractional, showing partial multireference character; T1 diagnostic only slightly above 0.02.
reference_short: Medvedko, Bhagat, Wagner, sigma-Resonance Stabilization of Aminomethylene by N-Halogenation, J. Comput. Chem.
notes: The (6e,5o) space is stated but its orbital composition is not, so active_space_orbital_description is left empty; the paper does identify sigma and sigma*(N-X) among the active orbitals through their fractional occupations. The pyoverlaps.py driver computes the overlap matrix between each sampled geometry's candidate active orbitals and a reference geometry's active orbitals, and automatically swaps orbitals in and out to preserve a consistent active space along the ensemble. Motivation is documented: for the five canonical nucleobases, geometries with undesired active spaces gave wrong densities-of-states/excitation energies until the active space was corrected.

method: DMRG-SCF with an NEVPT2 perturbative correction as the multireference route, compared against CC3 and EOM-CC3, time-dependent DFT and semiempirical CI (SECI); DMRG is used precisely because plain CAS-SCF cannot carry the natural active space of the longer chains

active_space_protocol: the space grows with the chain: n occupied pi, n virtual pi and the two lone pairs for a COn with n double bonds. Because CAS-SCF scales exponentially in that space, DMRG-SCF replaces exact diagonalization for the longer chains, with NEVPT2 added for dynamic correlation - a combination previously shown to capture nuclear relaxation effects on the excited-state manifold of extended carotenoids.
electronic_structure_description: The dark Ag- state has strong doubly excited character, so conventional TD-DFT overshoots its transition energy, while the bright Bu+ state is captured reasonably well by TD-DFT. DMRG/NEVPT2 is reliable for the states energetically separated from the others but systematically underestimates the bright Bu+ excitation energy across these systems, so the paper's final benchmark data set is assembled by mixing methods: CC3 for Au and Bg in short systems and NEVPT2 for longer ones, NEVPT2 throughout for Ag, and CC3 for the bright Bu+ in the shorter systems. The practical conclusion is that semiempirical CI is the right accuracy-cost compromise for real xanthophylls in their protein environment, demonstrated on canthaxanthin in the orange carotenoid protein.

method: CBS[H], a basis-set-incompleteness correction that dresses the electronic Hamiltonian with an effective short-range electron-electron interaction, based on a local mapping between the Coulomb operator projected onto a finite basis and a long-range error-function interaction with a local range-separation parameter; unlike the earlier correction of Giner et al. it uses no short-range correlation density functionals. Applied on top of complete active space wave functions with correlation energies from the linearized adiabatic connection (AC0) and from NEVPT2, and compared against the DBBSC correction
basis_set: cc-pVXZ, X = D through 6, with two-point extrapolation from cc-pV5Z and cc-pV6Z as the benchmark; cc-pVXZ-F12 sets also tested

active_space_protocol: helium: HF, CAS(2,5)SCF and CAS(2,14)SCF references. The active spaces for the molecular test set are not stated in the main text.
electronic_structure_description: Basis-set-incompleteness corrections to the helium correlation energy (mHa), CBS[H] / DBBSC / exact, against the exact energy of -2.903724 Ha. With a CAS(2,5)SCF reference: DZ -8.3 / -9.5; TZ -3.7 / -3.7; QZ -1.8 / -1.6; 5Z -1.0 / -0.9; 6Z -0.6 / -0.5, exact -3.5, -1.3, -0.6, -0.3 for TZ through 6Z. With CAS(2,14)SCF: DZ -16.1; TZ -3.3 / -3.6; QZ -1.5 / -1.8; 5Z -0.8 / -1.0; 6Z -0.6 / -0.5. With HF: DZ -9.0 / -12.3; TZ -3.9 / -5.1; QZ -1.9 / -2.3; 5Z -1.1 / -1.3; 6Z -0.7 / -0.8. From cc-pVTZ onward the CASSCF-based CBS[H] correction agrees with the exact value to within 0.2 mHa and stays sub-millihartree (at most 0.5 mHa) for larger bases; both corrections are nearly independent of the reference CASSCF wave function, as they should be, while HF-based errors exceed 0.5 mHa. The poor cc-pVDZ performance is attributed to projecting the short-range interaction operator onto the Hilbert space spanned by that basis. For the molecular set, CBS[H]-corrected AC0 and NEVPT2 correlation energies in a basis of cardinal number X (from X = 3) approach the uncorrected values in the (X+1) basis, so triple-zeta corrected results match uncorrected quintuple-zeta ones. CBS[H] works equally well for AC0 and NEVPT2. In cc-pVTZ the DBBSC-corrected relative energies stay within 1.5 mHa for every molecule while N2 is a clear CBS[H] outlier; conversely for O2 and F2, AC0-CBS[H] reaches 0.5 mHa at triple-zeta where DBBSC exceeds 1 mHa. In cc-pVDZ-F12 the CBS[H] relative-energy errors are smaller on average than in standard cc-pVDZ, and NEVPT2-CBS[H] there approaches uncorrected NEVPT2 in cc-pVTZ-F12.
reference_short: Hapka, Tucholska, Modrzejewski, Golub, Veis, Pernal, Correcting Basis Set Incompleteness in Wave Function Correlation Energy by Dressing Electronic Hamiltonian with an Effective Short-Range Interaction, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2025, 16, 6489-6499

The average metal-ligand bond length changes by 0.1136 A per centre for basal-plane electron transfer and 0.1223 A along c, roughly twice the change that accompanies hole transfer - the internal reorganization energy for electron transport is correspondingly larger, and that is what makes electron mobility more than three orders of magnitude smaller than hole mobility in both directions.

ligand_set: an eta4-cyclobutadiene ring and three carbonyls
point_group: C1 in the optimizations; the cyclobutadiene ring was held square
geometry_source: computational and experimental combined: the Fe-Cb and Fe-CO distances were optimized at the CASPT2 level by stepwise energy scans with 0.01 and 0.02 A steps and parabolic interpolation, with all three Fe-CO distances kept equal and every other parameter fixed at the crystallographic values. First-order relativistic mass-velocity and Darwin corrections were included, and a basis set superposition error correction was applied in the (12,12) optimization. Optimized Fe-Cb 1.790 A, 1.783 A with the relativistic correction and 1.82 A with the BSSE correction; Fe-CO 1.797 A and 1.786 A. The BSSE-corrected Fe-Cb distance is about 0.03 A longer than the electron-diffraction value and 0.05 A longer than the X-ray value, while the CASPT2 Fe-CO distance is close to experiment.
software: MOLCAS-3 for the CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; Gaussian 94 and GAMESS for the RHF, UHF and CAS(10,10) geometry optimizations
basis_set: ANO in MOLCAS: (17s12p9d) contracted to [6s4p3d] for iron, (10s4p3d) to [3s2p1d] for carbon and oxygen and (7s) to [2s] for hydrogen, with the carbon 1s and the iron 1s, 2s and 2p orbitals frozen in CASPT2. In the Gaussian and GAMESS calculations a Dunning-Huzinaga valence double zeta basis was used for C, O and H, with the argon core of iron replaced by a Hay-Wadt effective core potential and its double-zeta valence basis, one d polarization function of exponent 0.75 on the cyclobutadiene carbons and an additional diffuse d function on iron
active_space_orbital_description: twelve electrons in twelve orbitals. Ten of them follow a published general rule for transition metal compounds: the two singly occupied iron 3d(xz) and 3d(yz) orbitals paired with the two singly occupied cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, and the three doubly occupied 3d orbitals - dxy, dx2-y2 and dz2 - each paired with a combination of a 4d correlating orbital and a CO orbital. The remaining two are the lowest and highest cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, added to obtain the correct ordering of the singlet states. CAS(12,12) natural orbital occupation numbers, bonding against antibonding partner: 1.977/0.025 for the cyclobutadiene pair, 1.929/0.070 for dz2 with a CO combination, 1.924/0.073 for dx2-y2, 1.921/0.078 for dxy, and 1.895/0.107 and 1.894/0.107 for the two Fe-Cb pairs.
active_space_protocol: (10,10) following the general transition-metal rule - five 3d orbitals each with a correlating partner - used for the geometry optimization; (12,12) adding the two remaining cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, required for the correct ordering of the singlet states
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet, though the restricted Hartree-Fock wavefunction is unstable over a wide range of Fe-Cb distances. The lowest broken-symmetry unrestricted solution dissociates to triplet cyclobutadiene plus triplet Fe(CO)3; higher broken-symmetry solutions break symmetry within the cyclobutadiene ring as well and correspond to excited wavefunctions dissociating to singlet fragments. The CASPT2 binding energy of Fe(CO)3 to cyclobutadiene is 95.7 kcal/mol relative to square triplet cyclobutadiene and 90.3 kcal/mol relative to the rectangular singlet. The rotational barrier of the Fe(CO)3 group against the ring is exactly zero at RHF, UHF and CASSCF, in agreement with experiment and with extended Huckel predictions that such barriers should be very small for M(CO)3 fragments on even-membered carbon rings. The CAS(12,12) occupations show that correlation in the Fe-CO bonds is almost as important as in the Fe-Cb bond, and that correlation within the cyclobutadiene ring is the least important of the three.
Other: The most transferable thing in this paper is a rule for CHOOSING the active space from a broken-symmetry Hartree-Fock calculation. The restricted Hartree-Fock wavefunction of the complex is unstable over a wide range of iron-cyclobutadiene distances, and the unrestricted solutions break symmetry in the Fe-Cb bond, localizing electrons on the iron and on the ring. The author's conclusion is stated flatly: the Hartree-Fock orbitals that break symmetry are the ones that should be in the CASSCF active space, and the lowest-energy broken-symmetry solution shows the most important non-dynamical correlation in the molecule. The evidence is that the broken-symmetry natural orbitals and the CAS(10,10) natural orbitals have very similar contours and come out in the same ORDER, and that feeding the broken-symmetry natural orbitals in as CASSCF starting orbitals gives very good convergence - the CAS-UNO procedure. The occupation numbers show the difference between the two descriptions clearly: the broken-symmetry solution over-polarizes, giving 1.595/0.404 for the Fe-Cb pair where the CASSCF gives 1.894/0.107, but it puts the right orbitals in the right order. The space itself follows a published general rule for transition metal compounds - a (10,10) space correlating all five metal 3d orbitals, the empty ones against ligand orbitals that donate an electron pair and the doubly occupied ones against 4d correlating orbitals mixed with empty ligand orbitals - and the paper confirms that rule holds here, with the two singly occupied Fe 3d(xz,yz) orbitals correlating against the two singly occupied cyclobutadiene orbitals and the three doubly occupied 3d orbitals against combinations of 4d with CO orbitals. The 4d orbitals are the second orbitals of a triple-zeta d shell, that is the 3d correlating shell of the double-shell effect. Two orbitals then have to be ADDED beyond that rule: the remaining pair of cyclobutadiene pi orbitals, needed to get the ordering of the singlet states right, giving (12,12) - even though their own correlation contribution is small, with occupations of 1.977 and 0.025. A separate practical warning concerns CASPT2 rather than the space: the potential energy curve of the Fe(CO)3 fragment develops a discontinuity beyond an Fe-CO distance of 1.88 A where the reference weight collapses, an intruder-state artefact, and the minimum had to be found by interpolating over points whose reference weight exceeded 0.58. The paper gives a useful rule of thumb for what reference weight to expect: about (1 + 0.015) to the power -N/2 for N correlated electrons, predicting 0.71 for the 46-electron fragment and 0.61 for the 66-electron complex, against an observed 0.61 to 0.63.
notes: metal_ox_state and d_electron_count are arithmetic, treating the complex as iron(0) with a neutral four-electron cyclobutadiene donor and three carbonyls, an eighteen-electron count; the paper does not assign a formal oxidation state. The CASSCF Fe-CO distance is much longer than experiment, which the author attributes to the basis set and to the absence of dynamic correlation; the CASPT2 values are close. method: CASSCF(8,6) potential energy scans with NEVPT2(8,6) and MRCI-CASSCF(8,6) as independent checks, alongside DFT; Wiberg bond indices computed with Multiwfn

active_space_protocol: the multireference treatment is motivated by a diagnostic rather than chosen by default: T1 diagnostics at the minimum-energy geometries of both isomers come out at 0.04, above the 0.02 threshold, so the geometries are not satisfactorily described by single configurations. electronic_structure_description: Two minima are found lying on entirely different potential energy surfaces, corresponding to short-bond and long-bond isomers of the same spin state and symmetry, so interconversion cannot proceed over a single barrier on one surface. At CASSCF(8,6) and NEVPT2(8,6) the two curves cross at several points, indicating avoided crossings; at MRCI-CASSCF(8,6) they cross at a distance shorter than either minimum, leaving two complete separate pathways, which the authors attribute to the larger number of configurations included. compound_name: dioxygen chemisorbed on a germanium-germanium addimer of the Si(1-x)Ge(x)/Si(001) surface
formula: O2Ge2Si10H4 quantum region embedded in O2Ge2Si32H32
geometry_source: a hybrid quantum-mechanical / molecular-mechanical cluster representing the reconstructed surface, the two parts joined by the SIMOMM link-atom scheme and the cluster edges saturated with hydrogen; the reaction is followed as a scan in the O-O distance
method: CASSCF on the quantum region of a QM/MM cluster, used because breaking the O-O bond passes through a region of near-degenerate levels that a single-determinant treatment distorts
basis_set: the authors' N21-3** set for the production calculations, with N31-6** used as a check
active_space_orbital_description: two electrons in two orbitals - the bonding and antibonding pair of the O-O bond being broken
active_space_protocol: the minimal space for a single bond dissociation, and the paper's justification for it is a convergence test rather than an argument: the barrier and the reaction energy were recomputed for four small bare clusters - the two-atom dimer clusters with each combination of silicon and germanium, and a nine-silicon cluster - at both this space and a four-electron, four-orbital one, and in both basis sets. The barriers move by at most 0.09 eV between spaces in the smaller basis and by 0.04 eV in the larger, except for one mixed cluster where the four-orbital space with the smaller basis is an outlier. The reaction energy is more sensitive, changing sign for the nine-atom cluster. What the test establishes is that the two-orbital space suffices for the barrier, which is the quantity the paper reports.
nroots_per_mult: one
electronic_structure_description: Chemisorbed dioxygen lying across the addimer, dissociating by O-O bond scission with an activation barrier of 0.18 eV. The three addimer compositions give barriers within 0.04 eV of one another - 0.18, 0.17 and 0.14 eV for the germanium, mixed and silicon dimers - so the composition of the dimer barely matters. On the bare, unembedded dimer clusters the corresponding barriers are 0.39 to 0.49 eV in the same basis and space.
Other: The two-orbital space is doing the one thing a single determinant cannot: following the O-O bond through the region where its bonding and antibonding levels become near-degenerate, which the authors identify as the source of the geometric distortions that uncorrelated calculations produce along this path. What the calculation then shows is that the barrier is not a property of the adsorbate or of the dimer's composition at all - all three compositions give the same value within 0.04 eV - but of the embedding: removing the surface strain by computing the bare dimer cluster more than doubles it. The authors read the composition-independence as evidence that the dissociation is electron-transfer driven.
reference_short: Grynchuk, Koval and Nakhodkin, Surf. Sci. 623, 13 (2014)
notes: The chemisorption step that precedes dissociation releases about 6 eV and is non-dissociative; only the subsequent O-O bond breaking is computed here. The bare-cluster tests in the paper give barriers of 0.35 to 0.54 eV, two to three times the values obtained on the embedded surface clusters, which is the paper's evidence that the low barrier is a consequence of local surface strain rather than of the chemistry of the dimer alone. The quantum region is quoted in the paper only for the germanium case; the corresponding clusters for the other two addimers are not written out. Correlation treatment (moved 2026-10-12 from correlation_correction, which holds only a method name): none - only the static correlation captured by the active space itself

ligand_set: six hydride ligands in an octahedron, with the surrounding crystal represented by a Madelung field
point_group: Oh, with the calculations carried out in the D2h subgroup for technical reasons
geometry_source: the Fe-H distance optimized at each computational level; the rest of the crystal represented by the Madelung field of the infinite Mg2FeH6 lattice, computed by placing the whole negative charge at the metal and then iteratively redistributing it over the complex according to a Mulliken population analysis
method: SCF, CASSCF and contracted CI, with a multireference analogue of the Davidson correction added to the CI energies to account for higher excitations
basis_set: the SDZC set (1) of Tatewaki and Huzinaga for the metal, with the 3d and 4s shells each split into two functions and one diffuse p (0.09242 for iron) and one diffuse d function added. The metal 1s, 2s, 3s, 2p and 3p core orbitals are frozen in their atomic shape and not optimized in the MCSCF
active_space_orbital_description: two spaces were used. The first has only the bonding and antibonding orbitals of Eg symmetry active - four electrons in four orbitals, specified in D2h as (1,1,1,1,1,1,1,0 / 4,0,0,0,0,0,0,0) for inactive and active orbitals per irreducible representation. The second adds the nonbonding d orbitals of T2g symmetry and their d* counterparts, giving ten electrons in ten orbitals, (1,1,1,0,1,0,0,0 / 4,0,0,2,0,2,2,0)
active_space_protocol: the larger space was not planned but diagnosed: the CI calculation on top of the four-electron CASSCF showed that excitations from the nonbonding T2g d orbitals to d* orbitals were important, so a second CASSCF was run with those orbitals active as well. The authors describe this as bringing some pure atomic correlation into the CASSCF itself. Both CI calculations correlated all 18 valence electrons and used four reference configurations
electronic_structure_description: With 18 valence electrons the ion is very likely a closed-shell 1A1g ground state, and the calculations confirm it. The Fe-H distance shortens systematically with correlation: 1.69 A at SCF, 1.63 with the four-electron CASSCF, 1.59 after CI on those orbitals, 1.60 with the ten-electron CASSCF and 1.56 after CI on those - the last identical to the value from neutron diffraction on the Mg2FeH6 crystal. The iron d population rises in parallel from 8.1 to 8.5. ligand_set: four hydride ligands, compared in square-planar, slightly twisted (10 to 20 degrees) and pseudotetrahedral (90 degree twist) arrangements, embedded in a Madelung field

method: CASSCF followed by contracted CI correlating all 16 valence electrons, with three and two reference configurations respectively for the two CI sets
basis_set: Tatewaki-Huzinaga SDZC set for nickel with the 3d and 4s shells each split into two functions, one diffuse p (0.1122) and one diffuse d function added; metal core orbitals frozen in atomic shape
active_space_orbital_description: three spaces were used for the planar complex. The first has all the Ni-H bonds and their antibonding partners active together with the d and d* orbitals of A1g symmetry, since that d orbital mixes slightly with the bonding orbital of the same symmetry: (1,0,0,0,0,1,1,0 / 4,2,2,2,0,0,0,0). The second has only the bonding and antibonding in-plane d orbitals active, a four-electron space. The third extends the second to all five pairs of d and d* orbitals: (1,1,1,0,0,0,0,0 / 4,0,0,2,0,2,2,0)
active_space_protocol: the three spaces separate two different correlation effects deliberately - bond correlation, through the Ni-H bonding and antibonding pairs, and atomic d correlation, through the five d/d* pairs - so that their contributions to the bond distance can be read off independently
electronic_structure_description: For the singlet the planar structure is the most stable, 16 kcal/mol below the 90-degree twisted form at CI level, though the potential surface is very shallow near planarity - twisting by 10 degrees costs only 0.5 kcal/mol and by 20 degrees only 2.0. At 90 degrees the 3B3 triplet lies below the planar singlet by 4.6 kcal/mol at CASSCF level. The Ni-H distance is 1.60 A with the four-electron space, unchanged at 1.60 A when the three pairs of bonding and antibonding orbitals involving Ni 4s and 4p are added, 1.57 A after CI on those orbitals, 1.57 A directly from the CASSCF with all five d/d* pairs active, and 1.56 A after CI on those. A NiH4 2- complex is a formal Ni(II) species and would be square planar, comparable to the square-planar PtH4 units found in K2PtH4 and Na2PtH4; the 18-valence-electron NiH4 4- complex, formally Ni(0), would instead be tetrahedral. compound_name: O(1D) + N2O(X 1Sigma+) reaction system — ground 1A' potential energy surface giving NO+NO and N2+O2(a 1Dg)
point_group: Cs (1A' ground PES; N2O itself linear, NNO = 180.0 deg)
geometry_source: optimized in this work at CASSCF (no analytical CASPT2 gradients in MOLCAS 4.1, so CASSCF geometries were made as good as possible); stationary points first located with (14,12) then reoptimized at CASSCF(18,14); transition-state geometries additionally refined at the CASPT2 level to give approximate CASPT2 structures
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — CASSCF geometries with point-wise CASPT2 single points; transition state theory used for the kinetics
basis_set: Pople Cartesian Gaussian basis sets, chiefly 6-311G(2d) (100 basis functions for the system); 6-311+G(2d) also used for some stationary points
active_space_orbital_description: (14,12)B = all atomic 2p-derived molecular orbitals; (14,12)A = the same but with one 2p-derived MO replaced by one N-2s-derived MO; (18,14)A/B add 4 electrons in two further 2s(N and O)-derived MOs to (14,12)A or B respectively. CI expansion ~85 000 CSFs for (14,12) and ~500 000 CSFs for (18,14) in 1A' symmetry
active_space_protocol: Active orbitals chosen by a natural-orbital-occupation-number (NOON) criterion — keep as active the MOs with NOONs between 0.02 and 1.98 in the state-averaged first-order density matrix, which is argued to give the lowest energy for a fixed CI expansion size. Applied strictly, this criterion gives a DIFFERENT space per reactive channel — (14,12) for the NO+NO channel and (12,10) for the N2+O2 channel — hence inconsistent at, e.g., reactants; the authors instead adopt a homogeneous space over the whole PES even where NOONs fall outside those limits, accepting spaces that are not strictly homogeneous, and aiming at the lowest-energy ground-PES stationary points (NOONs maximally different from 0.0/2.0). Full valence is not feasible for this system, so trial and error plus comparison with experiment was needed. Sequence: (14,12)B all 2p-derived MOs; (14,12)A swaps one for an N 2s MO — needed because nitrogen is a limiting case for which orbitals to make active; (18,14)A/B add two 2s(N,O) MOs (+4 electrons). (18,14)A partitions as O(2,2)+N2O(16,12), i.e. the full valence space of the N2O fragment is correlated. At CASSCF, space A is clearly favoured for (14,12) and the A/B differences shrink for (18,14); once point-wise CASPT2 is applied all four spaces give similar results. B-type spaces were always used in products and describe some regions better
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A' (lowest singlet PES of the O(1D)+N2O system). Reaction energies, paper's kcal/mol at CASSCF with point-wise CASPT2 in parentheses [eV converted from the CASPT2 values], across the four active spaces: O(1D)+N2O -> NO+NO — (14,12)A -76.1 (-79.7) [-3.456]; (14,12)B -93.1 (-82.4) [-3.573]; (18,14)A -78.3 (-80.5) [-3.491]; (18,14)B -80.0 (-81.0) [-3.513]; experiment -80.4 [-3.486]. O(1D)+N2O -> N2+O2(a 1Dg) — (14,12)A -100.8 (-103.8) [-4.501]; (14,12)B -117.8 (-106.4) [-4.614]; (18,14)A -101.3 (-103.6) [-4.492]; (18,14)B -103.0 (-104.0) [-4.510]; experiment -100.9 [-4.375]
Other: The active-space choice is itself a main result: exoergicities and the N2O geometry vary strongly between the A and B spaces at CASSCF(14,12) (the NO+NO exoergicity swings from -76.1 to -93.1 kcal/mol), the spread narrows at (18,14), and CASPT2 washes out the difference almost entirely — evidence that dynamic correlation compensates an imperfect reference. N2O geometries (RNN / RNO / NNO angle, A and deg) for (14,12)A/(14,12)B and, in parentheses, (18,14)A/(18,14)B: 1.1323/1.1146 (1.1343/1.1339) [expt 1.1273]; 1.1901/1.1949 (1.1931/1.1919) [expt 1.1851]; 180.0 throughout. The 1Dg state of O is five-fold degenerate and resolves in the Cs subgroup into three A' and two A'' components; several 1A' and 1A'' PESs correlate reactants with both product channels. Stationary points reported at CASPT2//CASSCF(18,14)/6-311G(2d) except TS A3 (CASPT2//CASSCF(14,12)/6-311G(2d)); compared with BD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ and earlier CASPT2(10,10)/6-311+G(2d)//CASSCF(10,10)/6-31G(d) work. active_space_protocol: Deliberate hierarchy rather than one space. An (8,6) space is stated to be the MINIMUM needed to describe the topology of the surfaces, and its energetics can be corrected by CASMP2 single points — but CASMP2 gradients are unavailable, so improving the GEOMETRIES requires enlarging the space instead, which is why the C-O sigma/sigma* orbitals were added to give (12,10). The further (12,12) space (adding two virtual n* orbitals) is too large for CASSCF geometry optimization, so those structures were optimized with GVB-CAS keeping the four C-O sigma orbitals in the GVB space, and CAS(8,8)/MP2 energies (without the sigma/sigma*) were computed at those structures. Frequencies at every critical point used a (4,4) space at CASSCF/6-31G*, with (8,6) frequencies at four selected points (a, b, m, q) for the thermal corrections in Table 1. Spin-orbit couplings use a one-electron operator with the effective nuclear charges of Koseki et al. (C 3.6, O 5.6).
electronic_structure_description: Ground state S0 and lowest triplet T1, labelled by pi-electron count: the 1(4pi) singlet biradical surface, the 3(3pi) triplet biradical surface (about 2 kcal/mol below 1(4pi)) and the 2pi singlet/triplet states. Ring-opening barrier TS1 (a gauche structure, b) has an activation energy of ca. 17.6 kcal/mol uncorrected, 16.3 kcal/mol thermally corrected, against an experimental threshold of 22 kcal/mol for unsubstituted dioxetane. A syn MAXS saddle point lies some 6 kcal/mol above TS1. The lowest 1(4pi) biradical BIRS (anti, structure j) lies 9 kcal/mol below TS1 and is unstable to C-C cleavage — its fragmentation barrier could not be fully optimized. The anti minimum on the 3(3pi) surface, BIRT (structure m), lies 5-6 kcal/mol below TS1. At the best level (CAS(12,10)/6-31+G* + MP2 + thermal correction) the triplet fragmentation transition state TS2 (structure q) lies 20.3 kcal/mol above the reactant, 16.5 kcal/mol thermally corrected, so TS1 and TS2 are both about 16.5 kcal/mol. Spin-orbit coupling is large, ca. 60 cm-1, throughout the singlet/triplet crossing region, implying facile intersystem crossing along a crossing 'line' spanning the ground-state O-O cleavage valley a few kcal/mol above it.

CASMP2 on an (8,6) reference fixes the energies but cannot fix the GEOMETRIES, because CASMP2 gradients do not exist — so dynamic correlation had to be smuggled into the optimization by enlarging the space instead, adding the C-O sigma/sigma* pair to reach (12,10). Pushing further to (12,12) with two virtual n* orbitals broke CASSCF optimization entirely and forced a GVB-CAS compromise in which the four C-O sigma orbitals sit in the GVB rather than the CAS space, with the subsequent MP2 energies then computed in a (8,8) space that DROPS the sigma/sigma* orbitals again — so the (12,12) geometries and the (8,8) energies do not share an active space. Frequencies rest on a much smaller (4,4) space than the energies, and near surface degeneracies made some of them unreliable (flagged in the table). Even at the best level the O-O cleavage barrier converges to ~16.5 kcal/mol against an experimental 22 kcal/mol, so the remaining error is not removed by any of these active-space extensions.

active_space_orbital_description: the paper writes spaces as (a/b) with a electrons and b orbitals. The quality of a CASSCF on a transition metal system is said to depend critically on the choice of space, which must include all valence orbitals needed for an adequate description of the metal-ligand bonding. Cr(CO)6 was shown in earlier work to be well described by a 10/10 space built from the metal 3d orbitals and their bonding and antibonding counterparts - an occupied e_g (CO sigma) and t_2g (Cr 3d) shell and a virtual e_g (Cr 3d) and t_2g (CO pi*) shell. For Cr(CO)5-PH the PH ligand has a triplet ground state with two singly occupied pi orbitals, so both must be added to the 10/10, giving 12 electrons in 12 orbitals. In the CASPT2 all valence electrons and the Cr semi-core 3s and 3p were correlated, while the C and O 1s, P 1s2s2p and Cr 1s2s2p were frozen.
active_space_protocol: 12/12, the established Cr(CO)6 10/10 metal-ligand space plus the two singly occupied pi orbitals of the PH ligand
electronic_structure_description: Stabilization of phosphinidene by complexation to Cr(CO)5. The free PH ligand has a triplet ground state; the closed-shell singlet used for comparison is not its lowest singlet, since an open-shell 1Delta lies lower, but that state no longer exists in substituted phosphinidenes.
Other: This is a textbook demonstration of building a space additively: take the space already established for the metal fragment - Cr(CO)6's 10/10, the 3d set with its bonding and antibonding partners - and add exactly the orbitals the new ligand brings, here PH's two singly occupied pi orbitals. The result, 12/12, is justified by construction rather than by a convergence test. | The reason those two orbitals are non-negotiable is that free PH is a triplet: a space that cannot hold its two open shells cannot describe the singlet-triplet balance the stabilization question turns on. | Note the (a/b) notation with a slash, electrons first - the same order as the usual convention but easy to misread as a ratio.

electronic_structure_description: Stationary points were located on the A~ 1B2 excited state surface and their geometries compared side by side against TD-DFT structures. The transition state was optimized under C2v symmetry, and the Hessian used to confirm what each stationary point is - which is what settles whether the excited state is planar or whether the planar structure is a barrier between two equivalent non-planar minima along the intramolecular proton transfer coordinate.
Other: The planarity question is really a question about a stationary point's Hessian, and that is why the method matters: CIS is documented to get proton-transfer energetics wrong through missing dynamical correlation, so the shape of the surface near the C2v structure cannot be trusted from it. The CAS(10,10) over the ring pi system gives geometries, CASPT2 gives energies, and the numerical Hessian decides the character of each point. Note the acknowledged limitation that CASPT2 enters only as single points, so the surface curvature itself is CASSCF-quality.

compound_name: trans-azomethane, CH3-N=N-CH3, on the surfaces relevant to its photodecomposition to two methyl radicals and N2
point_group: C2h at the planar equilibrium geometry, where the states are labelled Ag, Bg, Au and Bu; C2 once torsion around the N-N bond destroys the mirror plane
geometry_source: equilibrium and transition structures on S0 and T1 optimized by MP2/6-31G*, with the lowest singlet and lowest triplet of each C2 symmetry optimized by CASSCF; potential surfaces explored with respect to CNNC torsion and CNN bending, and the lowest point on the S0/S1 crossing seam located
method: state-averaged CASSCF for the surfaces, internally contracted MRCISD on top for the energetics, with CCSD(T) and MP2 alongside; conical intersection searches
software: GAUSSIAN for MP2, CCSD(T), the CASSCF frequencies and the conical intersection searches; MOLPRO for the CASSCF, CCSD(T) and MRCISD
basis_set: Huzinaga-Dunning DZP, a [4s2p1d] contraction of a (9s5p1d) primitive set, and cc-pVTZ; for structures with only C2 symmetry the full cc-pVTZ was too large, so a truncated version was used omitting the f polarization functions on carbon and nitrogen and the d functions on hydrogen
active_space_orbital_description: the base space is CASSCF(6,4): the bonding and antibonding pi orbitals plus the two nitrogen lone pairs, six electrons in four orbitals. For stretching a single C-N bond this is supplemented by a C-N sigma bonding and antibonding pair, giving CASSCF(8,6); for stretching both C-N bonds the second sigma/sigma* pair is added as well, giving CASSCF(10,8)
active_space_protocol: the space is grown to match the coordinate being explored rather than fixed globally: (6,4) for torsion and bending, (8,6) for single C-N stretching, (10,8) for double C-N stretching. Torsion and bending surfaces were computed with state-averaged CASSCF over the lowest seven states - four singlets and three triplets - with equal weights. The MRCISD was run on CASSCF(6,4) references, using both state-averaged and state-specific orbitals, which gave very close results
nroots_per_mult: the lowest seven states - four singlets and three triplets - equally weighted in the state averaging
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is (6bu)2(2au)2(7ag)2; S1 (1Bg) and T1 (3Bg) promote an electron from 7ag to the pi* orbital 2bg, S2 (1Au) and T3 (3Au) from 6bu, and S3 (1Bu) and T2 (3Bu) from 2au. The pi* orbital is empty in the ground state and singly occupied in every excited state listed, so the N-N bond lengthens and the torsional motion softens on excitation - which destroys the mirror plane and lowers the symmetry to C2. Vertical excitation energies for S0 to S1 and S0 to T1 agree well with experiment. The lowest S0/S1 crossing point, where excited molecules would internally convert efficiently, is asymmetric: a CNNC dihedral of 92.8 degrees with the two CNN angles unequal at 132.0 and 115.6 degrees. Transition structures were found for both simultaneous and sequential C-N bond cleavage on S0; the sequential barrier is about 7 kcal/mol higher in energy, but its Gibbs free energy of activation is lower above 0 degrees Celsius.
Other: The coordinate-matched space growth is the transferable idea: a four-orbital pi-plus-lone-pair space is right for torsion and bending, where nothing breaks, but stretching a C-N bond needs that bond's sigma and sigma* in the space, and stretching both needs both pairs. Using (6,4) for a dissociation coordinate would give a qualitatively wrong curve; using (10,8) for the torsion scan would be wasted. The check that keeps the MRCISD honest is running it on both state-averaged and state-specific CASSCF(6,4) orbitals and confirming they agree - state averaging over seven states is a substantial compromise for any one of them, and this is the evidence it did not distort the energetics. Note that the asymmetry of the S0/S1 crossing point - unequal CNN angles - is exactly the kind of feature a symmetry-constrained search would have missed.

The MLCT band, 3d(Mn) -> pi*(CO): e1A' 36075 cm-1 (41149), d1A'' 37410 (40249), f1A' 40690 cm-1, 5.09 eV (47733) f = 0.0040, g1A' 41175 cm-1, 5.15 eV (46629) f = 0.0052, e1A'' 42346 (43278), f1A'' 45019 (47939). The reference CASSCF weight is 0.720-0.733 for every state. Experimentally the first band runs to about 375 nm with a maximum at 30769 cm-1 (325 nm) and the second peaks near 250 nm (40000 cm-1). Optimized geometries (10e10a values in parentheses): ground state Mn-Cip 1.810 (1.830), Mn-Cop 1.806 (1.831), Mn-Cring 2.231 (2.215), C-O 1.148 (1.146) A, against gas-phase 1.808, 1.808, 2.149, 1.148 A. Other: This paper is a controlled experiment on one question: what do the four pi*(CO) orbitals do? The electron count is held at 10 and only the orbital count changes, 10 to 14, so the comparison is not confounded by a change in the reference. Two effects are documented. On GEOMETRY, adding the pi*(CO) orbitals lets the d(pi)-p(pi) Mn-CO back-donation be described, which brings the Mn-CO bond lengths into perfect agreement with the gas-phase values and, as a knock-on, lengthens Mn-Cring — the largest deviation anywhere, and the paper states that Mn-Cop and the average Mn-Cring 'are both very sensitive to the CASSCF active space'. Note the direction: the LARGER space makes Mn-Cring worse relative to experiment (2.231 versus 2.215 A against 2.149 experimental), because it improves the competing back-donation. Both spaces and DFT underestimate the Mn-Cp interaction. On the DISSOCIATIVE c1A' state the space difference is enormous — Mn-Cip comes out at 2.846 A with 10e14a but only 2.249 A with 10e10a, a 0.6 A discrepancy in the very coordinate that defines the photochemistry, because carbonyl loss cannot be described without the pi*(CO) orbitals that accept the back-donation being broken. A trap for reuse: this optimization never converged (values are after 20 cycles), so neither number is a stationary point. Finally, CASSCF alone overestimates every excitation energy by 5000-9000 cm-1 (0.6-1.1 eV) and MS-CASPT2 also REORDERS the states — at CASSCF b1A'' lies lowest at 30779 cm-1 but at MS-CASPT2 a1A'' is lowest at 24972 — so the CASSCF ordering must not be used. The reference weight is a uniform 0.72-0.73 across all states, which is the paper's evidence that the perturbation is balanced despite its size.

notes: The d electron count 3d6 is read directly from the stated ground-state configuration (3dz2)2(3dx2-y2)2(3dxy)2. method: CASSCF (FORS) with MRMP2 (multireference Moller-Plesset second-order perturbation theory) single points

active_space_protocol: The active space is specified by ORBITAL LABEL rather than by a description of orbital character, in Cs symmetry: [8a'-15a', 1a''-4a''] for Be, [12a'-19a', 2a''-5a''] for Mg and [16a'-23a', 3a''-6a''] for Ca. electronic_structure_description: MRMP2 energies relative to the entrance complex I(Be,S), in kcal/mol, at CASSCF(12/12) geometries (bond lengths r1 = N-N, r2 = N-O, r3 = M...O in angstroms): I(Be,S) 0.0 with r3 = 4.602 A, a very weakly bound complex; TS(Be,S,cis) 9.5 (classical barrier quoted as 8.9 kcal/mol with zero-point correction) at r3 = 1.783 A; TS(Be,S,trans) 16.0 (15.5 kcal/mol above I with ZPE); exit-channel complex II(Be,S) -97.6. reference_short: Tishchenko, Vinckier, Ceulemans & Nguyen, J. Phys. Chem. A 2005, 109, 6099
notes: Reaction 1 is N2O(X 1Sigma+) + M -> MO + N2. electronic_structure_description: One- and two-photon absorption of the diamond nitrogen-vacancy centre. Optimized structures remain diamond-like with only modest distortion around the defect. Vertical excitation energies with the 6-31G(d) basis: 2.53 +/- 0.03 eV from CAS(6,8) on the smaller clusters, 2.66 +/- 0.02 eV from CIS and 2.17 +/- 0.02 eV from TD-DFT on the three largest models. geometry_source: CASSCF single points on the isolated basic unit taken from the experimental low-temperature (low-spin) and high-temperature (high-spin) X-ray crystal structures; no geometry optimization.
