electronic_structure_description: Table 3 gives the S1-S0 energy difference at the S1 minimum geometry in kcal/mol, together with the dihedral angle describing the C6-methyl orientation, for each low-level method. Under ONIOM-CLS: CAS(S0) 64.30 with error -1.54 against the Target and dihedral 35.6 degrees; RHF 57.27, error -8.57, 53.8 degrees; ROHF triplet 65.43, -0.41, 21.6; ROHF quintet 66.32, +0.48, 15.2; UHF singlet 66.53, +0.69, 22.8; UHF triplet 66.06, +0.22, 22.7; UHF quintet 66.84, +1.00, 15.2; UFF 59.77, -6.07, 43.4; AM1 64.86, -0.98, 25.6. Under ONIOM-CLS*: CAS(S1) 67.53, +1.69, 17.1; CAS(S1)/4-31G 69.30, +3.46, 5.7; model-only 68.76, +2.92, 5.5; and the Target 65.84 with dihedral 5.7 degrees. The all-CASSCF ONIOM combination overestimates the gap by about 3 kcal/mol even though its geometry is identical to the Target, so that error comes entirely from the localized description of the excitation rather than from the low-level method, and no other combination can be expected to do better. The residual error correlates with the out-of-plane orientation of the methyl group attached to C6, the linear best fit crossing the y axis at 3.5 kcal/mol, close to the localization error itself. That dependence is attributed to the C5-C6 bond being near-single at about 1.48 Angstrom in the excited state and therefore easily deformed, while formally double in the ground state where small deformations cost significant energy; the largest errors accordingly occur with low-level methods that describe the ground state, namely CAS(S0), RHF, UHF singlet, UFF and AM1, since the Target geometry is an S1 structure. For the conical intersection geometry the model-only structure represents the Target better than it did for the S1 minimum, but is still markedly worse than every ONIOM calculation, especially in the (4,5,6) angle and the dihedrals, one of which differs by nearly 10 degrees; absence of the cyclic substituent means the bare model cannot reproduce the Target geometry. Most ONIOM combinations reproduce the Target well and slightly better than at the S1 minimum, presumably because the open-shell low-level methods emulate the electronic structure of the conical intersection better than that of the S1 minimum; the best are triplet UHF and ROHF and singlet UHF, while RHF and UFF perform worst, followed by AM1. For the conical intersection minus S1 minimum energy difference, most ONIOM methods with quantum mechanical low levels come close to the Target; UFF in the low level gives a significantly larger error and places the crossing below the minimum, while AM1 gives a small error of opposite sign to all the others, and the correlation with methyl orientation disappears.

Only with the space held constant can the differences in Table 3 be attributed to the ONIOM partitioning rather than to the reference. What the paper then measures is a cost that has no analogue in ordinary active-space error: the cost of localizing the excitation. The cleanest number is the all-CASSCF ONIOM combination, whose geometry is identical to the Target by construction and which still overestimates the S1-S0 gap by about 3 kcal/mol. The authors state the inference explicitly -- that error results completely from the localized description of the excitation and not from the level of theory used as the low level, and since every other combination also uses the localized description, none can be expected to do better. That establishes a floor on accuracy set by where the active space is placed in the molecule rather than by how big it is. The complementary finding is that the space cannot be placed on the model system in isolation: the model-only calculation, the same six-electron six-orbital pi space on bare hexatriene, reproduces neither the S1 minimum nor the conical intersection geometry properly, because the absence of the cyclic substituent leaves the geometry wrong. So the environment matters geometrically even though the correlated wave function never leaves the fragment. A third observation concerns what kind of low-level wave function is compatible with an active space describing a crossing. The conical intersection geometries come out better than the S1 minimum geometries across the board, which the authors attribute to the open-shell low-level methods emulating the electronic structure of the intersection better than that of the S1 minimum, and the best performers are triplet UHF and ROHF and singlet UHF, while closed-shell RHF is as bad as molecular mechanics. Since the exclusion of the -R group C=C from the active space is what forces this partitioning in the first place, the choice of which double bond to correlate propagates all the way to which single-reference method can sit outside it. One methodological caveat is recorded by the authors: the nocpmcscf approximation was used in the crossing search, a small approximation to the orbitals and hence the gradient near the degeneracy, accepted because ONIOM and Target were run with the same approximation, so the comparison is internally fair but the absolute intersection geometry carries that approximation.

active_space_protocol: The initial space comprised all fourteen actinide 5f orbitals with their ten electrons. Because that space showed the 5f orbitals localized on the metal with no evident interaction with the coordinating phosphonate oxygens, it was expanded below the valence 5f orbitals to admit an additional doubly occupied orbital and the corresponding antibonding orbital, which turned out to be an An 6p; that orbital also showed no interaction with the coordinating ligands. The ground state electronic configuration was described as slightly complex because of the unpaired f electrons per actinide atom.
electronic_structure_description: The An 5f orbitals are localized on the metal site with no evident interaction with any coordinating oxygen atoms of the phosphonate ligands, and the An 6p orbital admitted by expanding the space likewise shows no interaction with the coordinating ligands. At the DFT-PBE level the ten highest singly occupied alpha spin orbitals are localized Pu 5f orbitals, with a little electron density delocalized onto the O 2p orbital of select coordinating PO3 groups; just below the localized valence 5f orbitals lie O 2p orbitals of those PO3 groups. Partial atomic charges per actinide are 2.87 by Mulliken and 2.45 by LoProp at CASSCF, against 1.10 by Mulliken and 1.57 by natural population analysis at DFT-PBE. Natural population analysis gives Pu 5f5.38 and Pu 6d0.79, and Mulliken gives Pu 5f5.04 and Pu 6d0.54. Atomic populations from the total density at DFT-PBE give, by Loewdin, Pu 6s 4.185, 6p 12.440, 5d 11.467 and 5f 5.895; by natural population analysis 4.165, 11.994, 10.844 and 5.423; by Mulliken 4.267, 12.301, 10.906 and 5.404. Total alpha minus beta spin densities are 5.030 by Loewdin, 5.096 by natural population analysis and 5.066 by Mulliken, with the 5f contribution being 4.927, 4.915 and 4.949 respectively.
Other: The active space is chosen to answer one question -- whether the actinide 5f orbitals are involved in bonding to the phosphonate ligands -- and the paper's result is a negative that the space is deliberately structured to be able to detect. The initial spaces contain all fourteen An 5f orbitals with the electrons that occupy them, ten for the plutonium complex from Pu 5f5 and twelve for the americium complex from Am 5f6. Irrespective of structure and actinide metal, those 5f orbitals come out localized on the metal site, with no evident interaction with any coordinating oxygen atom of the phosphonate ligands. The important methodological step is what follows: rather than accepting a null result from the first space, the authors expanded the space below the valence 5f orbitals, adding one doubly occupied orbital and its corresponding antibonding partner, which in both complexes turned out to be an An 6p. That orbital also shows no interaction with the coordinating ligands. Enlarging downward is the right test here, because a space containing only metal-localized f orbitals cannot by construction show metal-ligand mixing -- there is no ligand orbital in it to mix with -- so the absence of covalency in the small space is uninformative until an orbital that could have shown it is admitted and still does not. A caution for anyone reusing these numbers: the arithmetic of the final space is not stated consistently. The text gives initial spaces of ten and twelve electrons in fourteen orbitals and describes the expansion as adding one doubly occupied orbital plus its antibonding partner, which would give twelve electrons in sixteen orbitals for the plutonium complex and fourteen in sixteen for the americium one, whereas the caption to the figure showing the americium bonding orbitals labels it a (16,16) active space. The initial spaces as explicitly stated are recorded in the electron and orbital columns here and the expansion is described in the protocol, rather than reconciling the two statements. A second and independent caveat concerns what the space says about charge. At the CASSCF level the Mulliken and LoProp methods give similar actinide partial charges, but the Mulliken values are on average 0.4e larger than the LoProp ones and closer to the formal trivalent state, and the DFT Mulliken and natural population charges are further from +3 still. Since the localization conclusion is read off orbital plots and the covalency discussion off partial charges, and those charges vary by more than an electron between analysis schemes on the same wave function, the qualitative orbital result is the more robust of the two. Notably the DFT analyses, not the CASSCF ones, are what reveal occupancy of the An 6d orbitals -- Pu 6d0.79 versus Am 6d0.84 from natural population analysis, marginally reversed at the Mulliken level with Pu 6d0.54 versus Am 6d0.51 -- and the 6d orbitals were never in the active space at all, so that part of the electronic structure lies entirely outside the multiconfigurational treatment.

active_space_protocol: The initial space comprised all fourteen actinide 5f orbitals with their twelve electrons, and was then expanded below the valence 5f orbitals to admit an additional doubly occupied orbital and its corresponding antibonding orbital, an An 6p, which showed no interaction with the coordinating ligands. The occupation numbers of the resulting bonding orbitals are given below the orbital plots in the corresponding figure.
electronic_structure_description: The An 5f orbitals are localized on the metal site with no evident interaction with any coordinating oxygen atoms of the phosphonate ligands, and the An 6p orbital admitted on expanding the space likewise shows no interaction. At the DFT-PBE level the twelve highest singly occupied alpha spin orbitals are localized Am 5f orbitals, again with a little density on the O 2p orbitals of select coordinating PO3 groups. Partial atomic charges per actinide are 2.86 by Mulliken and 2.49 by LoProp at CASSCF, against 1.44 by Mulliken and 1.71 by natural population analysis at DFT-PBE. Natural population analysis gives Am 5f6.23 and Am 6d0.84, and Mulliken gives Am 5f6.03 and Am 6d0.51, so the 6d occupation is larger for americium by natural population analysis while the ordering is marginally reversed at the Mulliken level. Atomic populations from the total density at DFT-PBE give, by Loewdin, Am 6s 4.158, 6p 12.435, 5d 11.483 and 5f 6.682; by natural population analysis 4.164, 11.990, 10.888 and 6.246; by Mulliken 4.215, 12.183, 10.822 and 6.320. Total alpha minus beta spin densities are 6.026, 6.101 and 6.061 by the three methods, with 5f contributions of 5.916, 5.903 and 5.935. The solid-state absorption spectrum contains characteristic peaks at 500, 820 and 1050 nm, assigned to the 5L6, 7F6 and 7F4 states, indicating the trivalent state of americium.
Other: The active space is chosen to answer one question -- whether the actinide 5f orbitals are involved in bonding to the phosphonate ligands -- and the paper's result is a negative that the space is deliberately structured to be able to detect. The initial spaces contain all fourteen An 5f orbitals with the electrons that occupy them, ten for the plutonium complex from Pu 5f5 and twelve for the americium complex from Am 5f6. Irrespective of structure and actinide metal, those 5f orbitals come out localized on the metal site, with no evident interaction with any coordinating oxygen atom of the phosphonate ligands. The important methodological step is what follows: rather than accepting a null result from the first space, the authors expanded the space below the valence 5f orbitals, adding one doubly occupied orbital and its corresponding antibonding partner, which in both complexes turned out to be an An 6p. That orbital also shows no interaction with the coordinating ligands. Enlarging downward is the right test here, because a space containing only metal-localized f orbitals cannot by construction show metal-ligand mixing -- there is no ligand orbital in it to mix with -- so the absence of covalency in the small space is uninformative until an orbital that could have shown it is admitted and still does not. A caution for anyone reusing these numbers: the arithmetic of the final space is not stated consistently. The text gives initial spaces of ten and twelve electrons in fourteen orbitals and describes the expansion as adding one doubly occupied orbital plus its antibonding partner, which would give twelve electrons in sixteen orbitals for the plutonium complex and fourteen in sixteen for the americium one, whereas the caption to the figure showing the americium bonding orbitals labels it a (16,16) active space. The initial spaces as explicitly stated are recorded in the electron and orbital columns here and the expansion is described in the protocol, rather than reconciling the two statements. A second and independent caveat concerns what the space says about charge. At the CASSCF level the Mulliken and LoProp methods give similar actinide partial charges, but the Mulliken values are on average 0.4e larger than the LoProp ones and closer to the formal trivalent state, and the DFT Mulliken and natural population charges are further from +3 still. Since the localization conclusion is read off orbital plots and the covalency discussion off partial charges, and those charges vary by more than an electron between analysis schemes on the same wave function, the qualitative orbital result is the more robust of the two. Notably the DFT analyses, not the CASSCF ones, are what reveal occupancy of the An 6d orbitals -- Pu 6d0.79 versus Am 6d0.84 from natural population analysis, marginally reversed at the Mulliken level with Pu 6d0.54 versus Am 6d0.51 -- and the 6d orbitals were never in the active space at all, so that part of the electronic structure lies entirely outside the multiconfigurational treatment.

method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by multireference configuration interaction, used to generate the data that a diabatic Jahn-Teller and pseudo-Jahn-Teller Hamiltonian is fitted to; the fitted surface then carries nuclear wave-packet propagation by the multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree method. active_space_protocol: full valence, so the same space applies unchanged at every one of six thousand nuclear configurations, which is what the fit requires - the surface is only as smooth as the orbitals behind it. The three lowest states are averaged together, which is not an option here but a necessity: two of them are the components of a degenerate pair at the planar geometry and the third crosses them, so no state-specific treatment could follow all three through the intersections. No symmetry was imposed anywhere.

electronic_structure_description: Three doublet sheets, the ground X 2A''(2) state and the two components of the first excited degenerate state. The ground state has two equivalent pyramidal minima separated along the umbrella coordinate by a barrier of only 0.099 eV, lower than earlier calculations had found. Two symmetry-allowed three-state conical intersections sit near plus and minus 0.9 radian in that coordinate, and when displacements in all three bending modes are allowed they are joined by a hyperline of two-state intersections. Reproducing the data required expanding the Jahn-Teller and pseudo-Jahn-Teller coupling to eighth order in the bending modes - 208 coefficients in all. The simulated first photoelectron band is a single extended progression reflecting how far the umbrella angle moves on ionization, and the second band is nearly structureless, matching experiment, its diffuseness caused by the exceptionally strong coupling. Dynamically, the Jahn-Teller motion within the excited state finishes in about 5 fs, roughly 80 percent of the excited-state population reaches the ground state within about 10 fs, and after 20 fs the wave packets are so delocalized that no further population transfer occurs out to 100 fs.
Other: The active space is doing something a static calculation never asks of one: it has to remain the same object across six thousand geometries spanning three intersecting sheets, two of them degenerate at the reference point, because the entire result is a fitted analytic surface and any discontinuity in the orbitals would appear as a spurious feature in the dynamics. Averaging the three states together is what makes that possible. The payoff is that an eighth-order coupling expansion - unusually high, and needed because of how anharmonic the surface is around the intersections - can be fitted to data that is internally consistent, and the resulting 10 fs decay and structureless second photoelectron band both follow from the coupling rather than being put in by hand.

The kinetic energy operator uses Wilson G-matrix elements frozen at their values at the planar reference geometry.

electronic_structure_description: Table 4 gives excitation energies in eV with oscillator strengths, from PBE, CASSCF and CAS-srPBE alongside CASPT2, CC2, CCSD, CCSD(T) and a best estimate. 2 1A' pi to pi*: 4.51 (0.126), 6.02 (0.219), 5.31 (0.235), 5.11 (0.398), 5.20, 5.30 (0.021), 5.04, best 5.25 (0.302). 3 1A' pi to pi*: 4.90 (0.043), 5.00 (0.018), 5.48 (0.043), 5.02 (0.015), 5.20, 5.47 (0.275), 5.23, best 5.25 (0.302). 1 1A'' n to pi*: 4.24 (0.000), 6.31 (0.009), 5.44 (0.001), 5.04 (0.002), 5.13, 5.54 (0.001), 5.28, best 5.12 (0.007). 2 1A'' n to pi*: 4.77 (0.004), 6.37 (0.009), 5.98 (0.002), 5.75 (0.007), 5.74, 6.10 (0.003), 5.84, best 5.75 (0.003). 4 1A' pi to pi*: 5.14 (0.025), 7.08 (0.460), 6.59 (0.470), 6.25 (0.510), 6.58 (0.478), 6.36. 5 1A' pi to pi*: 5.41 (0.029), 6.61 (0.078), 6.10 (0.045), 6.65 (0.069), 6.68 (0.035), 6.53. 6 1A' pi to pi*: 5.77 (0.122), 7.73 (0.181), 7.18 (0.208), 6.96 (0.344). 7 1A' pi to pi*: 5.49 (0.034), 7.27 (0.006), 6.96 (0.032), 7.55 (0.036). Table 5 gives statistics over all four molecules for the three methods against CASPT2 and CC2 references, with oscillator strength statistics in parentheses. Counts are 30 states against CASPT2 and 26 against CC2. CAS-srPBE: mean deviations 0.13 and 0.11, mean absolute deviations 0.26 and 0.19, maximum 0.59 and 0.63 eV. CASSCF: means 0.71 and 0.71, mean absolute deviations 0.74 and 0.75, maxima 1.89 and 1.65 eV. PBE: means -1.07 and -1.09, mean absolute deviations 1.07 and 1.09, maxima 2.06 and 1.75 eV.
Other: The active spaces are selected algorithmically and by a chemical rule stated in one sentence: the spaces used in both the range-separated and the pure wave function calculations were based on MP2-srDFT and MP2 natural orbitals following previously described criteria, and they contain all pi/pi* orbitals as well as the n orbitals involved in a given excitation. That gives (12,12) for thymine, uracil and adenine and (10,10) for cytosine, sized to each molecule's own pi system rather than fixed across the set. The paper's point is what happens to those same spaces when short-range dynamical correlation is supplied by a density functional instead of by perturbation theory, and the statistics are unambiguous. Against CASPT2 and CC2 references over 30 and 26 states, plain CASSCF on these spaces has mean deviations of 0.71 eV against both and mean absolute deviations of 0.74 and 0.75 eV, with a maximum error of 1.89 eV; the same spaces with the short-range functional attached give mean deviations of 0.13 and 0.11 eV, mean absolute deviations of 0.26 and 0.19 eV, and a maximum of 0.59 eV. Pure density functional theory sits on the other side, underestimating by about 1.07 to 1.09 eV. So the active space is doing the same job in both cases and the entire near-eV improvement comes from the correlation treatment layered on it -- which is the cleanest available demonstration that a well-chosen space is necessary but not remotely sufficient. The individual tables show where CASSCF alone fails worst: for uracil the lowest n to pi* state comes out at 5.66 eV against a best estimate of 4.80, and the third 1A' pi to pi* state at 7.89 against 6.26 eV, errors of nearly 1.7 eV on a space that contains exactly the orbitals those excitations use. Oscillator strengths move too, and not always toward the reference. A second and quite different active-space concern is flagged by the authors and handled explicitly: with the large diffuse basis used, assignments of electronic transitions are not always straightforward because of Rydberg-valence mixing, so the nature of every excitation was examined by inspecting the orbitals appearing in the response vectors rather than trusting state labels. They find that some excitations are contaminated with Rydberg states, and to probe the effect they repeated the calculations in a basis without diffuse functions; in every case where an excitation is sensitive to adding diffuse functions the energy is lowered. That matters for reuse because a space selected from natural orbitals in a diffuse basis can admit Rydberg character that a valence-labelled orbital list would not reveal. Two practical notes: the range-separation parameter was fixed at 0.4 as previously recommended rather than optimized per system, and an alternative short-range exchange functional was tested without changing any conclusions. Cs symmetry was imposed on all four molecules, and some reference values quoted for comparison come from structures obtained with different methodologies.

ligand_set: para dimethylamino donor and nitrile acceptor on a benzene ring
point_group: C1 for unconstrained optimizations; a previously proposed C2-constrained partially twisted ICT structure was specifically tested and rejected as a likely constraint artefact
geometry_source: Ground, LE, PICT, RICT, TICT(Q) and TICT(AQ) geometries are the CASSCF geometries of ref. 4 (energies recomputed here at MS-CASPT2/cc-pVDZ); the LE/S0 and CT/S0 conical intersections and the transition state were optimized here at CASSCF/6-31G* without symmetry constraints. The ground state is untwisted with a 43.0 degree amino wag, the LE structure is near-planar, and TICT is amino-twisted/pyramidal. The six-page ESI gives selected bond lengths and rendered structures but no complete Cartesian or full internal-coordinate block, so no XYZ is fabricated.
method: MS-CASPT2(12,11)/cc-pVDZ single-point energies recomputed at the CASSCF critical-point geometries of ref. 4; new CASSCF(12,11)/6-31G* optimization of the LE/S0 and CT/S0 conical intersections and the transition state on the radiationless-decay path, with MS-CASPT2 energies; pTICT minimum search; CASSI transition moments from perturbed-modified CAS-CI wavefunctions
basis_set: 6-31G* for CASSCF geometry optimizations and MS-CASPT2 energy paths; cc-pVDZ for MS-CASPT2 single-point energies at CASSCF critical geometries
active_space_orbital_description: Six benzene pi/pi* orbitals, the dimethylamino nitrogen lone pair, and four cyano-group pi/pi* orbitals.
active_space_protocol: The common CAS(12,11) was used for ground, LE, ICT(Q), ICT(AQ), and ICT(CN) surfaces, minima, crossings, and paths. At TICT(Q), PM-CAS-CI mixes the ICT(Q) and LE CASSCF functions with nearly equal weights; a reported CAS(14,13) test adding the ring-amino sigma/sigma* pair decoupled those states without materially changing the energy, supporting retention of CAS(12,11). An exhaustive pTICT search varied active-space size/composition, basis, and geometric constraints but found no unconstrained minimum.
nroots_per_mult: Multiple singlet roots spanning S0, LE, ICT(Q), ICT(AQ), and ICT(CN); pair-state averaging for crossings/path calculations, while a single global root count is not reported
electronic_structure_description: At the Franck-Condon geometry, MS-CASPT2 vertical energies relative to S0 are 93.3 kcal mol^-1 for LE (dipole 6.01 D, f=0.006) and 102.7 for bright ICT(Q) (13.80 D, f=0.608), versus experimental nonpolar-band maxima 92.2 and 101.9. Relative to the S1-LE minimum, adiabatic energies/dipoles are: S2-PICT 8.44 kcal mol^-1/13.8 D; S1-RICT 22.81/16.8; S1-TICT(Q) 0.10/13.5; S2-TICT(AQ) 14.60/14.1. Thus LE and TICT(Q) are essentially isoenergetic, while RICT and TICT(AQ) are too high to be competitive emitters.
Other: Initial excitation populates ICT(Q); low-energy access between the LE and TICT surfaces allows both minima to be populated. Emission from LE is calculated to be 14 times more probable than from TICT, explaining normal fluorescence in gas/nonpolar media and dual fluorescence only when a polar environment stabilizes TICT. The radiationless-decay study newly reports a LE/S0 CI 17.6 kcal mol^-1 above LE at CASSCF and a CT/S0 CI 2.8 kcal mol^-1 above LE, but the transition state toward the CT/S0 crossing is 19.9 kcal mol^-1 at CASSCF and 8.2 at CASPT2 (experimental activation estimate 8.3). CASPT2 state energies at the LE/S0 CI are 27.3/37.5 kcal mol^-1 and at the CT/S0 CI -2.4/-13.5, illustrating the stated geometry-level inconsistency. The non-negligible barrier keeps internal conversion modest near room temperature. No stable pTICT minimum was found; a C2-constrained literature structure is interpreted as a likely saddle along pyramidalization.

ligand_set: para primary-amino donor and nitrile acceptor on a tetrafluorinated benzene ring
point_group: C1; all geometry optimizations were performed without symmetry constraints
geometry_source: Ground, LE, TICT(Q), RICT, TICT(AQ), S2/S1 and S3/S2 crossings, four S1/S0 crossings, and path transition states were optimized at CASSCF/6-31G*. The ground state is untwisted with a 40.0 degree amino wag; at LE the F atoms lie about 23 degrees out of the ring plane; TICT has a twisted/pyramidal amino group; RICT has a 123.8 degree cyano bend. The ESI supplies selected bond lengths and rendered critical structures but no complete Cartesian/full internal-coordinate block, so no XYZ is fabricated.
method: CASSCF(12,11) geometry optimization, conical-intersection searches, frequencies, and minimum-energy paths with MS-CASPT2 single-point/path energies; CASSI oscillator strengths from perturbed-modified CAS-CI wavefunctions; LIIC profiles and SA(2)-CASSCF/CASPT2 S1/S0 paths; expanded-active-space tests of C-F sigma* participation
basis_set: 6-31G* (also written 6-31G(d) in ESI Fig. S4) for CASSCF optimizations and MS-CASPT2 paths; cc-pVDZ for MS-CASPT2 single points at CASSCF critical geometries
active_space_orbital_description: Six benzene pi/pi* orbitals, the amino-nitrogen lone pair, and four cyano-group pi/pi* orbitals. A test CAS(12,12) adds the totally symmetric combination of antibonding C-F sigma* orbitals; a CAS(14,13) TICT test adds the ring-amino sigma/sigma* pair.
active_space_protocol: The production space is CAS(12,11). A CAS(12,12) calculation at the LE geometry tested possible pi-to-C-F-sigma* character and found none, confirming a pure LE state. A CAS(14,13) TICT test separated mixed LE/ICT references without appreciably changing energy. The high ICT(CN) root and S3/S2 ICT(Q)/ICT(CN) crossing used 13-state averaging. S1/S0 path profiles used SA(2)-CASSCF/CASPT2/6-31G*, and CI energies are averages over the two crossing states.
nroots_per_mult: Case-dependent singlet averaging: 13 states for the high ICT(CN) root/crossing; two states for SA(2) S1/S0 paths; general MS-CASPT2 root count otherwise not reported
electronic_structure_description: At FC, MS-CASPT2 gives LE 113.14 kcal mol^-1 (dipole 5.10 D, f=0.001) and bright ICT(Q) 126.23 (10.54 D, f=0.569) above S0; the nonpolar absorption maximum is 111.5. Relative to S1-LE, S1-TICT(Q) lies 4.58 kcal mol^-1 higher (10.5 D), S1-RICT 19.14 higher (9.2 D), and S3-TICT(AQ) 46.70 higher (13.6 D); no PICT minimum exists. The S2/S1 ICT(Q)/LE minimum crossing lies 12.44 kcal mol^-1 below the vertical excitation. The LE-to-TICT adiabatic barrier is 5.7 kcal mol^-1 and the reverse barrier only 0.3, thermodynamically favoring LE even though both surfaces can be populated.
Other: The ICT(CN) state is S7 at FC, 181.12 kcal mol^-1 above S0; relaxation brings it through an S3/S2 ICT(CN)/ICT(Q) CI only 7.92 kcal mol^-1 above the initial excitation at a 142.2 degree cyano bend, making a mediated RICT route possible but secondary. Four S1/S0 crossings were located. Relative to LE, CASSCF/CASPT2 state energies are CI-1 LE 2.4/-19.1 and S0 3.3/0.7; CI-2 LE 18.1/4.2 and S0 18.7/14.5; CI-3 LE 18.2/16.8 and S0 18.3/20.2; CI-4 ICT -2.3/-18.6 and S0 -0.6/-8.8. TS-1 is 3.5/-3.8 and TS-4 11.9/8.2. The more reliable SA(2) path profile gives about a 3.0 kcal mol^-1 lowest radiationless barrier, effectively accessible after excitation. TICT emission has f=0.007 versus LE f=0.003; fast LE internal conversion leaves weak ICT fluorescence, computed at 75.1 versus 71.3 kcal mol^-1 experimental, with quantum yield about 6e-5. Fluorination therefore promotes both ICT and ring-puckering nonradiative decay.

electronic_structure_description: DMABN-4F is the only series member whose ICT(Q) state is below LE at FC: MS-CASPT2 vertical energies are 95.7 kcal mol^-1 for ICT(Q) (dipole 14.22 D, f=0.318) and 97.9 for LE (5.03 D, f=0.009), versus a 95.5 experimental nonpolar absorption maximum; S0 has dipole 4.88 D. Other: Initial excitation directly populates ICT(Q), followed by barrierless ultrafast relaxation to the TICT minimum. The computed TICT emission is 58.4 kcal mol^-1 versus 59.6 measured in n-hexane, explaining the sole anomalous band. The competing LE/S0 CI lies 3.9 kcal mol^-1 below LE at CASSCF; its path TS is only 2.6 above LE, while CASPT2 gives CI state energies -13.5/-18.8 and a TS energy -7.0. Although the CASPT2 values reflect non-reoptimized critical geometries, both levels show nearly barrierless LE internal conversion, precluding normal emission and suppressing the ICT quantum yield to 2.6e-3. The second-order exchange-density/one-electron-density analysis distinguishes aromatic S0, anti-Kekule LE, quinoid charge-separated TICT, and bent-cyano RICT structures. Methyl donation and steric pre-twisting stabilize TICT, while fluorination both increases acceptor strength and facilitates ring-puckering decay.

method: CASSCF active-orbital/natural-occupation analysis and CASSCF-PT2 reaction energetics on a DFT-optimized interligand-addition path. DFT, CCSD, CCSD(T), T1-diagnostic, frequency, and IRC calculations provide mechanistic and benchmark context.
active_space_orbital_description: The Ni(edt)2 ligand-pi CAS(10,8) space (four carbon p-pi and four sulfur p-pi orbitals) is augmented by the two ethylene p-pi orbitals and two electrons. In 2H, two sulfur and two ethylene orbitals form two C-S bonding/antibonding pairs; the other two sulfur orbitals become nearly uninvolved lone pairs.
active_space_protocol: CAS(12,10) was chosen as the total active space for the interligand ethylene-addition reaction and analyzed at the omega-B97XD/6-31++G** geometries. The TS2yH pathway geometry and energetics are consolidated with the endpoint connectivity. Root count, state averaging, weights, convergence thresholds, and detailed CASSCF-PT2 settings are not reported.
nroots_per_mult: The lowest-energy singlet is analyzed; formal root count and state-averaging details are not reported
electronic_structure_description: Formation of 2H consumes the ethylene pi bond and forms two polarized C-S sigma bonds. The correlated singly occupied orbital pairs have occupations about 1.1 for the bonding-like orbitals (#5 and #6) and 0.9 for the antibonding-like orbitals (#9 and #10). The remaining ligand-carbon orbitals split into two occupation groups, while two sulfur orbitals revert toward lone pairs, reducing the multireference character relative to 1H.
Other: Relative to 1H + ethylene at 0 K, the reported 2H reaction enthalpy is +3.3 kcal/mol at CASSCF-PT2 and -7.7 kcal/mol at CASSCF; the TS2yH barrier is 49.5 and 46.2 kcal/mol, respectively. The CCSD T1 diagnostic for 2H is 0.045. electronic_structure_description: The ground state is a 3A'' triplet, essentially a single configuration with weight 0.925. The lowest excited state is a 1A' singlet at 10841 reciprocal centimetres, strongly two-configurational with weights 0.686 and 0.242 for configurations differing by a double excitation between the 14a' and 7a'' orbitals. A 1A'' state follows at 11248 reciprocal centimetres with weight 0.933, and a second 1A' state at 18094 reciprocal centimetres with weights 0.388 and 0.515, the second configuration dominating. All three of these singlets have oscillator strengths below 1e-10. Higher triplet and singlet states at 27710 and 28110 reciprocal centimetres carry oscillator strengths of 0.004 and 0.002 and show a much longer N-C bond, 1.643 and 1.652 Angstrom against 1.438 in the ground state. The 14a' and 7a'' orbitals are described as almost degenerate in the two 1A' states. Vertical absorption maxima are computed at 336 and 340 nanometres and emission at 383 and 392 nanometres. C-N hyperconjugation shortens the N-C bond, and increased s character along that axis strengthens the bonding interaction.
Other: This paper is an unusually clear case of a space whose NECESSITY varies from state to state within the same molecule, and the configuration weights make the point quantitatively. The triplet ground state is essentially a single configuration, weight 0.925 to 0.934, so a single-determinant method would describe it adequately. The low-lying closed-shell singlets are not: for the tert-butyl species the lowest 1A' state splits 0.686 against 0.242 between two configurations that differ by a double excitation between the two frontier orbitals, and the second 1A' state splits 0.388 against 0.515 -- meaning the configuration listed as leading is not the one with the largest weight. For the isopropyl species the inversion is present in the lowest singlet too, 0.420 against 0.516. Two configurations of comparable weight, with the ordering flipping between two states of the same symmetry, is exactly the situation that no single-reference method can represent, and the authors trace it to a physical cause: the two frontier orbitals are described as almost degenerate in these states. So the space is doing real work for half the states studied and almost none for the other half, and a reader comparing this study to a single-reference one should expect agreement on the triplet and disagreement on the singlets. The space itself is chosen by an explicitly stated trade-off between cost and precision, with a chemical rationale for what is left out -- the methyl groups are described as stable, so their orbitals stay inactive -- giving eight electrons in eighteen orbitals for the tert-butyl nitrene, itemized as eleven orbitals of one symmetry and seven of the other, and eight electrons in fifteen orbitals, nine and six, for the isopropyl nitrene. Note the shape of that space: far more orbitals than electrons, so the great majority are weakly occupied virtuals. This is the opposite of the usual balanced-space design, and it is a deliberate choice for a system whose interesting physics is a near-degeneracy among low-lying virtuals rather than strong correlation among many electrons. Because the spaces differ in size between the two molecules, the comparison between them is not strictly like-for-like, though both keep the electron count fixed at eight. Geometries were optimized for every state at the uncorrelated level and the perturbative correction applied at those geometries; the transition moments come from the uncorrected wave function while the excitation energies, which the authors note are very sensitive to dynamic correlation, come from the corrected one -- another split of labour between the two levels within a single reported oscillator strength. A version check is reported: the calculations were repeated in an older release of the program and gave almost the same results.

The lowest excited state is a 1A' singlet at 10953 reciprocal centimetres whose two configurations carry weights 0.420 and 0.516, so the second configuration dominates. A 1A'' state follows at 11512 reciprocal centimetres with weight 0.934, and a second 1A' state at 18694 reciprocal centimetres with weights 0.398 and 0.510. Higher states at 28916, 29316, 38559 and 38918 reciprocal centimetres show progressively longer N-C bonds, reaching 1.774 Angstrom against 1.438 in the ground state; the state at 28916 carries an oscillator strength of 0.012, the largest computed here. Vertical absorption maxima are computed at 324 and 333 nanometres and emission at 379 and 374 nanometres.
Other: This paper is an unusually clear case of a space whose NECESSITY varies from state to state within the same molecule, and the configuration weights make the point quantitatively. The triplet ground state is essentially a single configuration, weight 0.925 to 0.934, so a single-determinant method would describe it adequately. The low-lying closed-shell singlets are not: for the tert-butyl species the lowest 1A' state splits 0.686 against 0.242 between two configurations that differ by a double excitation between the two frontier orbitals, and the second 1A' state splits 0.388 against 0.515 -- meaning the configuration listed as leading is not the one with the largest weight. For the isopropyl species the inversion is present in the lowest singlet too, 0.420 against 0.516. Two configurations of comparable weight, with the ordering flipping between two states of the same symmetry, is exactly the situation that no single-reference method can represent, and the authors trace it to a physical cause: the two frontier orbitals are described as almost degenerate in these states. So the space is doing real work for half the states studied and almost none for the other half, and a reader comparing this study to a single-reference one should expect agreement on the triplet and disagreement on the singlets. The space itself is chosen by an explicitly stated trade-off between cost and precision, with a chemical rationale for what is left out -- the methyl groups are described as stable, so their orbitals stay inactive -- giving eight electrons in eighteen orbitals for the tert-butyl nitrene, itemized as eleven orbitals of one symmetry and seven of the other, and eight electrons in fifteen orbitals, nine and six, for the isopropyl nitrene. Note the shape of that space: far more orbitals than electrons, so the great majority are weakly occupied virtuals. This is the opposite of the usual balanced-space design, and it is a deliberate choice for a system whose interesting physics is a near-degeneracy among low-lying virtuals rather than strong correlation among many electrons. Because the spaces differ in size between the two molecules, the comparison between them is not strictly like-for-like, though both keep the electron count fixed at eight. Geometries were optimized for every state at the uncorrelated level and the perturbative correction applied at those geometries; the transition moments come from the uncorrected wave function while the excitation energies, which the authors note are very sensitive to dynamic correlation, come from the corrected one -- another split of labour between the two levels within a single reported oscillator strength. Other: Result: once the system is trapped in the 1(n,pi*) minimum, intersystem crossing proceeds with a time constant of about 1 ps, with the triplet manifold relaxing to T1 (3 pi,pi*). Experimental time constants for thymine are mostly sub-picosecond and a few picoseconds (5-7 ps), with some groups reporting nanosecond components and one reporting 2.8 and 30 ps. method: CASSCF used to determine multiconfigurational character and to test whether single-reference wave functions suffice, on density functional geometries; nonresonance Raman spectra computed for both spin states
software: Gaussian 09 for the CASSCF calculations; TURBOMOLE V7.0 for the density functional work
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in ten orbitals, described by the authors as a modest space, held fixed across the whole size series.
active_space_protocol: The space is deliberately kept constant across clusters spanning one to forty-two fused rings so that the leading configuration coefficient is comparable along the series; it therefore samples a shrinking fraction of the valence manifold as the clusters grow, and the authors present the result as detection of multiconfigurational character rather than its quantification.
electronic_structure_description: A rectangular cluster with 1 units along the zigzag edge and 1 along the armchair edge, comprising 1 fused rings. The squared coefficient of the leading configuration is 0.78 for the singlet and 0.56 for the triplet, and the triplet lies 33.019 kcal/mol from the singlet, so the singlet lies lower.
Other: Space fixed at ten electrons in ten orbitals, which the authors call modest, and held constant across clusters from one fused ring to forty-two, so the squared leading configuration coefficient is a like-for-like measure across the series. For the singlet it falls from 0.78 in the smallest cluster to 0.33-0.40 in the larger ones; for the triplet it stays between 0.49 and 0.77. Relative energies collapse from 33 kcal per mole in favour of the singlet at one ring to within a few hundredths of a kcal per mole, changing sign to favour the triplet past roughly a dozen rings. The space does not grow with the pi system it samples, so it covers a shrinking fraction of the valence manifold as the series extends, and the authors present the coefficient as detection rather than quantification. Workflow: density-functional geometries were tested for triplet-singlet instability of the reference wave function first, and where instabilities appeared the spin and spatial symmetry constraints were released and the geometry reoptimized with a broken-symmetry treatment before the multiconfigurational step. Reported spin contamination grows about 1.2 times faster along one edge direction than the other, more in the singlet than the triplet.
reference_short: Pablo-Pedro, Lopez-Rios, Fomine & Dresselhaus, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2017, 8, 615
notes: One of a series of rectangular hydrogen-passivated silicene nanoclusters indexed by the number of units along the zigzag and armchair edges. Across the series the singlet is the ground state when the zigzag index exceeds the armchair one, with a switch to a triplet ground state in the opposite regime; the two can be distinguished experimentally through characteristic Raman modes. correlation_correction: None; the CASSCF wave function is used to measure the leading configuration weight rather than to produce correlated energies.

active_space_orbital_description: Thirteen electrons in ten orbitals for the cation: the full pi valence occupied and virtual space plus the two occupied nO and nN lone-pair orbitals, the latter added expressly to make the 2n+ cationic states representable. active_space_protocol: The space is stated as 'the full pi valence occupied and virtual space plus the two occupied n lone pair orbitals to include the 2n+ states'. electronic_structure_description: The parent nucleobase cation. Its four lowest cationic states arise from removing an electron from the highest pi orbital, the two oxygen and nitrogen lone pairs, and the next pi orbital down, giving the 2pi+HOMO ground state and 2nO+, 2piHOMO-1+ and 2nN+ excited states. Vertical ionisation potentials come out at 7.62, 8.63, 8.67 and 9.08 eV from CASSCF and 8.82, 9.68, 9.77 and 10.14 from XMS-CASPT2, with the averaged CASPT2 values of 8.74, 9.44, 9.59 and 9.94 carrying standard deviations of 0.16 to 0.28 eV from the choice of zeroth-order Hamiltonian alone; the ground-state vertical and adiabatic values fall within the measured range. Geometrically the ground cationic state shows only a 0.03 angstrom C5-C6 elongation from the neutral, while the first excited state distorts strongly around the carbonyl where its hole localizes - C2-O lengthening by 0.09 angstrom with N1-C2 and C2-N3 shortening by 0.07 and 0.08. Three crossings were located: the D3/D2 and D2/D1 intersections sit essentially at the Franck-Condon geometry, distorted by only 0.02 angstrom, reflecting an effective THREE-STATE near-degeneracy right at the point of ionisation; the D1/D0 intersection is far more distorted, mirroring the excited-state minimum. The decisive result is that the path from the first excited minimum to that lowest crossing is BARRIERLESS at XMS-CASPT2 but carries 'a sizeable energy barrier at CASSCF' - the correction converts a trapped excited state into an ultrafast one. Decay is therefore predicted to be prompt, and the ground state surface then funnels the population to the cationic ground-state minimum rather than toward fragmentation, which is the paper's explanation for the photostability of the ionised base.
Other: The headline finding is that dynamic correlation changes the mechanism, not merely the numbers, and the paper is built around demonstrating it. For the parent cation the decay from the first excited doublet minimum to the conical intersection with the ground state is BARRIERLESS at XMS-CASPT2 while 'presenting a sizeable energy barrier at CASSCF'; for the methylated derivative the corrected barrier is 0.03 electronvolts against 0.22 at CASSCF. In both cases the uncorrected surface would predict a trapped, long-lived excited state and the corrected one predicts ultrafast depopulation. Bare CASSCF is not a neutral reference here: for barrier heights on decay pathways it errs systematically toward too much barrier. A protocol the authors tried and threw away, with the failure mode named: 'additional computations on top of the CASSCF geometry optimisations employing the SS-CASPT2//CASSCF protocol were carried out but were discarded as the system presented strong differential correlation effects leading to the appearance of artificial crossings along the decay pathways, thus discouraging its use.' That is the single-state perturbative energy on multiconfigurational geometries, and here it manufactures conical intersections that do not exist: where differential correlation between states is strong, single-state corrections on a common geometry can produce spurious crossings. Four zeroth-order Hamiltonians are benchmarked and the spread is reported as a standard deviation. On identical geometries and an identical space, the four lowest vertical ionisation potentials come out at 7.62, 8.63, 8.67 and 9.08 electronvolts from CASSCF; 8.54, 9.06, 9.31 and 9.66 from single-state CASPT2; 8.61, 9.26, 9.44 and 9.79 from the multistate variant; and 8.82, 9.68, 9.77 and 10.14 from the extended multistate one. The authors average over the formulations and quote standard deviations of 0.16 to 0.28 electronvolts. The extended multistate values sit systematically 0.3 to 0.5 electronvolts above the single-state ones - a shift comparable to the differences between the electronic states being assigned. An empirical parameter is used outside the regime it was calibrated for, and the authors say so plainly. Both IPEA values of 0.0 and 0.25 atomic units were tested, and the paper notes that 'the IPEA shift described above was calibrated for the single-state formulation of CASPT2, 0.25 a.u. therefore being possibly a non-optimal value for correcting MS-/XMS-CASPT2 energies. We made use of this value due to its wide use in the literature ... and to roughly estimate its effect in its multistate formulations.' A shift parameter fitted for one variant of a method carries no guarantee for another variant of it, and the multistate formulations are noted to reach the experimental range already at zero shift, so applying the standard value may double-count. An imaginary level shift of 0.2 atomic units was used throughout to suppress intruder states. The space is specified in the exemplary form - requirement first, orbital list second - and is held fixed across charge states. It comprises 'the full pi valence occupied and virtual space PLUS the two occupied n lone pair orbitals to INCLUDE the 2n+ states', giving fourteen electrons in ten orbitals for the neutral and thirteen in the same ten for the cation. So the pi system enters by a rule that scales with the molecule, and the two lone pairs enter for a NAMED PURPOSE - to make two specific cationic states representable at all. Since the ionisation potentials are differences between neutral and cation, holding the orbital set fixed and changing only the occupancy is what makes those differences meaningful; this is the same discipline recorded for redox series elsewhere here. Five doublet states were state-averaged. The correction matters for energies but not for geometries, and the split is demonstrated rather than assumed. Comparing CASSCF against XMS-CASPT2 optimized structures, the excited-state minimum differs by bond shortenings of only 0.02 to 0.03 angstrom and the two sets are 'shown to be qualitatively [similar], validat[ing] the use of CASSCF as a potential cost-effective alternative' for structures. The authors are careful to note this does not generalize, citing prior work 'where XMS-CASPT2 geometries were shown to deviate more prominently from CASSCF estimates, particularly at conical intersections' - which is precisely where this study needs them. So the licence granted to CASSCF here is for geometries only, on this system, and the paper says as much. How much dynamic correlation matters varies between two nearly identical molecules treated with the same space: the authors 'conclude that dynamic electron correlation in 5-methyl-cytosine [plays a lesser role] compared to cytosine', the correction removing a barrier entirely in one case and reducing it from 0.22 to 0.03 electronvolts in the other. A single methyl group changes not the answer but the size of the correction needed to get it - which means a protocol validated on one member of a family is not automatically licensed for its close analogue. Finally, note what the multireference work does not supply: the connection to photostability is an argument from surface topography - 'the shape of the ground state potential energy surface strongly directs the decaying excited state population towards the cationic ground state minimum' - rather than from dynamics, since no trajectories were run. The 'ultrafast' timescale is inferred from barrierless topology and proximity of crossings to the Franck-Condon region, not computed. Basis ANO-L at valence double-zeta polarised quality; resolution of identity by Cholesky decomposition used for energies, analytical gradients and non-adiabatic couplings, with second nuclear derivatives taken numerically.

geometry_source: Full-valence iCASSCF geometry optimizations at n=2, 3, and 4 with 6-31G*, plus n=3/cc-pVTZ and conventional CASSCF comparisons. The attached six-atom XYZ is the exact SI iCASSCF(n=4)/6-31G* optimized Cartesian block.
method: incremental full-valence CASSCF (iCASSCF, 2-, 3-, and 4-body expansions); conventional full-valence CASSCF and RI-CASSCF benchmarks; RI-MP2 geometry comparison
software: development version of Q-Chem 5.0 for iCASSCF and RI-CASSCF; MOLPRO 2012.1 for conventional CASSCF
basis_set: 6-31G* and cc-pVTZ; RI auxiliary basis was RIMP2-VDZ or RIMP2-cc-pVTZ (the source does not map the auxiliary choice per row)
active_space_orbital_description: full valence space: every valence bonding orbital and an equal set of matching antibonding orbitals; localized bonding/antibonding pairs form the incremental bodies
active_space_protocol: Global CAS(12,12). Default bodies contain 2 electrons in 2 orbitals; tests also group the C=C sigma and pi bonding/antibonding pairs into one 4-electron/4-orbital body. iCASSCF n=2, n=3, grouped n=2/n=3, and n=4 are compared with full conventional CASSCF.

geometry_source: Room-temperature X-ray diffraction geometry used without reoptimisation for the CASSCF/CASPT2 work; for the CASSCF/NEVPT2 work the same structure with the PPh3 phenyl groups replaced by methyls
method: DKH2-CASSCF with CASPT2 and with NEVPT2; state-averaged CASSCF with SO-RASSI; MRCI; SINGLE_ANISO; Hartree-Fock and DFT (BP86, B3LYP, PBE0, BHandHLYP)
software: MOLCAS 8.0 (CASSCF/CASPT2, SO-RASSI, SINGLE_ANISO); ORCA 4.0.1 (CASSCF/NEVPT2, MRCI, HF and DFT)
basis_set: ANO-RCC-VDZ for the CASSCF/CASPT2 calculations; DKH-def2-TZVP with SARC-DKH-TZVP on rhenium for the CASSCF/NEVPT2, HF and DFT calculations
relativistic_treatment: All-electron treatment with the standard second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH2) Hamiltonian for scalar relativistic effects; spin-orbit coupling introduced by mixing state-averaged CASSCF spin multiplets through the SO-RASSI procedure
active_space_orbital_description: Five rhenium 5d orbitals plus four ligand MOs. The individual active orbitals are characterised: MOs 3 and 4 are the LUMOs of the two o-quinone ligands with negligible mixing into the Re d orbitals; the Re d(yz) and d(xz) orbitals mix strongly with oxo 2p/3p orbitals to give pi-type bonding MOs 1 and 2 and antibonding MOs 6 and 7, the antibonding pair carrying about 59-60% and the bonding pair about 51-64% oxygen 3p character; MO 5 is mainly d(xy) at about 63%
active_space_protocol: The active spaces are built as the five rhenium 5d orbitals plus a set of ligand orbitals, and the orbital composition of every active MO is shown and discussed, which is what lets the paper distinguish localized from delocalized valence states. Two independent correlated treatments are run on top of the same reference - CASPT2 in MOLCAS with ANO-RCC-VDZ on the experimental XRD geometry, and NEVPT2 in ORCA with DKH-def2-TZVP on a slightly modified geometry in which the PPh3 phenyl groups are replaced by methyls (P-CH3 set to the experimental P-C length of about 1.83 angstrom and C-H to 1.096 angstrom) - and the two agree to within 3-7%, which is the paper's main internal consistency check. For the spin-orbit treatment, state-averaged CASSCF was run over every state up to about 50000 cm-1 before SO-RASSI mixing. The limitation is that all calculations are single points on crystallographic geometries, so no geometry relaxation accompanies the changes in valence state being assigned.
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged CASSCF over 7 quintets, 27 triplets and 22 singlets, all states up to about 50000 cm-1, before SO-RASSI spin-orbit mixing
electronic_structure_description: Singlet ground state, dominated to about 90% by a single configuration in which the two o-quinone LUMOs (MOs 3 and 4), the two pi-bonding Re-O MOs (1 and 2) and the mainly d(xy) MO 5 are each doubly occupied. Both o-quinone LUMOs therefore hold an electron pair and the d-orbital occupations are close to 2, which is exactly the localized Re(V)-Cat2 valence state proposed from the crystal structure, and is consistent with the normal chemical shifts in the measured proton NMR spectrum. The first excited triplet lies 17730 cm-1 above the singlet at CASSCF level, 91% a single MO 5 to MO 6 excitation; dynamic correlation cuts this gap by more than half, to 7570 cm-1 at CASPT2 and 7350 cm-1 at NEVPT2 on the methyl-truncated structure. The lowest quintet is 97% a double excitation from MOs 1 and 2 into MOs 6 and 7 and is almost unaffected by dynamic correlation: 44400 cm-1 at CASSCF, 43890 at CASPT2 and 47150 at NEVPT2. LoProp atomic charges in the ground state: Re +1.75, Cat1 -1.33, Cat2 -1.23, oxo -0.48, PPh3 +0.29 - far from the formal oxidation states, which the authors attribute to ligand-to-metal pi donation, visible as substantial oxo p character in the doubly occupied bonding MOs 1 and 2.
Other: Spin-orbit coupling shifts the picture only slightly, in sharp contrast to lanthanide complexes: the ground spin-orbit state is a pseudo-singlet, 93% the SA-CASSCF ground singlet with about 5.2% admixture of first-triplet components. SINGLE_ANISO g tensors for the excited triplet states: 1.93, 1.89, 1.63 for the first and 1.76, 1.85, 2.26 for the second; zero-field splitting D = -157.9 cm-1 with E/D = -0.23 for the first triplet and D = 844.6 cm-1 with E/D = 0.13 for the second. MRCI predicts two ligand-to-metal charge transfer transitions at 218 and 283 nm with oscillator strengths 0.092 and 0.089 and a d-d transition at 850 nm with f = 0.002, against the measured spectrum with maxima (log epsilon) at 220 (3.36), 270 (3.43) and 647 (2.0) nm.
reference_short: A. A. Dmitriev, N. P. Gritsan, Int. J. Quantum Chem. 119, e26018 (2019)
notes: This complex is the clean localized case: a 90% single-configuration singlet with both dioxolene ligands fully reduced to catecholate, confirming the valence-state assignment made from the crystal structure. The one number that should be treated with care is the singlet-triplet gap, which dynamic correlation more than halves (17730 to about 7400 cm-1), while the singlet-quintet gap barely moves - so CASSCF alone would badly misplace the first excited state. The two correlated treatments agree within 3-7% despite using different basis sets, programs and a truncated PPh3, which is a reasonable robustness check. All results are single points on the crystallographic geometry.

active_space_protocol: The active spaces are built as the five rhenium 5d orbitals plus a set of ligand orbitals, and the orbital composition of every active MO is shown and discussed, which is what lets the paper distinguish localized from delocalized valence states. Two independent correlated treatments are run on top of the same reference - CASPT2 in MOLCAS with ANO-RCC-VDZ on the experimental XRD geometry, and NEVPT2 in ORCA with DKH-def2-TZVP on a slightly modified geometry in which the PPh3 phenyl groups are replaced by methyls (P-CH3 set to the experimental P-C length of about 1.83 angstrom and C-H to 1.096 angstrom) - and the two agree to within 3-7%, which is the paper's main internal consistency check. For the spin-orbit treatment, state-averaged CASSCF was run over every state up to about 50000 cm-1 before SO-RASSI mixing. The limitation is that all calculations are single points on crystallographic geometries, so no geometry relaxation accompanies the changes in valence state being assigned. For this complex two spaces of different size were used - CAS(12,10) with ANO-RCC-VDZ and CAS(6,9) with DKH-def2-TZVP - and they agree on the triplet ground state, which is the main qualitative claim, but they disagree on the ordering of the first two excited states, so the state ordering here is active-space dependent as well as correlation-dependent. Note that the running text and Table 2 twice write this space as CASSCF(10,12), inconsistently with the CASSCF(12,10) used elsewhere in the same paper.

electronic_structure_description: Triplet ground state, consistent with the paramagnetism inferred from the large chemical shifts in the measured proton NMR spectrum. Unlike complex 2, four configurations contribute significantly: all have MOs 1-4 doubly occupied, MOs 6 and 7 singly occupied and MOs 9 and 10 empty, and they differ in the occupation of the bonding/antibonding pair MO 5 and MO 8 - 64% with an electron pair in bonding MO 5 and MO 8 empty, about 15% with the pair in antibonding MO 8, and 7% and 5% for single alpha or beta excitation between them. Because the rhenium d AO and the o-quinone LUMO contribute about equally to both combinations, the quinone LUMO ends up holding about one electron in all four configurations, matching the empirical metrical oxidation state of 1.0 +/- 0.2 for the ligand - yet the spin density is concentrated on rhenium, making this a genuinely intermediate case rather than cleanly localized. State orderings: at CASSCF(12,10) the first excited state is a quintet at 3030 cm-1 with the singlet at 7120 cm-1; CASPT2 keeps the triplet ground state but swaps the order, singlet at 3840 and quintet at 6550 cm-1; CASSCF(6,9)/DKH-def2-TZVP on the truncated structure gives quintet 2550 and singlet 7290 cm-1; and NEVPT2 again swaps them, singlet 1908 and quintet 5513 cm-1. The quintet is 94% a single configuration with MOs 1-4 doubly occupied and MOs 5-8 each holding an alpha electron; the first singlet is 74% one configuration with MOs 1-6 doubly occupied plus 12% transfer of the pair from bonding MO 5 to antibonding MO 8. LoProp charges and Mulliken spin populations in the ground triplet: Re q = 1.51 and rho = 2.18, Diox q = -0.40 and rho = -0.35, averaged Cl q = -0.49 and rho about 0.06, PPh3 q = 0.36. In the excited quintet the spin distribution becomes fully consistent with a Re(IV)-SQ valence state.
Other: Spin-orbit coupling again only splits the multiplets slightly, leaving the ground pseudo-triplet and excited pseudo-quintet intact. SINGLE_ANISO g-tensor principal components: 2.00, 1.98, 1.95 for the pseudo-triplet and 1.97, 1.96, 1.95 for the pseudo-quintet; zero-field splitting D = 204.4 cm-1 with E/D = 0 for the ground triplet and D = 16.8 cm-1 with E/D = 0.11 for the pseudo-quintet. MRCI predicts transitions at 713 and 682 nm against the measured ligand-to-metal charge transfer band at 612 nm. The ground triplet resembles that of the related complex 1, [(3,5-di-tert-Bu2C6H2O2)ReCl3(OPPh3)], treated in earlier work at CASSCF(4,6): both localise spin density on rhenium (rho about 2.2) with moderate negative spin density on the dioxolene (about -0.36), but in complex 1 the quinone LUMO dominates the pi-bonding MO at about 75% with only 15% d(yz), and the Re d(yz) dominates the antibonding MO at about 71%, whereas in complex 3 the two contribute equally - so the delocalisation is greater here. Benchmarks against the CASPT2 reference show Hartree-Fock gives the correct level ordering but badly underestimates the singlet-triplet (3850 cm-1) and singlet-quintet (26400 cm-1) splittings, and the DFT results depend systematically on the fraction of exact exchange (BP86, B3LYP 20%, PBE0 25%, BHandHLYP 50%).
reference_short: A. A. Dmitriev, N. P. Gritsan, Int. J. Quantum Chem. 119, e26018 (2019)
notes: The more interesting of the two complexes, because the proposed localized Re(IV)-SQ assignment only partly survives: the dioxolene LUMO does carry about one electron, as the metrical oxidation state implies, but it does so through four configurations and an equal d/LUMO mixing in the bonding and antibonding pair, with the spin density sitting on rhenium. The ordering of the first two excited states is not settled by this work - CASSCF puts the quintet first, both CASPT2 and NEVPT2 put the singlet first, and the gap between them is only 1-4 thousand cm-1 - so the excited-state sequence should be taken as method-dependent. The printed active space is inconsistent between CASSCF(12,10) and CASSCF(10,12) within the same article.

formula: C2H4O, the adduct of triplet atomic oxygen with ethylene
point_group: C1 along the reaction paths; individual stationary points such as oxirane carry higher symmetry and their states are labelled accordingly, for instance the 1B1 transition
geometry_source: All geometry optimizations performed at the CASSCF level, with the reason for not going further stated precisely: 'CASPT2 optimizations using a CAS(12,12) active space was not possible with our computational resources', because although CASPT2 single points cost about the same as CASSCF ones, the energy gradients and derivative couplings do not. Reaction paths are followed by intrinsic reaction coordinate analysis where a transition state can be located.
method: State-averaged CASSCF with multi-state CASPT2 on top, applied across the whole reaction surface rather than at selected points, with CCSD(T) single points as an independent check. The parameters are disclosed and some are justified: a standard IPEA shift of 0.25 au, and a level shift of 0.3 au that was 'carefully chosen in order to avoid intruder states'. The Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian and Cholesky decomposition at a 1e-6 threshold are used throughout. Separate MS2-CASPT2 calculations are run for each multiplicity. Biradical character is quantified from the natural orbital occupation number of the LUMO-like orbital, which is itself identified by inspecting the CASSCF configurations to find the orbital each excitation targets.
software: OpenMolcas for all CASSCF and CASPT2 work; ORCA 4.1.2 for the CCSD(T) single points
basis_set: ANO-L-VTZ all-electron on oxygen and carbon with ANO-L-VDZ on hydrogen for the multireference work, chosen after testing: 'some tests with a larger basis set did not show any notable change in the energies', so the smaller combination was kept as 'a good compromise between accuracy and computational cost'. The CCSD(T) comparison uses aug-cc-pVTZ on all atoms.
relativistic_treatment: Douglas-Kroll-Hess Hamiltonian applied in all CASSCF and CASPT2 calculations; CASSCF wave functions also serve as the basis for a spin-orbit Hamiltonian, since the reaction proceeds by intersystem crossing
active_space_orbital_description: Twelve electrons in twelve orbitals, itemized in the text and chosen 'in view of the reactive scattering process, which mainly involves the O and C atoms, with C-C and C-O bond breaking and bond formation': the sigma/sigma-star and pi/pi-star pairs for the carbon-carbon bond, the 2s and all three 2p orbitals of oxygen, the pi orbital for the C-H bond, and the pair of virtual 3p(x) and 3s orbitals. The two Rydberg-like virtuals were added for a stated double purpose, 'to stabilize the active space and to recover some dynamic correlation'; 3p(x) proves 'essential to capture the C-H bond breaking' on three of the five channels, and 3p(z) is the acceptor orbital of the experimentally validated first singlet excitation.
active_space_protocol: A rule stated in terms of the jobs the space must do, and then checked at every point: the orbitals are chosen from the bonds that break and form in the scattering process, and 'the active space has been carefully checked after every single-point calculation to ensure the stability and reliability of the CASSCF wave function'. The design goal is consistency along the whole surface rather than accuracy at any one point, and the trade-off is spelled out: the authors 'opt toward identifying a stable and smoothly varying active space that is able to capture the majority of the reaction channels - about 70 percent - rather than adapting the active space to the various reaction channels, which would prevent from a straightforward application in on-the-fly dynamics'. State averaging over two states per multiplicity is justified twice, both because 'this number of states stabilizes the active space' and because only the lowest two singlets and triplets are energetically accessible in this collision.
multiplicities_studied: Singlet and triplet, two states of each - S0, S1, T1 and T2 are analysed at every stationary point, with separate state-averaged CASSCF and MS-CASPT2 runs per multiplicity
nroots_per_mult: Two roots per multiplicity, denoted SA2-CASSCF(12,12) and MS2-CASPT2
electronic_structure_description: A scattering reaction of atmospheric and interstellar relevance that proceeds on both singlet and triplet surfaces via intersystem crossing. The paper characterizes minima, transition structures and a conical intersection on the lowest singlet and triplet surfaces, analysing S0, S1, T1 and T2 at every geometry, and quantifies the biradical character of each from the occupation number of the LUMO-like natural orbital on a scale where 100 percent denotes a pure biradical. For oxirane, MS-CASPT2 places the first singlet excited state at 7.18 eV against a measured 7.24 eV, an error of 0.06 eV. The character of that state is contested: the multireference assigns it as a 1B1 transition from the oxygen 2p(x) lone pair into the virtual 3p(z) orbital, and this 'is in disagreement with the earlier TD-DFT calculations, using different functionals, at the same geometry, which predict a contribution from an s-like virtual orbital'. Along the reaction paths the active orbitals acquire 'atom-like' character at the later transition structures, reflecting the partial dissociation of the system.
Other: Consistency of the reference along the reaction paths is the stated design objective: the authors set out to identify 'an active space that changes smoothly along several reaction paths', and the space is 'carefully checked after every single-point calculation'. It fails on one channel while the energy profile still looks well behaved. Of the five reaction pathways the space handles four, but 'the same active space, however, rotates along pathway (5), and while the energy profiles look smooth, we cannot conclude on the reliability of this active space to describe correctly pathway (5)'. The authors decline to report it: 'therefore, we will not describe in detail this low-probability reaction pathway'. Rather than switch spaces per channel they keep one space covering about seventy percent of the reactive flux, because 'adapting the active space to the various reaction channels would prevent from a straightforward application in on-the-fly dynamics'. The space is also validated externally, with the licence limited in the same sentence: CCSD(T) single points on the CASSCF geometries lead the authors to conclude that 'the CASSCF/CASPT2 computational procedure and the chosen active space are accurate enough to describe the electronic structure of the system in the relevant regions visited along the reaction'.
reference_short: Talotta, Morisset, Rougeau, Lauvergnat & Agostini, J. Phys. Chem. A 2021, 125, 6075
notes: A dedicated electronic-structure study, five authors with two corresponding, explicitly framed as preparatory work for on-the-fly nonadiabatic dynamics rather than as an end in itself - 'the results presented in this work shall be intended as a preliminary study for dynamics on-the-fly simulations'. That framing accounts for the premium on a single smoothly varying space, the willingness to sacrifice one reaction channel, and the note that the chosen orbitals 'could also serve as the starting point' for larger spaces later. No trajectories are run here; the product is a validated protocol and a characterization of the stationary points and their multiconfigurational character. The one experimental comparison available, the oxirane first singlet excitation, is met to 0.06 eV. Earlier surface-hopping simulations by others on fitted surfaces with a spatially constant spin-orbit coupling, and crossed-molecular-beam branching ratios, are cited as context and are other groups' work, so they carry no rows. Only one chemical system is treated, so this is a single-row entry; its several stationary points and four electronic states belong to that one reaction surface. Spans oxirane, acetaldehyde, the transition structures connecting them and a singlet-triplet crossing, on the lowest two singlet and two triplet surfaces. Multi-state CASPT2 was run with a standard IPEA shift of 0.25 au and a level shift of 0.3 au chosen specifically against intruder states, separately for each multiplicity on the lowest two states. No bare-CASSCF versus CASPT2 comparison is tabulated in the passages examined, so the size of the correction is not directly readable; instead the corrected result is validated against an independent single-reference method, CCSD(T)/aug-cc-pVTZ single points on the CASSCF-optimized geometries computed in a different code 'to give further support to the MS-CASPT2 results'. An Arrhenius fit at high temperature gives U_eff = 582(13) K with tau_0 = 1.4(6)e-11 s, but linearity holds only to 30 K; fitting the whole range with QTM, direct, Raman and Orbach terms gives U_eff = 609(4) K with tau_0 = 6.6(6)e-12 s and a Raman contribution (C = 2.0(7.0)e-4 s-1 K-n, n = 3.6(1.1)). The computed U_cal is 606.3 K, consistent with experiment, and relaxation proceeds |-15/2> -> |-13/2> -> |-1/2> -> |+1/2> -> |+13/2> -> |+15/2>. Blocking temperature T_B = 8.2 K (at 2 K/min) and T_irr = 14.7 K, the lowest of the series. Applied dc fields have only a slight effect on the barrier, indicating QTM is effectively quenched by the high symmetry and strong axial crystal field. Stripping the halide counter-anions from the secondary coordination sphere (models 1a, 2a, 3a) raises the computed barrier from about 606-669 K to 1032-1116 K; removing the non-coordinating phosphonamide ligands instead while keeping the halides (models 1b, 2b, 3b) gives 794-898 K; removing both (models 1c, 2c, 3c) gives 1344-1407 K, roughly 2.1-2.2 times the parent values, with relaxation shifting from the first to the third excited Kramers doublet. And replacing the five equatorial waters by acetone or THF lowers the barrier to 491.4 and 427.1 K because the optimized structures lose axial linearity and equatorial planarity, whereas replacing them by H2S raises it to 1325.9 K through the smaller charge on sulfur - so the donor atom matters more than the bulk of the ligand. active_space_protocol: Unusually explicit for a dynamics paper. Five active spaces - (8,8), (8,9), (10,10) and (10,8) - were compared at both CASSCF and MRCIS with 6-31G* against the experimental S1 excitation energy of 3.71 eV: CASSCF gives 4.292 (8,8), 4.476 (8,9), 4.290 (10,10) and 4.406 eV (10,8), and MRCIS 4.168, 4.381, 4.168 and 4.286 eV, so enlarging the space does not move the excitation energy toward experiment and (8,8) is kept. The basis was tested the same way: 6-31+G* gives no improvement over 6-31G*, and product energies for the dissociation channels differ by at most 8.0 kcal/mol between the two, so 6-31G* is used. The number of averaged states was also justified rather than assumed: two-state averaging with equal weights is adopted because S2 lies about 51 kcal/mol above S1 in the Franck-Condon region, and a four-state average (S0-S3) along a representative trajectory confirms that S2 and S3 never approach S1 over the whole propagation. The CASSCF surfaces are then validated against MRCIS(8,8) single points both at the critical points of the mechanism (largest discrepancy 9.7 kcal/mol, at the trimethylene biradical) and along a complete trajectory. The one weakness the authors acknowledge is that CASSCF overestimates the excitation energy, which blue-shifts the simulated absorption maximum.

electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet ground state. TD-B3LYP/6-31G* places the same transition, mainly HOMO -> LUMO, at 3.95 eV. Two distinct S1/S0 conical intersection minima are located. In CI-I the intact C-N=N group lies out of the three-carbon plane, with C3-C4-C5-N1 at 62.0 degrees, N2-C3 stretched to 3.67 angstrom and N1-N2 at 1.185 angstrom; in CI-II the same group is coplanar with the carbon skeleton, C3-C4-C5-N1 at 177.0 degrees, N2-C3 at 4.807 angstrom and N1-N2 at 1.206 angstrom. The CI-I seam is much more steeply sloped than CI-II, and the interpolated S1 path from the Franck-Condon point is barrierless to CI-I but carries a barrier to CI-II, which the authors could not refine into a transition state.
Other: Dynamics: 363 trajectories propagated from S1 at 334 nm with a 2000 fs maximum propagation time and a 0.1 fs integration step, reduced to 0.05 fs where energy conservation demanded it; hopping decided by comparing the computed transition probability against a random number at each step. Four-fifths of the trajectories break one C-N bond promptly in S1 and then hop; the remaining fifth break it more slowly before hopping. Hopping times span 60-450 fs with a few out to 720 fs, and 78% of trajectories decay through CI-I against 22% through CI-II, matching the barrierless-versus-barriered interpolated paths. Hopping geometries separate cleanly: C3-C4-C5-N1 between -100 and 100 degrees with C3-N2 under 4 angstrom funnel to CI-I, while dihedrals near +/-180 degrees with C3-N2 beyond 4 angstrom correlate with CI-II. After the hop a second C-N bond breaks on S0 to give trimethylene biradical plus N2. Continuing the trajectories on S0 gives three secondary channels: cyclopropane + N2 at about 77.8% (barrierless ring closure), propene + N2 at about 12.5% through a [1,2]-hydrogen shift with a barrier of 17.8 kcal/mol at CASSCF(8,8) but only 4.8 kcal/mol at MRCIS(8,8), and CH2 + C2H4 + N2 at about 9.7%, endoergic by 30 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 27.6 kcal/mol at MRCIS relative to the biradical. multiplicities_studied: the multiplicities appropriate to the d configuration, state-averaged as set out in the paper's Table 1
nroots_per_mult: d8: 10 triplets and 15 singlets
electronic_structure_description: The highest magnetic anisotropy in the series: D = -382.945 cm-1 at CASSCF and -234.145 cm-1 at NEVPT2, far above the values for the chromium and manganese members and above what had been claimed as the maximum for this ligand family. The blocking barrier Ueff is 127 cm-1, so the complex has strong potential as a single-ion magnet. The D_zz axis superimposes on the C3 axis. The AIM analysis shows non-covalent interactions between the methyl hydrogens to be prevalent, and EDA-NOCV shows the amide ligand bonding to the metal through both sigma and pi interactions with a substantial dispersion contribution.
Other: A minimal 3d-only space carried across an entire first-row series, which is what makes the comparison between metals meaningful - the differences in D are differences in d configuration and ligand field, not in the correlation treatment. The state averaging is the part that varies, scaled per configuration up to 100 roots for d5, so that high-lying states feed into the spin-Hamiltonian parameters. Note that CASSCF and NEVPT2 disagree by very different amounts across the series - by under a wavenumber for the manganese(III) complex and by 150 cm-1 for the nickel(II) one - so the size of the dynamic correlation correction is not transferable even within one ligand set.
