compound_name: Michler's hydrol blue (HB), a monomethine cyanine / diarylmethane dye - charge/bond-resonance diabatic analysis
geometry_source: ground-state minimum geometry from MP2/cc-pVDZ
method: canonical-ensemble SA-CASSCF (a new strategy: the state-averaging weights are a self-consistent Boltzmann distribution parametrized by an effective electronic 'temperature'/Lagrange multiplier on the energy) with a complete-active-space valence-bond (CASVB) diabatic decomposition; weights equilibrated iteratively over electronic temperatures spanning the visible (1.5-3.5 eV)
active_space_orbital_description: the four pi electrons in three p orbitals of the cyanine chromophore (rings and methine bridge), Boys-localized for the valence-bond labeling
active_space_protocol: CAS(4,3) - four active electrons in three orbitals - identified as the minimal complete quantum many-body model for coherent transport of an excess charge plus a covalent bond-pair (Moffitt's formamidinium-cation picture of cyanine dyes). Four electrons in three orbitals generate six singlet CSFs. The paper's methodological point: an ordinary microcanonical (uniform-weight) SA-CASSCF cannot self-consistently resolve all six CSF energies/couplings for this 'more diabatic than adiabatic' problem (the solution does not persist beyond 3 states), whereas the proposed canonical-ensemble SA-CASSCF puts weight self-consistently on the full 6-dimensional CAS-CI Hilbert space, enabling the complete diabatic decomposition - a strategy for including more adiabatic states in the ensemble without convergence collapse.
nroots_per_mult: full 6-CSF CAS-CI Hilbert space (canonical ensemble)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0
Other: The CASVB decomposition resolves the charge/bond-resonance of the dye into two chemically distinct superexchange channels through symmetric 'bridge' CSFs (labeled 121 and 202): both couple strongly to the polarized covalent CSFs 211 and 112, producing the visible charge/bond-resonance absorption band at second order. The two bridge states are quasi-degenerate and weakly coupled; the bonding channel has the larger energy dispersion. Both contribute to S2/S3 (not S1 by symmetry, nor S4); the ionic bridge state 202 contributes significantly to the ground state. Michler's hydrol blue is an important reference cyanine and an amyloid-sensitive fluorogenic stain.
reference_short: Canonical-ensemble SA-CASSCF strategy for problems with more diabatic than adiabatic states, arXiv:1407.6063
notes: Metal-free organic dye (metal_center = none). Recorded because, although it is primarily an SA-CASSCF methodology paper, it applies a concrete CAS(4,3) to a real molecule (Michler's hydrol blue) with a genuine diabatic/CASVB result, and because the canonical-ensemble SA-CASSCF idea - self-consistent Boltzmann state-averaging weights that let the full CAS-CI space be resolved - is a transferable strategy for diabatic/multi-state active-space problems.

relativistic_treatment: Scalar relativistic correction from the third-order Douglas-Kroll Hamiltonian (DKH3), taken as the difference between aug-cc-pV5Z-DK with DKH3 and aug-cc-pV5Z without it at icMRCI level; spin-orbit coupling from the state-interaction method with the Breit-Pauli Hamiltonian at icMRCI level with the all-electron cc-pCV5Z basis, the bra and ket states assigned by MOLPRO with no manual adjustment. Ground-state frequencies computed at the same B3LYP level in Gaussian
method: CASSCF geometry optimization of the lowest excited states, with CASPT2 used in the authors' earlier work for the vertical transition energies. Vibrations activated by the electronic transition are identified by projecting the calculated excited-state atomic displacements onto the ground-state normal-mode vectors. The barrier for nitrogen migration through the vacancy is evaluated separately at TD-B3LYP
software: MOLPRO for the CASSCF; Gaussian for the B3LYP geometries and frequencies
basis_set: B2, which is the B1 set (6-31+G* on the atoms of the first shell around the vacancy, 6-31G* on the second shell, 6-31G on the rest) augmented by diffuse s functions with the 6-31+G exponent on the second-shell atoms
active_space_orbital_description: Two spaces, (8,11) and (4,11), eight or four electrons in eleven active molecular orbitals. The (8,11) space covers orbitals with occupation numbers from 1.98 down to 0.002. The (4,11) space covers only the occupied MOs built from the broken bonds of the vacancy-related carbon atoms, together with empty MOs down to occupation 0.0001.
active_space_protocol: the active window is positioned on the occupation-number spectrum rather than by orbital count: shifting it down by several MOs pulls the N-C and C-C bonds around the vacancy into the space in non-equivalent amounts and does not improve the result, so both spaces are anchored on the vacancy-related non-bonding orbitals. Both were established as the most suitable for this excited state in the authors' earlier study
electronic_structure_description: The ground state is 3A2 and the first triplet excited state 3E. The transition involves only the non-bonding electrons of the vacancy-related carbon atoms; the electrons in the C-C and N-C bonds do not participate, which is why excitation cannot be expected to lower the nitrogen-migration barrier appreciably. The zero-phonon line is observed at 1.945 eV with a photoluminescence progression spaced by about 0.07 eV; the computed activated frequencies come out around 600 cm-1. The ground-state barrier for N migration through the vacancy is about 5 eV and no significant reduction of it is found on excitation, which argues against the nitrogen-tunnelling explanation of the doublet splitting in the absorption band.
Other: The two spaces are a deliberate pair rather than a refinement of one another - (8,11) reaches down to orbitals with occupation 1.98, (4,11) keeps only the broken-bond orbitals of the vacancy carbons and their empty partners - and the selection criterion is stated in terms of occupation numbers and of which bonds would enter the space if the window moved. That the same eleven orbitals serve with either four or eight electrons is the practical point: the states of interest live entirely in the dangling-bond manifold, so the additional four electrons buy correlation rather than new physics. Only the C19NVH28 cluster could be used for the excited states at all, on computer-time grounds, so the size of the model rather than the space is the binding constraint here.

The first excited state is defined here as the first state above the two 1 2A' and 1 2A'' components of 1 2E, and reproducing its excitation energy and wave function requires selecting from the initial CASSCF the state involving electron transfer from the two highest doubly occupied orbitals HOMO-1 and HOMO into the SOMO

active_space_protocol: chosen against a failure mode rather than for completeness. A larger basis with more diffuse functions produces a dense set of states involving transitions to diffuse orbitals, which crowds out the state of interest; the space is limited to (9,6) and the diffuse functions restricted to the vacancy-related atoms specifically to keep the required state available in the CASSCF calculation

The resulting CASPT2 wave function for the first excited 1 2A2 state is genuinely multireference, its largest coefficient of about 0.7 corresponding to the 3 2A'' state of the CASSCF wave function - which is why the geometry relaxation was evaluated by optimizing 3 2A'' at CASSCF(9,6). The relaxed geometry breaks C3v symmetry, one vacancy-related carbon moving away from the vacancy, and since the two components of 1 2E should be roughly equally populated the mean geometry in that state is expected to look C3v.

The physically wanted state - HOMO-1/HOMO to SOMO - is not among the low CASSCF roots when diffuse functions let Rydberg-like states intrude, so the authors restrict both the space and the diffuse set until it reappears, then take the CASSCF root that carries the largest weight in the CASPT2 wave function as the one to optimize. method: CASSCF relocation of every stationary point starting from B3LYP/cc-pVDZ geometries, with vibrational frequencies computed for all of them; then internally contracted multireference configuration interaction including all single and double excitations relative to a reduced reference, with a Davidson correction. Only the singlet surface was considered. Both approach modes were followed - the oxygen end of NO attacking the CH carbon, and the nitrogen end attacking it.
software: MOLPRO and DALTON for the multireference calculations; Gaussian 98 for the B3LYP starting geometries
basis_set: cc-pVDZ and aug-cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF work; cc-pVDZ for the multireference CI
active_space_orbital_description: twelve electrons in eleven orbitals, defined by exclusion: everything except the 1s orbitals of carbon, nitrogen and oxygen and the 2s orbitals of nitrogen and oxygen. For the multireference CI the reference had to be reduced to ten electrons in ten orbitals, because CI on the twelve-electron reference was not feasible.
active_space_protocol: (12,11) full valence minus the C, N and O 1s orbitals and the N and O 2s orbitals, used for all geometry optimizations and frequencies; (10,10) as the reduced reference for the internally contracted multireference CI, chosen for feasibility rather than on physical grounds
electronic_structure_description: Relative energies in kcal/mol from separated CH(2Pi) plus NO(2Pi), given as CASSCF(12,11)/cc-pVDZ, CASSCF(12,11)/aug-cc-pVTZ, MRCI/cc-pVDZ and MRCI with the Davidson correction. Intermediates: A -4.75, -6.67, -10.83, -11.26; B -17.90, -21.19, -24.13, -26.93; C -93.23, -95.61, -98.88, -99.15; D -155.69, -159.28, -156.95, -158.69; E -177.38, -182.37, -180.39, -181.20; F -95.36, -99.44, -98.10, -100.89; G -71.97, -75.37, -77.33, -78.20; H -110.74, -115.83, -111.27, -112.38. Asymptotes: H + c-NOC -1.43, 0.70, 2.20, 2.26; N(4S) + HCO 11.39, 9.62, 13.88, 15.27; H + CNO -13.55, -14.43, -11.71, -13.05; O(1D) + HNC -18.11, -20.16, -19.05, -10.96; O(1D) + HCN -36.67, -35.64, -35.58, -26.68. The two entrance transition states TS1 and TS2 sit at 9.10 and 8.77 kcal/mol above the reactants at CASSCF but go NEGATIVE at the correlated level, -2.51 and -1.79 and, with the Davidson correction, -5.70 and -5.18, so the barriers that CASSCF predicts vanish once dynamic correlation is added. The formation of intermediates A and B from the reactants is therefore essentially barrierless, as is the further conversion to C. The main products are H + NCO and NH + CO when the oxygen end of NO attacks the carbon; when the nitrogen end attacks, the reaction is expected to stop at fulminic acid.
Other: Two active-space observations here, and one of them is the paper's most consequential result. First, the space is defined by EXCLUSION rather than by construction: everything is active except the three 1s core orbitals and the nitrogen and oxygen 2s orbitals, giving twelve electrons in eleven orbitals. That is a clean recipe for a small reactive system and it makes the space transferable across every stationary point of a complicated multi-channel surface without re-selection. Second, and inevitably, the CI could not be run on that reference: the authors state flatly that multireference CI with the twelve-electron reference is not feasible and reduce it to ten electrons in ten orbitals for that step. So the geometries come from one space and the energies from a smaller one, and the reduction was made for cost rather than physics. The consequence is visible in the entrance channel and it changes the chemistry: at CASSCF(12,11) the two transition states leading to the first intermediates lie about 9 kcal/mol ABOVE the reactants, whereas at the correlated level they lie 2 to 6 kcal/mol BELOW them. A CASSCF-only reading of this surface would predict an activation barrier for a reaction that is in fact barrierless. Anyone using CASSCF stationary-point energies for radical-radical addition should expect exactly this sign of error. A reassuring result on the other axis: enlarging the basis from cc-pVDZ to aug-cc-pVTZ at fixed active space changes the geometries by under 0.04 A and 4 degrees.
notes: This is a metal-free system, so metal_center, metal_ox_state, d_electron_count and ligand_set are left empty. The formula CHNO is that of the reacting complex and of all its isomers; the individual intermediates are labelled A through H in the paper and are not all identified by chemical name in the extracted text, so the row covers the surface as a whole. Only singlet surfaces were computed, although the reactants CH and NO are both doublets and one product asymptote involves quartet nitrogen. Relative energies are electronic energies without zero-point correction.

electronic_structure_description: The mapped states are X 1A1-prime, A 1A2-double-prime, and a 3A2-double-prime ammonia, with higher B 1E-double-prime and b 3E-double-prime states entering conical-intersection correlations. On the constrained planar C2v ground-state NH+H2 path, a 68,500 cm^-1 barrier occurs at r(NH)=2.0, NH-to-H2 center=2.9, and r(HH)=1.6 bohr relative to equilibrium NH3; the A singlet and a triplet cuts have no analogous barrier. The A state primarily dissociates to NH2(X 2B1)+H, whereas the a triplet preferentially reaches NH(X 3Sigma-)+H2(X 1Sigma-g+).
Other: The X/A/B singlet surfaces and a/b triplet surfaces form common conical intersections under symmetry reduction, providing vibronic-coupling channels. Product correlations depend strongly on whether C2v, Cs with a bisecting plane, or coplanar Cs symmetry is enforced; lowering symmetry can remove avoided-crossing barriers. At large H-H separation, NH+H+H channels can become more favorable than NH+H2. The CASSCF treatment recovers only about 30-40% of valence correlation, and the authors report typical excitation/dissociation-energy errors of 0.1-0.5 eV; the surfaces are partial planar cuts rather than global six-dimensional PESs.

compound_name: Ni(C2H4)2 — bis(ethylene)nickel(0), D2d / C2v(planar) / C2v(bent) / D2h critical points
point_group: D2d (minimum), C2v(planar), C2v(bent) and D2h — four symmetry-distinct critical points on the same surface
geometry_source: CASSCF gradient optimization of each structure with the (14,10) space; CASPT2 single points at those CASSCF-optimized geometries. DFT (LSD/DZVP, and LANL2DZ ECP) optimizations performed for comparison with B3LYP, BLYP and BP86.
method: CASSCF geometry optimization with CASPT2 single points (Andersson et al. multireference perturbation approach)
basis_set: Atomic natural orbital (ANO) basis of Bauschlicher et al. for nickel and Dunning cc-pVDZ for carbon and hydrogen: primitives (Ni 20s15p10d6f), (C 7s6p4d2f), (H 4s1p) contracted to [Ni 7s6p4d2f], [C 3s2p1d], [H 2s1p)
active_space_orbital_description: (14,10) for the CASSCF geometry optimizations: the pi and pi* orbitals of the two ethylene moieties plus the 4s and 3d orbitals of the nickel atom — all the orbitals required to describe the forming Ni-C bonds and the low-lying states of the metal atom. The space is ENLARGED for the CASPT2 single points by adding a correlating 4d orbital for each doubly occupied 3d orbital not taking part in the bonding, following Pierloot, Persson and Roos: this gives 14 electrons in 12 orbitals for the D2d, C2v(planar) and C2v(bent) structures and 14 electrons in 13 orbitals for the D2h structure.
active_space_protocol: Two-stage: a (14,10) space carries the geometry optimizations, then the space is extended with 3d-correlating 4d orbitals for the single-point CASPT2 energies. The number of added 4d orbitals is structure-dependent, because it is set by how many 3d orbitals remain doubly occupied and non-bonding in each symmetry — hence (14,12) for three structures and (14,13) for D2h. The adequacy criterion is stated numerically: with this extended space "the perturbation contributions are all smaller than 1.0 kcal/mol".
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet d10 nickel(0) complex. Four critical points, with relative energies in kcal/mol at CASSCF and (in the CASPT2 column E(2)) at CASPT2: D2d 0.00 / 0.00, C2v(planar) 6.89 / 5.07, C2v(bent) 18.05 / 17.31, D2h 36.56 / 18.96. Absolute energies of the D2d structure are -1663.01454 (CASSCF) and -1664.27375 (CASPT2) hartree. D2d is the only genuine minimum (all real frequencies); C2v(planar) is a saddle point of index 1 connecting two equivalent D2d structures, C2v(bent) has index 2 and D2h index 3. Geometrical parameters are barely affected by structure: Ni-C distances 2.021 A (D2d) lengthening to 2.121 A (D2h), C=C 1.399 A (D2d) shortening to 1.373 A (D2h), and the ethylene pyramidalization angle epsilon 18.8 deg in D2d, 18.5/20.2 deg in C2v(planar), 18.7 deg in C2v(bent), falling to 11.6 deg in the planar D2h form.
Other: A textbook double-shell case with a structure-dependent twist. The (14,10) space that suffices for geometries does not suffice for energies: for every 3d orbital that stays doubly occupied and out of the bonding, a correlating 4d orbital must be added for the CASPT2 step (the Pierloot-Persson-Roos prescription), and because the count of such orbitals depends on symmetry the extended space is (14,12) for D2d, C2v(planar) and C2v(bent) but (14,13) for D2h. The payoff is quantified — with the extended space "the perturbation contributions are all smaller than 1.0 kcal/mol" — and the effect on the answer is highly non-uniform: adding dynamic correlation barely moves the D2d-C2v(planar) and D2d-C2v(bent) gaps (6.89 -> 5.07 and 18.05 -> 17.31 kcal/mol) but nearly HALVES the D2d-D2h gap, from 36.56 to 18.96 kcal/mol. So a (14,10) CASSCF number for the planar D2h form is wrong by 17.6 kcal/mol, while the same space is good to ~2 kcal/mol for the other two — the structure needing the extra 4d orbital is exactly the one whose energy is most wrong without it. The topology of the surface nonetheless survives: the energetic ORDER of the four critical points is unchanged by correlation, only the gaps move. active_space_orbital_description: (8,8): the four sigma and pi bonding orbitals involved in the rearrangement together with their four antibonding counterparts.
active_space_protocol: A single (8,8) space of four bonding and four antibonding orbitals is used for every stationary point on the surface, so reactant, both transition structures, the diradical intermediate and the product are directly comparable. The paper notes explicitly that structures 10, 11 and the diradical intermediate 12 were optimized "with the correct active space orbitals in each case", i.e. orbital identity was verified rather than assumed at each optimization. Dynamic correlation enters as (8,8)CASPT2 single points at all stationary points, and reported enthalpy differences are zero-point corrected using the CASSCF numerical frequencies.
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell singlet reactant of the conformationally restricted allenyl Cope rearrangement, optimized as an energy minimum at (8,8)CASSCF/6-31G* with the correct active space orbitals. It rearranges to triene 11 through either of two transition structures — 13 and 15 — which differ by 2.1 kcal/mol in zero-point-corrected enthalpy and both lead to the common diradical intermediate 12. Passing through the lower-energy structure 13, the terminal methylene group rotates in only one direction, whereas through 15 it appears free to rotate either way; this asymmetry is consistent with the 90% stereoselectivity observed in the thermal rearrangements of the dimethyl derivatives. A separate structure lies 32.7 kcal/mol above 10 with a large associated H term.
Other: A uniform (8,8) space of four bonding and four antibonding orbitals across every stationary point, which is what allows a two-transition-state mechanism to be established at all — the two structures 13 and 15 differ by only 2.1 kcal/mol in zero-point-corrected enthalpy, a margin that would be meaningless if the two had been computed in differently composed spaces. The paper also records that the reactant, product and diradical intermediate were optimized "with the correct active space orbitals in each case", i.e. orbital identity was checked at each optimization rather than assumed to persist — the failure mode being that an (8,8) optimization can converge onto a different set of eight orbitals at a distant geometry and silently break the comparison. The mechanistic conclusion depends on dynamic correlation being added on top: an earlier study at CASSCF level alone gave a different picture for the parent system, and it was "the inclusion of dynamic electron correlation at the (8,8)CASPT2/6-31G* level" that located allylic-stabilized structures and changed the pathway. The result here — two separate transition structures both leading to a common diradical intermediate — differs substantially from the parent 1,2,6-heptatriene rearrangement, which has a single transition structure that either proceeds to the diradical or bypasses it entirely. That contrast between a conformationally restricted system and its flexible parent, computed with the same space and the same correction, is the paper's central point.

notes: Computational study of the conformationally restricted allenyl Cope rearrangement of syn-7-allenylnorbornene (10) to triene 11, undertaken to explain stereoselectivity observed experimentally in the thermal Cope rearrangements of dimethyl allenylnorbornene derivatives. The terminal methylene group rotates in only one direction through the lower-energy transition structure 13 but appears to rotate freely in either direction through 15, a finding described as remarkably consistent with the 90% stereoselectivity observed experimentally. Direct participation of the terminal allenyl pi bond is also addressed. compound_name: Pyrene radical cation (Py+) — photostability via sloped conical intersections
point_group: D2h for all CASSCF geometry optimizations, matching the planar-constrained MMVB structures
geometry_source: CASSCF geometry optimizations within D2h symmetry for the D0, D1 and D2 minima. Conical intersections optimized at CASSCF in a REDUCED (13e,14o) active space, with full (15e,16o) CASSCF energies then computed at the resulting crossing structures. CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF geometries. MMVB structures optimized with planar constraints.
method: CASSCF and CASPT2 as benchmarks for a hybrid QM/MM molecular mechanics-valence bond (MMVB) force field, for which an analytical energy gradient for cations was implemented in this work
basis_set: 6-31G*, including polarization d functions on the carbon atoms
active_space_orbital_description: The FULL pi active space: 15 pi electrons distributed in 16 valence pi orbitals. A reduced (13e,14o) space is used for conical intersection optimization and as the CASPT2 reference.
active_space_protocol: Three distinct uses of two spaces, each forced by a stated computational limit. The full (15e,16o) pi space is used for minima and for single-point energies, and the paper quantifies why it cannot be used everywhere: 'CASSCF presently has a practical limit of around 10^7 configuration state functions (e.g., Py+ with 15 electrons in 16 active orbitals and D2h point group symmetry)' — this molecule sits AT that limit. Conical intersections therefore had to be optimized in a reduced (13e,14o) space 'as computationally expensive orbital state-averaging procedures are required for such calculations', with full-space energies recomputed at the resulting geometries. For CASPT2 'we also had to reduce the reference space to (13e,14o), keeping the CASSCF optimized orbitals frozen with the (15e,16o) active space' — so the CASPT2 reference orbitals come from the large space while the reference configurations come from the small one. The choice of a multiconfigurational method is argued from first principles: the one-electron approximation 'is unreliable, because so many problems involve interaction of many configurations', and CASSCF 'fully accounts for configuration interactions within a pi-electron system'.
nroots_per_mult: 3 (D0, D1, D2); state averaging required for the conical intersection optimizations
electronic_structure_description: Vertical excitation energies in kcal/mol as CASSCF / CASPT2 / MMVB: D1 at 22.9 / 23.7 / 21.5; D2 at 39.9 / 36.2 / 47.0, against an experimental D2 value of about 36 kcal/mol. At the D1 minimum the D0-D1 energy gap is 7.4 kcal/mol at CASSCF and 11.9 at CASPT2 (1.9 at MMVB). The D0/D1 conical intersection lies 1.9 kcal/mol above the D1 minimum at CASSCF (0.1 at MMVB). The D1/D2 conical intersection lies 8.1 kcal/mol above the D2 minimum at CASSCF and 7.9 at MMVB. Both conical intersections are SLOPED, with parallel gradients on the upper and lower states and equivalent gradient difference vectors at CASSCF and MMVB. Root-mean-square deviations of MMVB from CASSCF bond lengths over six distinct bonds are 0.006, 0.009 and 0.011 A for the D0, D1 and D2 minima (maximum errors under 0.01, 0.015 and 0.02 A), 0.010 A for the D0/D1 CI (maximum 0.015 A) and 0.017 A for the D1/D2 CI (maximum 0.030 A). The mechanism proposed is photoexcitation to an absorbing Dn state, rapid decay to D1 consistent with Kasha's rule, then ultrafast nonradiative decay to D0 at an easily accessible sloped D0/D1 conical intersection — accounting for the observed photostability.
Other: The most important caveat is one the authors state against their own conical intersections: 'at the CASSCF D0/D1 CI and D1/D2 CI optimized geometries, the two respective electronic states split by over 6 kcal/mol at the CASPT2 level, indicating that differential dynamic electron correlation is not negligible. We therefore do not know the real crossing energy and geometry at the CASPT2 level.' The crossings were located where the CASSCF space makes two states degenerate, and adding dynamic correlation lifts that degeneracy by more than 6 kcal/mol — so these are CASSCF crossing points, not true conical intersections of the correlated surface, and the paper says the same effect was seen for the naphthalene cation. It cannot be fixed here because CASPT2 geometry optimization is not available at this size. The second point concerns how the reduced space is used: conical intersections need state averaging, which is expensive enough that the space had to drop from (15e,16o) to (13e,14o) for those optimizations, and the CASPT2 reference is a hybrid — orbitals frozen from the large-space CASSCF, configurations from the small space. That is a defensible compromise but means the CASPT2 energies do not correspond to any single self-consistent active space. Finally, pyrene sits exactly at the stated practical CASSCF ceiling of about 10^7 configuration state functions even with D2h symmetry, so this molecule marks the size boundary for full-pi treatment of PAH radical cations — which is the whole motivation for benchmarking the cheaper MMVB force field against it.
reference_short: Tokmachev, Boggio-Pasqua, Bearpark et al., J. Phys. Chem. A 2008, 112, 10881
notes: MMVB is a hybrid QM/MM method parameterized to reproduce CASSCF calculations, not experimental or CASPT2 results — a point the authors make explicitly before comparing. Its analytical energy gradient for cations was implemented for this work. MMVB reproduces the CASSCF geometries well (RMS deviations 0.006-0.017 A) and the sloped topology of both conical intersections, but overestimates the D1-D2 gap: its D2 vertical excitation of 47.0 kcal/mol against an experimental 36, which is the origin of its larger error in the D1/D2 CI geometry. It also brings the D0/D1 CI too close to the D1 minimum (0.1 against 1.9 kcal/mol). A previous study of the naphthalene radical cation had shown that CASSCF alone cannot be completely adequate and that CASPT2 may be needed to reproduce experimental excited states. Absolute CASSCF and CASPT2 energies are in Tables S3 and S4; CASSCF bond lengths in Table 1. The CASSCF derivative coupling vector was not computed. correlation_correction: CASPT2 single points at the CASSCF-optimized geometries, using a reduced (13e,14o) reference space with the CASSCF orbitals from the full (15e,16o) space held frozen.

CAS(6,6) NN-bond test includes NN sigma, NO sigma, and NO pi bonding/antibonding orbitals.

electronic_structure_description: Nonplanar NH2 and NO approach forms pyramidal N-nitrosamide NH2NO. A concerted 1,3-H shift transfers an NH bond pair to OH while an O lone pair becomes an N lone pair, yielding HNNOH. Low NO-bond rotation and NN inversion interconvert trans/cis isomers before a rectangular H-N-N-O saddle leads to closed-shell N2+H2O. Any HNNOH isomer can instead dissociate without an additional barrier to spin-coupled HN2+OH.

compound_name: Glyoxal (S1) with argon — collision-induced intersystem crossing
point_group: C2h (planar in the S0, S1 and T1 states)
geometry_source: Geometries of the S0, S1 and T1 states optimized with the eight-in-six CASSCF method, with zero-point energies from the same level. For the interaction calculations the glyoxal geometry was FIXED at the isolated-molecule S1 optimized structure, since the region of interest is where the interaction energy is sufficiently low. Roughly 150 points were sampled over a quarter sphere by symmetry: r from 3.0 to 6.0 A in 0.5 A steps, theta from 0 to 90 degrees and phi from -90 to 90 degrees, both in 30 degree steps.
method: CASSCF with multireference configuration interaction (MRCI) including Davidson and Pople corrections; full CI within the same active space for the T1 interaction energies; Breit-Pauli spin-orbit interaction calculations on the resulting CI wave functions
basis_set: Gaussian basis sets of double-zeta plus polarization quality: Dunning-Raffenetti [9s5p1d/3s2p1d]/(3s1p/2s1p) for glyoxal and [12s8p/5s3p] for the argon atom
active_space_orbital_description: Eight electrons in six orbitals. The individual orbitals are not itemized in the text.
active_space_protocol: A single eight-in-six CASSCF space is used for the geometries, frequencies and vibrational basis sets of both the S1 and T1 states. For the glyoxal-argon interaction energies the S1 orbitals were computed at this level and then a FULL CI was carried out within the same active space to obtain the T1 interaction energies — the paper notes 'the results for S1 by the full-CI calculations are identical as those by the eight-in-six CASSCF', so the full CI is exact within the space and serves to put both spin states on precisely the same orbital footing. The resulting CI wave functions for S1 and T1 were used directly in the spin-orbit interaction calculations. Separately, MRCI with Davidson or Pople corrections was used to improve the S0/S1/T1 energy differences.
electronic_structure_description: Optimized geometries (bond lengths in angstroms, angles in degrees), calculated then experimental: S0 r(C-H) 1.088 vs 1.132, r(C-C) 1.508 vs 1.526, r(C-O) 1.208 vs 1.212, angle CCH 116.2 vs 112.2, angle CCO 121.1 vs 121.2; S1 r(C-H) 1.077 vs 1.115, r(C-C) 1.419 vs 1.460, r(C-O) 1.281 vs 1.252, angle CCH 121.1 vs 114.0, angle CCO 120.4 vs 123.7; T1 r(C-H) 1.076, r(C-C) 1.435, r(C-O) 1.265, angle CCH 120.9, angle CCO 119.8. Adiabatic energy differences including zero-point corrections in kcal/mol (CASSCF, MRCI, MRCI+Davidson, MRCI+Pople, experiment): E(S1)-E(S0) 79.79, 74.05, 70.49, 70.07, 62.8; E(T1)-E(S0) 73.69, 65.64, 61.68, 61.83, 54.9; E(S1)-E(T1) 6.10, 8.41, 8.82, 8.24, 7.9. CASSCF overestimates the adiabatic excitation energies to S1 and T1 while underestimating the S1-T1 gap; MRCI improves both because the dynamical correlation lowers S1 and T1 more than S0. The MRCI+Pople S1-T1 gap of 8.24 kcal/mol agrees excellently with the experimental 7.9 and was adopted for the dynamics. The T1 optimized geometry is very close to that of S1, so intersystem crossing is intrinsically slow because the Franck-Condon factors between the initial S1 vibrational state and the numerous isoenergetic T1 vibrational states are small. Normal mode frequencies agree with experiment in the low-frequency region but differ substantially at high frequency, with the C=O stretching (bu) mode particularly discrepant. A lifetime of 5.3 ps is quoted for a state at a given energy in the collision dynamics analysis.
Other: This paper records a specific pathology of excited-state CASSCF: symmetry breaking. The discrepancy between calculated and experimental S1 geometries is 'attributed to the instability problem, i.e., the symmetry-broken solutions with a lower symmetry than the C2h nuclear framework exist in the CASSCF wave functions for the excited states. It seems that the excited-state CASSCF wave function overemphasizes the O-C=C-O resonance structure.' The consequence propagates into the vibrational analysis — the C=O stretching bu mode is singled out as badly wrong and explicitly linked back to the same symmetry-breaking problem — and matters here because those frequencies build the vibrational basis sets for the collision dynamics. An eight-in-six space is not large enough to prevent one resonance structure dominating the excited-state wave function. The energetics show the complementary limitation: CASSCF overestimates both excitation energies by 17-19 kcal/mol and simultaneously UNDERestimates the S1-T1 gap (6.10 against 7.9 experimental), because dynamic correlation stabilizes the two excited states more than the ground state. MRCI with the Pople correction repairs the gap to 8.24 kcal/mol but leaves the absolute excitation energies still 7 kcal/mol high. A neat methodological detail worth carrying: the T1 interaction energies were obtained by full CI within the same active space using the S1 orbitals, and the authors verify that this reproduces the CASSCF S1 result exactly — so both spin states are described in an identical orbital basis, which is what makes the computed spin-orbit matrix elements between them meaningful.
reference_short: Nakajima & Kato, J. Phys. Chem. A 2001, 105, 10657
notes: The study computes cross sections for the S1 to T1 transition in glyoxal induced by collision with argon, combining the interaction potential with the spin-orbit interaction. Vibronic basis sets were constructed from the CASSCF vibrational analysis, and Franck-Condon factors between the S1 and T1 manifolds were required. The MRCI+Pople S1-T1 difference was the value adopted for all subsequent dynamics. correlation_correction: MRCI with Davidson or Pople energy corrections; full CI within the active space for the T1 interaction energies.

compound_name: yttrium clusters Yn for n = 2-4, in tetrahedral, rhombus and square structures
method: restricted active space MCSCF (in place of a full CASSCF) followed by higher-order CI
software: a modified version of ALCHEMY II
active_space_orbital_description: in both the CASSCF and the higher-order CI, all sixteen 4s and 4p orbitals were kept inactive - no excitations from these shells were allowed, though the orbitals were allowed to relax - leaving twenty-four orbitals for the active space in both the C2v and D2h point groups. Including all twenty-four orbitals with the twelve valence electrons (4d1 5s2 per atom) gave too many configurations, so a restricted active space MCSCF was used, chosen from several preliminary test sets with different active orbitals; the optimal space for a given total number of orbitals was taken as the one yielding the lowest energy. The final CASSCF for the tetrahedral structure in C2v included four a1, three b2 and three b1 orbitals.
active_space_protocol: restricted active space MCSCF: 4a1 + 3b2 + 3b1 = ten orbitals for the tetrahedron in C2v, with a separate selection for the rhombus and square structures; all sixteen 4s and 4p orbitals inactive but relaxed
electronic_structure_description: Electronic states of the yttrium clusters Y2, Y3 and Y4 in tetrahedral, rhombus and square geometries.
Other: The selection criterion is stated plainly and is worth noting because it is not the usual one: among several trial spaces of the same total size, the one giving the lowest energy was kept. Changing the basis set does not affect the oscillator strengths at all, and both sets of values agree well with experiment and with MS-CASPT2 results. Experimentally the first band shows a vibrational progression with an oscillator strength of 0.009 and the second band an oscillator strength of 0.12. Excitation at 363.5 nm corresponds to the S0 to S1 transition and gives the dimethylamino radical with a lifetime above 0.5 s, while excitation at 248 nm implies a different mechanism. Experimentally, after dissociation the fragments carry 18.4 kcal/mol and the dimethylamine radical the remaining 23.0 kcal/mol. A surface crossing point occurs at 75.9 kcal/mol (3.29 eV) above the ground-state minimum. Dissociation after excitation at 363.5 nm deviates from planarity, whereas at 250 nm NDMA exhibits planar character. Nesting is what makes the dissociation energetics meaningful, since the asymptotic limits and the parent molecule must be described consistently. The basis strategy is split deliberately for the same reason: geometries at 6-31G* justified by the size of the molecule, energies recomputed with the more balanced ANO-L specifically to make the vertical transitions and excited-surface energies quantitative. That split is validated by the observation that changing the basis set does not affect the oscillator strengths at all, so the smaller basis is adequate for the geometry-dependent quantities and the larger one is needed only for energies. basis_set: 6-31G* for all geometry optimizations; ANO-L with the C, N, O [3s2p1d] / H [2s1p] contraction scheme for the energy recalculations
active_space_orbital_description: Eleven electrons in eight orbitals, the space used to optimize the NO moiety.
active_space_protocol: The NO fragment is treated with its own space rather than a reduction of the parent, unlike the dimethylamine fragment. The resulting internuclear distance of 1.159 A serves as the check on that choice.
electronic_structure_description: The NO moiety was optimized at the CASSCF(11,8) level, giving an internuclear distance of 1.159 A. It is the counter-fragment to the dimethylamine radical in the homolytic N-N cleavage of NDMA, and together the fragments carry 18.4 kcal/mol of the available energy against 23.0 kcal/mol for the dimethylamine radical.
Other: Four different spaces are used across one study and their relationships are stated explicitly. The parent (14,10) is inherited from the authors' earlier work on NH2NO and lists its orbitals individually: 2sO, 2sN, sigma-NN, pi-NO, sigma-NO, np-N, np-O, pi*-NO, sigma*-NN and sigma*-NO. Studying the tautomerizations required adding a sigma-CH orbital and its virtual partner, giving (16,12) -- the space grows to accommodate a hydrogen migration that the original set could not represent. The dimethylamine radical fragment gets its own (11,10) built for the two extrusion channels it participates in, and that space is described as obtained by reduction of the parent space, so the fragment and parent descriptions are nested rather than independent. The NO fragment was optimized at yet another level, CASSCF(11,8). Nesting is what makes the dissociation energetics meaningful, since the asymptotic limits and the parent molecule must be described consistently. The basis strategy is split deliberately for the same reason: geometries at 6-31G* justified by the size of the molecule, energies recomputed with the more balanced ANO-L specifically to make the vertical transitions and excited-surface energies quantitative. That split is validated by the observation that changing the basis set does not affect the oscillator strengths at all, so the smaller basis is adequate for the geometry-dependent quantities and the larger one is needed only for energies. Core orbitals were frozen in CASPT2 as optimized at the CASSCF level, and imaginary modes at the Franck-Condon geometries were characterized separately at CASSCF/ANO-L with gradients, rotations and translations projected out.
reference_short: Arenas, Otero, Pelaez & Soto, J. Org. Chem. 2007, 72, 4741
notes: This is the only fragment in the study whose active space is not described as a reduction of the parent NDMA space. correlation_correction: CASPT2 and MS-CASPT2 on the CASSCF reference with the 1s core orbitals of C, N and O frozen as optimized at the CASSCF level, with a shift applied to minimize intruder state contamination.

d_electron_count: 5d10 in the 2A1 state; the gold atom valence space is 5d10 6s1
point_group: C2v; the ground state is X 2B2 and the bent HAuH structure was studied on a bending potential energy surface
geometry_source: Bending potential energy surfaces computed in two and three dimensions for the 2A1 and 2B2 states. Dissociation energies computed by a supermolecular calculation with the Au-H distances set to 10 A, because MRSDCI is not size consistent. Vibrational frequencies computed at the coupled cluster (CCD) and MP2 levels in the same gold basis with aug-cc-pVTZ on hydrogen, and compared with experiment and with DFT.
method: CASSCF followed by multireference singles and doubles configuration interaction (MRSDCI); CCD and MP2 for frequencies; matrix isolation infrared spectroscopy in solid hydrogen for comparison
software: Balasubramanian's programs for all CASSCF and MRSDCI computations
basis_set: Extended (3s3p4d1f) basis for gold with a relativistic effective core potential of Ermler and co-workers replacing 68 electrons and leaving the 5d10 6s1 shells as the valence space; triple-zeta plus polarization for the hydrogens; aug-cc-pVTZ on hydrogen for the frequency calculations
relativistic_treatment: Relativistic effective core potential on gold, replacing 68 electrons; relativistic mass-velocity stabilization of the 6s orbital and destabilization of the 5d orbital are noted as essential for gold
active_space_orbital_description: Five a1 orbitals, three b2 orbitals, two b1 orbitals and one a2 orbital, holding all 13 valence electrons of AuH2, distributed in all possible ways among the active orbitals. The space was chosen to include all 5d, 6s and 6p orbitals of gold.
active_space_protocol: The space is dictated by the atomic spectroscopy of gold rather than by the molecular bonding: because the first excited state of the gold atom arises from 5d9 6s2 and the second from 5d10 6p1, all of the 5d, 6s and 6p orbitals must be active if the molecular states correlating with those atomic limits are to be described. Listing the space by symmetry block -- five a1, three b2, two b1 and one a2 -- makes the composition explicit rather than leaving it to a bare count. The MRSDCI built on it correlates the same 13 electrons and takes as references all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients at or above 0.01, which typically gave 65 reference configurations and up to 3.4 million total configurations. Because MRSDCI is not size consistent, dissociation energies were obtained from a supermolecular calculation at 10 A rather than by subtracting fragment energies.
electronic_structure_description: The gold atom 2D state from the 5d9 6s2 configuration lies 1.7 eV above the ground state while the corresponding state from 5d10 6p1 lies 4.9 eV higher, a consequence of relativistic mass-velocity stabilization of the 6s orbital and destabilization of the 5d orbital. The barrier to insert Au(2D) into H2 is 53 kcal/mol, but the 2P state of gold lies considerably above this barrier and is very reactive because it also yields a 2B2 state which undergoes an avoided crossing with the 2B2 state arising from Au(2D); the barrier appears to arise from that avoided crossing. The barrier for formation of the lowest 2A1 state from Au(2S) + H2 is 95 kcal/mol. Once the X 2B2 state is formed through excitation of gold to the 2P state it remains in its potential well, since dissociating back to Au(2D) + H2 requires surmounting a large barrier. The 2B2 and 2A1 surfaces cross at a bond angle of 65 degrees, about 25 kcal/mol above the X 2B2 minimum, and that 25 kcal/mol barrier must be overcome before decomposition to Au(2S) + H2. Spin-orbit coupling between the two states cannot be large because the 2A1 state has predominantly Au(5d10 6s1) character; the 2B2 state has a larger spin-orbit effect but its coupling to 2A1 should be negligible because of the closed 5d10 shell in the latter. X 2B2 is therefore a long-lived ground state, 27 kcal/mol more stable than Au(2D) + H2. A zero-point correction of 6.4 kcal/mol is applied. The computed 2A1 bending surface is close to a previous study but the 2B2 surface differs, especially near the dissociation limit and the minimum. Adding an f function gives unrealistic infrared intensities. The AuH2 anion has also been observed, with a related energy of 68 kcal/mol from DFT.
Other: The composition of the active space is fixed by where the atomic excited states come from, not by which orbitals form bonds: since gold's first excited state is 5d9 6s2 and its second is 5d10 6p1, the 5d, 6s and 6p sets all have to be active for the molecular states correlating with those limits to exist in the wave function at all. That matters directly for the physics being reported, because the barrier to insertion is attributed to an avoided crossing between two 2B2 states arising from the 2D and 2P atomic asymptotes -- a feature that simply cannot appear if the 6p orbitals are outside the space. The paper reports its space by symmetry block (five a1, three b2, two b1, one a2) rather than as a bare pair of numbers, and the MRSDCI inherits it by taking every CASSCF configuration with coefficient at or above 0.01 as a reference, typically 65 references expanding to 3.4 million configurations. One methodological consequence is handled explicitly: MRSDCI is not size consistent, so dissociation energies come from a supermolecular calculation at 10 A separation rather than from fragment subtraction. The comparison with earlier work is instructive -- the 2A1 bending surface reproduces a previous study closely while the 2B2 surface differs near both the minimum and the dissociation limit, which is where the multi-asymptote character of the space would be expected to matter most. Separately, adding an f function to the gold basis produces unrealistic infrared intensities, so the basis was not simply extended for its own sake.
reference_short: Andrews, Wang, Manceron & Balasubramanian, J. Phys. Chem. A 2004, 108, 2936
notes: The molecule was observed by infrared spectroscopy in solid hydrogen; the 650-400 cm-1 region is shown for thermally treated samples. The AuH2 anion has been observed separately. correlation_correction: MRSDCI including single and double excitations from 65 reference configurations, correlating all 13 electrons.

electronic_structure_description: Cs complex with one water hydrogen above and one below the aromatic plane, hydrogen bonded at the amide NH. Ionisation energy D0 <- S0: CASSCF 55041 (3768), CASSCF+ZPE 55265 (3655), CASMP2 63418 (3504), CASMP2+ZPE 63642 (3392), experiment 64225 +/- 5 (3182). Excitation shortens the H12-O18 hydrogen bond only slightly, while ionisation changes it substantially. Within the amide group the C1-N2 and C14-O15 distances shorten on excitation and again on ionisation while N2-C14 and N2-H13 lengthen; 34% of the excess positive charge delocalises onto the amide group and the N2-C14 bond loses double-bond character. compound_name: cyanogen iodide, ICN, in its ground state - near-equilibrium potential energy surface and anharmonic force field
geometry_source: 45 energy points computed on a grid, 1.905-2.328 A for the C-I bond, 1.058-1.328 A for the C-N bond and 180-150 degrees for the ICN angle, then fitted to a quartic polynomial in the two bond stretches and the angle bend; the fit reproduces the CASSCF energies to 1.1 cm-1 rms. Points up to 9000 cm-1 above the minimum were computed and the expansion is expected valid to 6000 cm-1.
method: CASSCF, used to generate a ground-state adiabatic potential energy surface from which the anharmonic force field is derived; the resulting force constants then serve as the starting point and as fixed constraints for a weighted least-squares fit to 35 experimental spectroscopic data for three isotopomers
basis_set: cc-pVDZ for carbon and nitrogen, [3s2p1d] contractions of the (9s4p1d) primitive sets with polarization up to d; for iodine, no such set being available, a similar polarized double-zeta basis, a [11s9p6d] contraction of a (19s15p12d) primitive set. 96 contracted Gaussians in total.
active_space_orbital_description: 16 valence electrons in 12 orbitals, giving 35793 configuration state functions; the space is the valence shell, chosen so that valence electron correlation is included in the surface
electronic_structure_description: The CASSCF minimum lies at re(C-I) = 2.048 A, Re(C-N) = 1.180 A and a linear ICN angle, against the experimental equilibrium values 1.9921 and 1.1604 A. The computed force constants are f11 = 3.033, f22 = 17.36, f33 = 0.2636 aJ A-n for the C-I stretch, C-N stretch and bend. Predicted fundamentals for I12C14N are nu1 = 464.3, nu2 = 303.7 and nu3 = 2161.8 cm-1, against observed 488.8, 304.2 and 2179.2 cm-1; the vibration-rotation alpha constants come out 12.323, -9.501 and 15.974 MHz against 11.895, -9.499 and 14.314.
Other: The (16,12) valence surface is accurate enough to bootstrap the experimental analysis but not to replace it, and the paper is explicit about where it fails: agreement is percentually much worse for the anharmonic contributions to overtones and combination bands than for the fundamentals, so the quartic constants are where the empirical refinement had to move most. Accordingly all quadratic, five cubic and three quartic constants were fitted to the spectroscopic data while six quartic constants were held fixed at the CASSCF values - the space is trusted for the parts of the potential the data cannot pin down, and overruled where they can.
reference_short: Degli Esposti, Bizzocchi, Tamassia, Puzzarini, Tarroni and Zelinger, Mol. Phys. 93, 95-106 (1998)
notes: The paper is primarily a millimetre-wave and diode-laser spectroscopic study of IC15N; the CASSCF calculation supplies the ab initio force field that seeds the empirical fit. correlation_correction empty: the reported surface is variational CASSCF with no post-CASSCF correction.

electronic_structure_description: Ground-state electron density of thorocene, ThCOT2 computed at CASSCF and analysed topologically (QTAIM) to quantify the covalent contribution of f-orbital participation to An-COT bonding across the series. active_space_protocol: The full valence space, and the paper states the practical test it had to pass: with these orbitals the curves come out smooth over the whole range from 0.06 to 1.20 nm, which for seventeen states of a molecule with several low-lying crossings is the real constraint - a space that describes the equilibrium region well but breaks down at short or long separation would be useless here. The 1s electrons are kept in closed-shell orbitals. All four symmetry blocks of the Abelian subgroup are computed, since the seventeen states span all of them.
nroots_per_mult: seventeen states in all: the X 3Pi ground state, a 1Sigma+, b 1Pi, A 3Sigma+, B 3Sigma-, c 1Delta, D 3Pi, and ten higher states including quintets - 1 5Pi, 3 1Sigma+, 3 3Pi, 2 1Pi, 2 3Sigma+, 1 3Delta, 1 5Sigma+, 4 3Pi, 2 3Sigma- and 1 5Sigma-

The first excited state a 1Sigma+ lies only 111.49 cm-1 above it at 0.12734 nm and 1706.97 cm-1, against measured values of 0.12745 nm and 1705.40 cm-1 - the near-degeneracy of these two states of different multiplicity is the central difficulty of this molecule. The b 1Pi state follows at 3737.87 cm-1 with 0.13271 nm and 1537.03 cm-1, against measured 0.13279 nm and 1531.65 cm-1. Spin-orbit coupling splits the ground state into components 23.70 cm-1 apart, lowering the ground level by that amount, with the two nearly coincident components separated by only 2.2 cm-1; the D 3Pi state at about 27958 cm-1 splits similarly but its corresponding pair is closer together, which the paper attributes to the much weaker perturbation from the nearby Sigma state at that energy. active_space_protocol: The fourteen-electron ten-orbital space is taken over deliberately from earlier work on this molecule rather than rederived, so that the present results can be set against that study's. The same space is then used with both the small and the large basis sets, which is what isolates the basis-set effect from the space. A full-valence space of twenty electrons in fifteen orbitals was also run with the small basis as a check: it raises both excitation energies by about 0.06 and 0.09 eV, so the smaller space is not the limiting approximation. Three states - two of a-prime and one of a-double-prime symmetry - are state-averaged, and the calculations meant for dynamics are run without symmetry because the trajectories will not preserve it. The paper reports more than one active space for this system and the field held all of them: nel was '14, with a full-valence 20-electron variant also tested'; norb was '10, with a full-valence 15-orbital variant also tested'. The structured fields now carry the production space -- the leading number, which the cell's own wording marked as the one used, the others being described there as a test, check or variant. What the cell said is preserved in full.

electronic_structure_description: The two lowest excited singlets are an A-double-prime and an A-prime state. The configuration-interaction excitation energies converge along the basis sequence to 4.13 and 5.27 eV, against measured absorption maxima at 4.00 and 5.25 eV. The self-consistent-field values in the small basis are 4.313 and 5.782 eV, high by 0.18 and 0.51 eV relative to the best benchmark. Transition dipole moments are where the two methods part company: the self-consistent-field values are 0.282 and 0.331 debye where the correlated values are 0.089 and 0.270. Along the O-Cl stretch the first three singlet states were mapped to establish where the excited states become accessible.

Excitation energies from the cheap method are acceptable for judging which states are energetically reachable, and the gradients - compared against numerical correlated gradients projected onto the O-Cl bond vector, since analytic ones are unavailable - are adequate to drive the trajectories. The transition dipoles are not: the ratio of their squares, which is what sets the relative absorption cross sections, comes out 1.38 from the cheap method against 9.30 from the benchmark, and the measured cross-section ratio is 9.99. So the cheap method cannot predict the relative populations of the two excited states at all, and the planned dynamics will instead assume a geometry-independent dipole and weight the two states 1:9 by hand. That is an unusually explicit account of which quantities a method may and may not be trusted for.

method: Ab initio molecular dynamics at the CASSCF level, with Hartree-Fock geometry optimization and MP2 single-point energies for the reaction energetics
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for the CASSCF dynamics and the Hartree-Fock optimizations; 6-31+G(d,p) used additionally at the MP2 level and to test the CASSCF dissociation curve

active_space_protocol: A minimal two-electron two-orbital space confined to the colliding hydrogen atoms, chosen so that the formation and dissociation of the H-H bond is described correctly across the whole trajectory while the cage is treated at the mean-field level. The two-electron two-orbital dissociation curves for the hydrogen molecule were compared between the 6-31G(d) and 6-31+G(d,p) basis sets and found essentially indistinguishable, which justified running all the dynamics in the smaller basis.
electronic_structure_description: Trajectories were started by inserting a second hydrogen atom into the hydrogen-encapsulated cage, and in many cases the gradual formation of a hydrogen molecule was observed after frequent collisions of the two hydrogen atoms within the cage. Two sets of initial conditions were used: inserting the second hydrogen with a small kinetic energy of 0.5 kcal/mol starting from the transition state for the insertion reaction, and inserting it with a kinetic energy larger than the insertion barrier, starting 2.5 Angstrom above a cage face; the latter used 60 kcal/mol of kinetic energy for this cage. method: State-averaged CASSCF with an n-electron valence-state second-order perturbation theory correction, the spin-orbit coupling operator being evaluated over a basis of the state-averaged wave functions using the perturbatively corrected total energies; coupled-perturbed density functional theory with the B3LYP functional computed alongside for comparison
basis_set: TZVP for Mn, O and N with SVP for C and H, together with SV/C and TZV/C auxiliary basis sets and the resolution-of-identity approximation for the multiconfigurational calculations; the density functional calculations used SV/J and TZVP/J auxiliary sets with the RIJCOSX approximation. soc_included: yes, spin-orbit coupling contributes about 85 percent of the axial zero-field splitting parameter
ss_included: yes, the spin-spin coupling term supplies the remaining contribution to the axial parameter
active_space_orbital_description: All three manganese(IV) 3d electrons in the five 3d orbitals, CAS(3,5). For one complex an enlarged CAS(7,7) was also tried, adding the oxygen-based manganese-oxo bonding pi orbitals to the metal d set.

nroots_per_mult: 10 quartet and 40 doublet roots

geometry_source: Optimized at the CASSCF level with a correlation-consistent double-zeta basis, with frequency analyses confirming the transition states
method: CASSCF geometry optimization and frequency analysis, with multireference configuration interaction including single and double excitations used to refine the energetics at those geometries and zero-point corrections taken from the CASSCF frequencies; vertical excitation energies additionally computed with time-dependent density functional theory and equation-of-motion coupled cluster
software: GAUSSIAN03 for the density functional and CASSCF calculations; GAUSSIAN09 for the coupled cluster calculations
active_space_orbital_description: Ten electrons in eight orbitals: the pi and pi* orbitals of the carbonyl group, two lone-pair orbitals on the two oxygen atoms, and the sigma and sigma* orbitals of both the carbon-chlorine and the carbon-oxygen bonds that can undergo alpha cleavage.
active_space_protocol: Both competing alpha-cleavage channels are represented in the same space so that their barriers can be compared on a common footing. The authors state explicitly that CASSCF cannot provide sufficient correlation energy, so the space serves to generate geometries and a reference wave function while all energies are refined by configuration interaction.
electronic_structure_description: The first excited singlet minimum arises mainly from an n to pi* excitation. On excitation the carbonyl bond lengthens from 1.193 Angstrom in the ground state minimum to 1.380 Angstrom, and the carbon rehybridizes from sp2 to sp3, converting the planar ground state structure into a pyramidal excited state one; the adiabatic energy difference between the two minima is 102.2 kcal/mol. Two transition states for alpha cleavage were located and confirmed by frequency analysis, one for carbon-oxygen fission and one for carbon-chlorine fission. The carbon-oxygen barrier is 9.7 kcal/mol on the refined electronic energies and 15.6 kcal/mol once zero-point energy is included, the increase arising because the transition state has one fewer real vibrational mode than the minimum and so a smaller zero-point energy. The carbon-chlorine barrier is 1.5 kcal/mol, with the corresponding bond significantly elongated at its transition state.
Other: The authors say the space selection 'requires some details' and then supply them, orbital class by orbital class, which is the level of specification that makes a space reusable. Ten electrons in eight orbitals: the pi and pi* of the carbonyl, two lone-pair orbitals on the two oxygen atoms, and the sigma and sigma* pairs of both bonds that can undergo alpha cleavage. Both competing dissociation channels are therefore represented in the same space, which is what allows their barriers to be compared on one footing -- the central quantitative claim of the paper is that one barrier is 9.7 kcal/mol and the other 1.5, and that comparison would be worthless if each channel had been given its own tailored space. Including the sigma manifold of a bond that stays intact in one channel is the price of that comparability. The paper is unusually blunt about what the space alone cannot do, stating flatly that the CASSCF calculations cannot provide sufficient correlation energy and using configuration interaction with single and double excitations on the reference geometries to refine every energy. So the space is treated as a geometry and reference generator rather than as an energy method, with the division of labour stated rather than implied. A subtle trap is documented in the process. The barrier for one channel is 9.7 kcal/mol on the refined electronic energies but 15.6 kcal/mol once zero-point energy is included, and the authors explain the direction: the transition state carries one fewer real vibrational mode than the minimum because one has become imaginary, so its zero-point energy is smaller and the correction raises rather than lowers the barrier. A 6 kcal/mol swing on a 10 kcal/mol barrier from a bookkeeping effect, moving in the counterintuitive direction, is worth carrying generally -- zero-point corrections at transition states are not small and are not signed the way one expects. The wave function analysis at the excited minimum shows what the space buys structurally: the carbonyl bond lengthens from 1.193 to 1.380 Angstrom on excitation and the carbon rehybridizes from sp2 to sp3, turning a planar structure pyramidal, with an adiabatic excitation energy of 102.2 kcal/mol. A space containing the carbonyl pi system and the oxygen lone pairs is exactly what is needed to describe an n to pi* state that rehybridizes the carbon, and a space built only from the breaking bonds would have missed it. Vertical excitation energies were cross-checked against time-dependent density functional theory and equation-of-motion coupled cluster as well as the configuration interaction treatment, so the state characters do not rest on the active space alone.

active_space_protocol: A detailed, transferable RAS active-space-selection recipe for core (X-ray) excitation/ionization, tested on 1,1-difluoroethene at the C K-edge. The space must contain: (i) the core orbital(s) of interest, placed in the subspace to which the HEXS core-hole projection is applied; (ii) virtual orbitals, chosen deliberately by the user - more virtuals give a more complete spectrum, since they are the arrival orbitals of the excited 1s electron and enable multiple-excitation intensity; (iii) occupied valence orbitals for correlation and shake-up states, where often just the highest occupied (HOMO) suffices. Key finding: even a MINIMAL active space of just the core orbital + HOMO(pi) + LUMO(pi*) reproduces the strongest pre-edge pi*-resonances accurately in energy, relative intensity and line shape; missing correlation from excluded occupied orbitals is recovered by the PT2 step, which stays stable as long as the HOMO is in the space. The paper gives an iterative algorithm (minAS + n virtuals per step) to systematically grow the virtual set and add core-excited states while keeping cost low. No molecular symmetry was imposed, to keep the recipe general.
Other: Applications: N/C/O K-edge XPS and XANES spectra of the two most stable glycine conformers (the three edges ~100 eV apart allow unique conformer identification), C K-edge of formaldehyde and the fluoroethane/ethene series. Sub-eV accuracy against high-resolution experiment, with the DHO vibronic treatment quantitatively reproducing line shapes. The core-hole formation modulates (weakens or strengthens) bonds, rationalized via an ESCA-potential/chemical-shift picture.

The natural orbitals show exactly one sizeable Co-N bonding interaction, the axial sigma bond between Co d(z2) and N p(z) at 40 percent Co and 53 percent N. Perpendicular to it, Co d(xz) and d(yz) stay practically nonbonding with occupation numbers of 1.95 and 1.97 and 90 and 97 percent Co character. The singly occupied orbital is centred on the nitrene nitrogen p(x) at 84 percent N with an occupation number of 1.03, and the spin density reproduces its shape, giving a spin population of +0.88 on nitrogen - close enough to unity to establish an N-centred radical. For the iron-nitrene, B3LYP identifies the second singly occupied orbital as an Fe-N pi antibond, pi*(x), which would mean two Fe-N pi bonds and hence a metal-nitrido-like description. The CASSCF natural orbitals show instead that this orbital is essentially pure metal - 94 percent Fe d(xz) with an occupation number of 1.01 - and the paper states plainly that the density-functional picture 'is an overestimation of the Fe-N covalency', since two Fe-N pi bonds are not feasible for a nitrene. The verdict is delivered despite, not because of, strong multireference character. method: state-averaged CASSCF with four different active spaces compared head to head, followed by three post-CASSCF corrections - strongly contracted NEVPT2, its quasi-degenerate extension with a Van Vleck effective Hamiltonian, and spectroscopy-oriented MRCI with singles and doubles plus the Davidson correction (SORCI+Q) - all in multi-state formulation and all built on the corresponding state-averaged CASSCF densities. Real-time TDDFT with Ehrenfest nuclear dynamics run separately in CP2K to demonstrate dissociation explicitly
software: ORCA 5.03 for all static multireference work; CP2K for the real-time TDDFT Ehrenfest dynamics
basis_set: segmented all-electron relativistically contracted SARC-DKH-TZVP on iodine and relativistically recontracted def2-DKH-TZVP on all other atoms; a mixed Gaussian and plane-wave dual-space basis for the CP2K dynamics
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess one-particle Hamiltonian with a finite-size Gaussian-like nucleus model
soc_included: yes, and it is the entire subject: spin-orbit coupling matrix elements and SOC-corrected transition moments from the DKH2-transformed spin-orbit mean-field operator including spin-other-orbit and spin-own-orbit terms with a DFT-like local correlation term, treated throughout in a quasi-degenerate perturbation theory framework
active_space_orbital_description: the recommended space is ten electrons in nine orbitals: the six benzene pi orbitals, the occupied and virtual sigma orbitals of the C-I bond, and the out-of-plane pz lone pair of iodine. Three other spaces were run for comparison - (8e,8o) with benzene pi plus the C-I sigma/sigma* pair only; (10e,9o)-LP with the in-plane px/y iodine lone pair added instead of the pz; and (12e,10o) with both iodine lone pairs - and a six-orbital benzene-pi-only space was tried and rejected
active_space_protocol: A stepwise enlargement in which every step is justified by a named failure of the previous one. The six-orbital benzene pi space suggested by TD-DFT was rejected because it gives an almost zero spin-orbit coupling matrix; the C-I sigma and sigma* pair was added because the dissociation cannot be described without it, giving (8e,8o); the iodine lone pairs were added because (8e,8o) misses low-lying states carrying very large couplings to the ground state. The paper states explicitly that these orbitals 'has to be included during CASSCF orbital optimization for efficient orbital mixing, not only in the final CAS-CI stage'. State averaging is over six low-lying singlets and nine low-lying triplets, the number 'chosen based on level spacing to include all near-degenerate energy states and provide efficient mixing in spin-coupling'
nroots_per_mult: 6 low-lying singlet roots and 9 low-lying triplet roots in every space compared
electronic_structure_description: Closed-shell aromatic iodide whose ground state is dominated by a single CAS-CI configuration with weight above 0.99 regardless of the active space chosen. With the recommended (10e,9o) space the lowest six triplets lie at 3.752, 4.876, 4.884, 5.035, 6.982 and 7.068 eV above the ground state, with averaged spin-orbit coupling matrix elements to the ground state of 0.926, 6.63, 0.106, 1286.754, 4.571 and 0.122 reciprocal centimetres - the fourth triplet, T4 of B2 symmetry, carrying a coupling three orders of magnitude larger than any other. That state is dissociative along the C-I coordinate. It cannot be reached directly from S1 B1 by intersystem crossing because of spin-orbit selection rules, but is easily populated by coupling from other triplets, the squared matrix element from T1 A1 being 4965.7 reciprocal centimetres squared. T1 A1 is stable near equilibrium but dissociative at long range. The conclusion is that iodobenzene cannot phosphoresce because every strongly spin-orbit coupled triplet sublevel leads to dissociation - confirmed by explicit Ehrenfest dynamics
Other: Four active spaces are run at fixed root set on the same molecule. Across them the excitation energy of the strongly coupled triplet moves by about half an electronvolt while its spin-orbit coupling moves by a factor of six hundred. Across the four post-CASSCF treatments at fixed space the energy moves 5.035 to 4.523 eV while the coupling moves only 1287 to 1160 reciprocal centimetres, about ten percent. Two spaces of identical size differ in one orbital: (10e,9o)-LP, which adds iodine's in-plane px/y lone pair, gives a coupling of 2.085 reciprocal centimetres for the fourth triplet, while (10e,9o)-Pi, which adds the out-of-plane pz orbital that can mix with the benzene pi system, gives 1286.754 for the same state, at the same electron count, orbital count, root set and code. Adding the second lone pair on top of the pz, to reach (12e,10o), then changes that coupling by only four percent. The space also decides which state carries the coupling: the very large matrix element sits on T4 in the (8e,8o) and pz-containing spaces but moves to T5 in the in-plane-lone-pair space, so the state ordering itself is active-space dependent. The six-orbital benzene pi space that linear-response TD-DFT points to 'leads to an almost zero-defined SOC matrix in CASSCF and all post-CASSCF methods', which would leave phosphorescence available only through spin-vibronic Herzberg-Teller coupling. Strongly contracted NEVPT2 returns spin-orbit coupling matrix elements identical to CASSCF to every printed digit - 1286.754 and 635.898 reciprocal centimetres - because a non-quasi-degenerate perturbative correction shifts state energies without touching the wavefunctions the coupling is built from; only the quasi-degenerate variant, which rotates the states, and SORCI+Q, which rebuilds the wavefunction, move those numbers at all. The ground state is over 99 percent one configuration in every one of the four spaces. On procedure, the extra orbitals 'has to be included during CASSCF orbital optimization for efficient orbital mixing, not only in the final CAS-CI stage' - enlarging the CI expansion after the orbitals are fixed is not the same thing as enlarging the active space.
reference_short: Rublev, Boldyrev & Scheiner, J. Phys. Chem. A 2023, 127, 4927-4933
notes: The heavy-atom effect does deliver a very large spin-orbit coupling here, but every triplet sublevel that carries it is dissociative along the C-I coordinate, so the molecule cannot phosphoresce. The argument is a composite of three independent pieces - multireference vertical energies and couplings, an unrelaxed potential energy scan showing the dissociative character, and RT-TDDFT Ehrenfest dynamics in a different code showing the dissociation explicitly - and the paper is clear about which piece does what. Intersystem-crossing accessibility is argued through Fermi golden rule proportionality to squared coupling matrix elements together with spin-orbit selection rules, not by computing rates. Note a printing artefact in Table 1: the row labelled S0 to T7 in the two pz-containing columns repeats the T1 values exactly and should not be read as a seventh state. The recommended production protocol is QD-SC-NEVPT2 on the (10e,9o) space with the benzene pi system, the C-I sigma and sigma*, and the pz lone pair. Three corrections are compared at fixed active space: SC-NEVPT2, QD-SC-NEVPT2 and SORCI+Q. For the strongly coupled triplet they give excitation energies of 4.966, 4.694 and 4.523 eV against 5.035 eV at bare CASSCF, and couplings of 1286.754, 1299.534 and 1159.658 reciprocal centimetres against 1286.754 - the SC-NEVPT2 value being numerically identical to CASSCF because that correction cannot alter the wavefunction from which the coupling is computed. QD-SC-NEVPT2 is the one the authors recommend.

point_group: C2v at the symmetric geometries; the scan is carried out in Cs, where the two triplets both become 3A'' and can interact
geometry_source: energies computed on a grid r1 in [2.0, 3.0] a0, r2 in [2.0, 3.5] a0 and alpha in [90, 160] degrees, with steps of 0.05 and 0.1 a0 in the bond lengths and 2 to 5 degrees in the angle - the wide angular range being needed because the 3A2 and 3B1 minima are about 27 degrees apart (99 and 126 degrees). method: CASSCF orbitals state-averaged over X1A1, 3A2 and 3B1, followed by internally contracted MRCI with the Davidson correction, icMRCI(Q); the adiabatic pair is then transformed to a quasidiabatic representation by the procedure implemented in MOLPRO, which minimizes the change in shape of the active orbitals rather than computing nonadiabatic coupling matrix elements directly

active_space_orbital_description: all valence orbitals with only the three oxygen 1s orbitals closed. The alternative CAS(12,9) used in much of the ozone literature keeps both the 1s and 2s orbitals of each oxygen doubly occupied and out of the excited determinants
active_space_protocol: the choice between the two standard ozone spaces is decided on a stated criterion: the adiabatic excitation energy. CAS(18,12) gives 11 637 configuration state functions for the two triplets against 1710 for CAS(12,9), and a correspondingly larger correlation energy. Measured against T00(3A2) = 9553 cm-1 with ZPE(X1A1) = 1444 and ZPE(3A2) about 1000 cm-1, every combination overestimates Te(3A2) except CAS(18,12)/aug-cc-pVTZ, and the same holds for 3B1 with T00 = 11 695 cm-1. The orbitals are averaged over three states because the ground state lies close to the triplets and shares a dissociation channel with 3B1, and because averaging over it is what makes Te available as a check.
multiplicities_studied: singlet ground state and two triplets
nroots_per_mult: one singlet (X1A1) and two triplets (3A2, 3B1) in the orbital averaging
electronic_structure_description: Adiabatic excitation energies Te in cm-1: with CAS(12,9), 10 606.615, 10 924.823 and 10 985.080 for 3A2 and 14 630.844, 14 857.748 and 14 912.132 for 3B1 across aug-cc-pVTZ, QZ and 5Z; with CAS(18,12), 9938.945, 10 268.678 and 10 345.907 for 3A2 and 12 323.491, 12 526.421 and 12 583.627 for 3B1. Fitting the diabatic surfaces with 92 parameters to eighth order reproduces 3871 points of the 3A2 surface to within 32 cm-1 RMS and 3801 points of 3B1 to within 40 cm-1, against under 1.0 cm-1 for the ground state - the excited-state ab initio energies are simply several times less accurate. From the fitted 3A2 surface, ignoring the interaction: re = 2.5504 a0 and alpha_e = 98.575 degrees with aug-cc-pVTZ (2.5367, 98.652 with QZ) against an empirical 2.542 a0 and 98.9 degrees; Te 9814.933 (10 126.133), ZPE 1190.401 (1211.214), T00 9561.811 (9893.824) against 9553.021 empirical; nu1 1055.610, nu2 552.972, nu3 704.518 cm-1 with TZ, against empirical 1190 +/- 15, 528.99 and 367 +/- 17. For 3B1: re 2.4955 a0 and alpha_e 126.571 degrees with TZ, Te 12 165.341, T00 11 834.295 against 11 695 +/- 15 empirical, nu1 874.077, nu2 514.574, nu3 748.155 cm-1 against empirical 1090 +/- 80 and 555 +/- 15. The two states interact only in Cs - in C2v they belong to different irreducible representations - so the off-diagonal diabatic coupling is nonzero only when the antisymmetric mode nu3 is excited, and their surfaces cross at alpha between 115 and 120 degrees. Including the interaction shifts the bending fundamental of 3A2 down by about 50 cm-1 and that of 3B1 up by about the same amount.
Other: Enlarging the basis set here makes the agreement worse, not better: the extra correlation energy raises Te and hence T00, so with aug-cc-pVQZ the 3A2 origin comes out about 130 cm-1 above the empirical value even with the interaction included and ZPE taken as 1000 cm-1. The two standard ozone active spaces differ by nearly 2300 cm-1 in Te(3B1), far more than the basis-set effect within either, so the space and not the basis is what decides this number. The diabatization is the other half of the construction - the states cross, and only the diabatic representation is smooth enough to fit with a Partridge-Schwenke-type expansion.

compound_name: Cyclopropanone, photodissociation to carbon monoxide and ethylene (Norrish-type CO release) plus a polymerization channel
geometry_source: initial conditions from ground-state molecular dynamics sampling at constant excitation energy, mimicking continuous-wave excitation in resonance with the laser; 100 geometries sampled across the spectrum. The cheaper (2,4) active space was used for this ground-state sampling stage
method: a controlled comparison of eight electronic structure methods - SA-CASSCF, SS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2, XMS-CASPT2, MRCI, FOMO-CASCI, MR-CISD/OM3 and SI-SA-REKS - crossed against several nonadiabatic algorithms (Landau-Zener surface hopping, fewest-switches surface hopping, AIMSWISS), to separate the influence of electronic structure from that of the coupled electron-nuclear algorithm
software: BAGEL for the CASPT2 simulations; other packages per method
basis_set: 6-31G* for most calculations; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 runs in BAGEL where 6-31G* is unavailable; a pseudominimal basis by default for MR-CISD/OM3
active_space_orbital_description: two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO) and two sigma*(CC)
active_space_protocol: (8,7) - two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO), two sigma*(CC) - used for every method except SI-SA-REKS. The choice was triangulated three ways rather than assumed: previous studies of this molecule, automated selection with the AutoCAS code, and the authors' own benchmarking of potential energy surfaces and absorption spectra. Two reduced spaces appear for practical reasons: (2,4) for the cheaper ground-state sampling, and (2,2) containing only n(O) and pi*(CO) for SI-SA-REKS, which has no other space implemented. All CASPT2 calculations used a 0.5 a.u. level shift, tested to be insensitive across a wide range. Only S0 and S1 were treated, equally weighted in the SA-CASSCF state-averaging
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1, equally weighted)
Other: The paper's central result is that the electronic structure method matters far more than the nonadiabatic algorithm. Excited-state lifetimes across the ab initio family span nearly a factor of two: XMS-CASPT2 39 fs, MS-CASPT2 54 fs, FOMO-CASCI 58 fs, SA-CASSCF 68 fs - a spread the authors call surprising given that the underlying potential energy surfaces differ negligibly. Semiempirical MR-CISD/OM3 is fastest at 36 fs (within XMS-CASPT2 error bars); SI-SA-REKS is an outlier at 90 fs whose population transfer stops abruptly at 140 fs. CO release quantum yields: all ab initio methods agree within error bars and sit close to the experimental 0.73 (intensity-weighted average); MR-CISD/OM3 overestimates at 0.89; SI-SA-REKS fails outright at 0.20 (the authors could not reproduce the 0.44 +/- 0.11 previously published for that method). All ab initio methods find the polymerization channel at least once while the DFT and semiempirical ones never do. By contrast the coupled electron-nuclear algorithms give identical quantum yields within statistical error and consistent population transfer, with FSSH and LZSH essentially equivalent - so when conical intersections are well defined the cheaper LZSH is sufficient.
reference_short: Janos and Slavicek, What Controls the Quality of Photodynamical Simulations? Electronic Structure Versus Nonadiabatic Algorithm, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2023)
notes: Metal-free organic (metal_center = none).
